data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Durbin wrote a bill making data centers disclose their electricity and water use, tied rising Illinois utility bills to energy-hungry data centers, and cosponsored the Power for the People Act so data centers pay their own grid costs. He has not called for a pause on building.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.4213 Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would force data centers to report energy and water use to states, project five years of demand, and face fines for not complying.

evidence.title: Press release: As utility costs rise, Durbin introduces data center transparency bill
evidence.what_it_shows: Durbin said a sharp rise in utility bills may come from the growth of energy-hungry data centers and that Illinoisans deserve an honest analysis of data centers' electricity and water needs; the release notes he also wrote about rising water and electric bills in the Chicago Tribune.

evidence.title: News report: Durbin listed as cosponsor of Van Hollen's Power for the People Act
evidence.quote: Joining Van Hollen as cosponsors on the legislation are Democratic Senators Dick Durbin, Richard Blumenthal, Cory Booker, Tammy Duckworth, Tina Smith, and Angela Alsobrooks.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed a bill creating data center load queues, new rate classes and FERC rules so data centers, not households, pay for grid upgrades.

evidence.title: Press release: Van Hollen leads new bill to ensure Americans aren't footing the bill for big data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: The sponsor's release lists Durbin as an original cosponsor of the ratepayer-protection bill, which the Illinois Citizens Utility Board endorsed.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Durbin wants binding rules now: his AI LEAD Act would let anyone harmed by an AI system sue the company under product liability law, and he cosponsors the GUARD Act to keep kids away from AI companion bots. His focus is harm to kids and consumers from AI products, not existential risk.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.2937 AI LEAD Act (federal product liability for AI systems)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill classifies AI systems as products so the Attorney General, state attorneys general and private people can sue developers and deployers for harms.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley, Durbin introduce legislation empowering Americans to bring liability claims against AI companies
evidence.quote: By opening the courtroom and allowing victims to sue, our bill will force AI companies to develop their products with safety in mind. Our message to AI companies is clear: keep innovating, but do it responsibly.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words, he wants courts and liability, not self-policing, to force safer AI design.

evidence.title: Press release: Durbin exposes harms of unregulated AI chatbots during Senate Judiciary hearing
evidence.what_it_shows: Questioning parents whose children were harmed by Character.AI and ChatGPT, Durbin said the problem is money and profit and that making companies pay a price for the devastation would change their conduct; he previewed the AI LEAD Act at the hearing.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3062 GUARD Act (age checks, no AI companion bots for minors)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined Hawley's bill requiring chatbot companies to verify ages and bar minors from companion bots.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Ban on kids' companion chatbots advanced by Senate committee
evidence.what_it_shows: Roll Call names Durbin, the committee's ranking member, among the GUARD Act's cosponsors as the Judiciary Committee advanced it.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Senate passes Durbin's DEFIANCE Act on nonconsensual deepfake images
evidence.quote: This legislation says if they are guilty of such reckless misconduct, that they can be sued for it and held civilly liable for the damages.
evidence.what_it_shows: As sponsor he won unanimous passage of a civil right to sue over AI sexual deepfakes and criticized X for letting Grok create exploitive images.

evidence.title: IPWatchdog: Senate Judiciary hearing on Chinese IP theft (Durbin exchange with Helen Toner)
evidence.quote: In response to a question from Senator Dick Durbin (D-IL) about whether the government should be more involved in the development of AI technologies
evidence.what_it_shows: Durbin raised whether government should have a bigger role in AI development; the witness replied the mismatch between AI's importance and government involvement is unprecedented.

evidence.title: Press release: Durbin opening statement at Judiciary hearing on AI training on copyrighted works
evidence.what_it_shows: He said AI innovation and intellectual property protection are not mutually exclusive and criticized Meta and Anthropic for training models on pirated books without paying creators.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Durbin wants to rein in Big Tech. He cosponsors the Sunset Section 230 Act, campaigned for it with actor Joseph Gordon-Levitt, opened a Judiciary investigation into child abuse on Roblox, and backs STOP CSAM, KOSA and an ad-tech antitrust bill.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3546 Sunset Section 230 Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs ending the legal shield that protects platforms from lawsuits over user content.

evidence.title: Courthouse News: Joseph Gordon-Levitt joins Durbin to urge rollback of Section 230
evidence.quote: rolling back liability protection for tech companies would help to force “real accountability” in the industry
evidence.what_it_shows: At his own press event Durbin argued repealing Section 230 would force accountability and acknowledged the tech lobby would fight it.

evidence.title: Letter: Hawley and Durbin launch Judiciary subcommittee investigation into child sexual abuse on Roblox
evidence.what_it_shows: As subcommittee ranking member he co-signed a letter saying Roblox appears to prioritize revenue and engagement over children's safety and ordering it to preserve all child-safety records.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs letting victims sue platforms that host child sexual abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports a duty of care for platforms used by minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1060 AMERICA Act (breaking up online ad market control)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs antitrust limits on giant ad-tech companies like Google.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Durbin cosponsors the States' Right to Regulate AI Act, which would block Washington from wiping out state AI laws, and voted to strip the 10-year state AI moratorium from the 2025 budget bill. No separate statement on the December 2025 executive order was found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3557 States' Right to Regulate AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined the bill one week after the Trump executive order targeting state AI laws; it says states keep the power to pass their own AI rules.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Senate roll call 363, Blackburn amendment striking the state AI moratorium from H.R. 1 (99 to 1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to remove the moratorium, as did nearly every senator, so the vote alone is weak evidence. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Durbin signed a June 2026 letter questioning the approval of 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips for the UAE firm G42 despite warnings China could access them, which leans hawkish. He has no bill or major statement on chip export controls.

evidence.title: News report: Five Senate Democrats including Durbin demand hearings on Trump UAE deal and G42 chip approval
evidence.quote: despite warnings from U.S. intelligence officials that China could access the technology through the firm
evidence.what_it_shows: The letter he signed treats the Blackwell chip transfer to G42 as a national security concern tied to possible Chinese access.

evidence.title: IPWatchdog: Senate Judiciary hearing on Chinese IP theft
evidence.what_it_shows: He took part in a hearing on Chinese theft of US AI technology and asked about a larger government role in AI development, but did not stake out a chips position.

members.signature: Senate Judiciary ranking member behind the AI LEAD Act (letting people sue AI companies), the DEFIANCE Act on sexual deepfakes, the Sunset Section 230 Act and a data center energy and water disclosure bill; retiring in January 2027.

quote.text: By opening the courtroom and allowing victims to sue, our bill will force AI companies to develop their products with safety in mind. Our message to AI companies is clear: keep innovating, but do it responsibly.

evidence.title: Letter: Wyden and Merkley to Gov. Kotek's Data Center Advisory Committee
evidence.quote: your work to strike a balance between pursuing economic development opportunities in alignment with sustainable utility costs and environmental impacts is critical for Oregon and the Northwest
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked the state panel to address rising electricity costs for consumers, water use, farmland rezoning, tribal rights and transparency, while calling data centers critical to national security and union jobs.

evidence.title: Same letter: list of concerns the senators asked the committee to weigh
evidence.quote: Increasing electricity costs for consumers because of increased demand.
evidence.what_it_shows: Ratepayer costs were listed first among the concerns he wants the state to solve before data centers expand.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Merkley is one of the Senate's most persistent critics of government facial recognition and AI surveillance, and he wants binding rules against AI misuse in elections. His focus is targeted guardrails on specific harms, not frontier AI licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: KATU: Wyden, Merkley introduce ICE Out of Our Faces Act to bar ICE and CBP facial recognition
evidence.quote: Without oversight, this technology is dangerous in the hands of any government, and the Trump Administration is abusing it to trample on privacy, freedom of speech, and civil liberties.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a statutory ban on federal immigration agencies using face recognition and other biometric AI.

evidence.title: Democracy Docket: Merkley introduces the FAIR Elections Act on AI and voter suppression
evidence.quote: The ballot box is the beating heart of democracy, and we must use every tool at our disposal to protect it
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would prohibit AI-generated content used to intimidate election officials or spread false voting information.

evidence.title: S.4774 Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: He sponsors a bill setting binding rules against AI deepfakes and AI-driven disinformation in federal elections.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Senators want TSA to scale back facial recognition at airports (Traveler Privacy Protection Act)
evidence.quote: Folks don’t want a national surveillance state, but that’s exactly what the TSA’s unchecked expansion of facial recognition technology is leading us to
evidence.what_it_shows: He leads the bipartisan bill to make TSA face scans opt-in and has pushed a watchdog audit of the program.

evidence.title: S.1691 Traveler Privacy Protection Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill requires airport security to get consent before scanning travelers' faces.

evidence.title: S.2164 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs mandatory bias and harm testing of automated decision systems by large companies.

evidence.title: S.3308 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports banning discriminatory uses of AI and requiring bias testing.

evidence.title: S.1394 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a legal guarantee that only humans, never AI, can order a nuclear launch.

evidence.title: S.681 Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He has long backed pausing federal use of face recognition until Congress writes rules.

evidence.title: Press release (Quiver copy): Wyden and Merkley request transparency from Meta on facial recognition in smart glasses
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed Meta on plans to add face recognition to consumer glasses, warning it could normalize mass surveillance; answers were due April 6, 2026.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Merkley backs specific rules on Big Tech: kids' online safety and privacy laws, takedowns of voting lies, liability for fake goods on marketplaces, and limits on health data collection. He has not called for break-ups or repeal of Section 230.

evidence.title: S.836 Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports requiring consent before companies collect data on kids and teens and banning targeted ads to them.

evidence.title: S.1409 Kids Online Safety Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He cosponsored the main bill imposing a duty of care on platforms toward minors.

evidence.title: S.840 Digital Integrity in Democracy Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants large platforms required to quickly remove false information about how to vote.

evidence.title: S.2934 SHOP SAFE Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He would make online marketplaces liable for counterfeit goods unless they vet sellers.

evidence.title: S.1656 My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports limits on collecting and selling reproductive health data.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found. I searched for Merkley statements on the 10-year state AI law moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order, the March 2026 White House framework and the States' Right to Regulate AI Act, and found none; he did not cosponsor S.3557. His Yea on the 99-1 strike vote matched nearly the whole Senate and is not evidence on its own.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted with 98 other senators to remove the moratorium after the deal collapsed; the vote alone does not show a settled view on preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Merkley signed a November 2025 letter urging the Trump administration to restore export controls on advanced AI chips that were suspended in trade talks with China. That is his only located action on chip export policy.

evidence.title: Press release: Wyden, Schumer, Warren, Cortez Masto press Trump to restore export controls after trade talks (Merkley a signer)
evidence.quote: Trump struck a deal that suspended the ability of the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) to enforce export controls on key technologies, including American-made advanced AI chips.
evidence.what_it_shows: The release names Merkley as a signer of the letter demanding the administration reverse the suspension of chip export controls; the quoted line is the release's description, not Merkley's own words.

members.signature: Longtime critic of facial recognition and government surveillance who now pushes bans on TSA and ICE face scanning, an AI-in-elections bill, and data center guardrails with Wyden.

quote.text: For years, I’ve been ringing the alarm bells about the dangers of a national surveillance state built on facial recognition technology.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Reed led a letter from six New England senators asking the regional grid operator how it will keep AI data centers from raising household electric bills, saying the AI industry should pay those costs. He also wants the AI buildout to happen in America rather than the Middle East, so he is not against building data centers.

evidence.title: Letter: Reed and Whitehouse lead six New England senators asking ISO New England how it will protect ratepayers from data center costs
evidence.quote: As the ones who stand to benefit most, the multi-billion-dollar AI industry should be responsible for these costs.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants tech companies, not families, to pay for the grid costs data centers create.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Reed, Coons, Shaheen, Warner, Kelly, Himes and Krishnamoorthi on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: Under this deal, data centers and AI systems that would otherwise be built in America will be built in the Middle East
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats data centers as valuable infrastructure that should be built in the U.S., which tempers his ratepayer concerns.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Reed has said since 2023 that AI needs federal regulation done quickly but carefully. His main work is on military AI: he co-wrote a bill requiring human oversight and a manual override for AI weapons and barring AI from nuclear launch decisions, much of which the Senate Armed Services Committee folded into its 2027 defense bill. He also backed an office to check the most powerful AI models for serious dangers.

evidence.title: S.4707 Responsible Artificial Intelligence Defense Act of 2026 (cosponsor with Sen. Coons)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill sets rules so the Pentagon keeps humans in the loop on AI weapons and bars AI from deciding to launch a nuclear weapon.

evidence.title: Axios: Coons and Reed to introduce the Responsible Artificial Intelligence in Defense Act
evidence.quote: A rigorous framework for human oversight is not a brake on adoption; it is the foundation that makes sustainable, confident adoption possible.
evidence.what_it_shows: The sponsors' memo frames binding human oversight rules as the way to adopt military AI safely, written after the Pentagon's fight with Anthropic.

evidence.title: Arms Control Association: Senate Armed Services Committee adopts AI and autonomous weapons framework based on the Coons-Reed bill in the FY2027 NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: As ranking member he got most of his human-judgment and testing rules for military AI, including a ban on AI nuclear launch decisions, into the committee's defense bill.

evidence.title: Press release: Reed attends first Senate AI Insight Forum
evidence.quote: There was unanimous consensus that there should be federal regulation of AI and it should be done rapidly, but very carefully.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he supports federal AI regulation and says there are dangers as well as benefits to sort out.

evidence.title: S.5616 Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed creating a government office to evaluate the most powerful AI models for serious dangers before release.

evidence.title: Letter: Reed, Brown, Menendez and Smith urge CFPB to act on AI voice-cloning scams
evidence.quote: The FTC and CFPB need to take action to help thwart this type of fraud
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants regulators to use existing powers against AI-enabled scams.

evidence.title: The Hill: Reed questions Pentagon CIO on labeling Anthropic a supply chain risk while still using Claude in the Iran war
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed the Pentagon on why it punished an AI company that resisted broad military uses of its model, calling it odd that the department kept using the product.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Reed supports targeted online rules, chiefly the Kids Online Safety Act, the STOP CSAM Act, and letting news outlets bargain with Google and Facebook. He has not called for breaking up tech companies or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms to protect minors.

evidence.title: Press release: Reed helps build momentum for bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.quote: Ensuring a safe environment online should be the default, especially for children.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he wants tech and social media companies held accountable for harm to kids.

evidence.title: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making platforms report and remove child sexual abuse material and letting victims sue.

evidence.title: S.1094 Journalism Competition and Preservation Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed letting news outlets team up to make Google and Facebook pay for their stories.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: Reed voted with 98 other senators to strip the state AI law moratorium from the 2025 budget bill, but no statement, letter or bill was found on preempting state AI laws, the December 2025 executive order, or the March 2026 White House framework as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R.1 (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the near-unanimous vote to remove the moratorium, but almost every senator did, so the vote alone does not show a position. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Reed is a consistent hawk on AI chip exports. He signed every major Senate Democratic letter against the Trump administration's H20 and H200 sales to China and its Gulf chip deals, and in his own words called the H200 decision a flawed, transactional move that could gift China's military key technology.

evidence.title: Press release: Reed and colleagues warn Trump's U-turn on AI chip sales to China is a colossal economic and national security failure
evidence.quote: This flawed, transactional decision without a broader AI export control strategy could gift China's military key technology gains and seems completely divorced from any consideration of America's economic and national security interests
evidence.what_it_shows: His own words opposing the December 2025 decision to let Nvidia sell H200 chips to China.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Reed, Coons, Shaheen, Warner, Kelly, Himes and Krishnamoorthi on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: AI chips must only be exported to trusted companies, in reasonable numbers, and in concert with credible security standards and assurances.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed exporting large volumes of advanced chips to the Gulf without security assurances against diversion to China.

evidence.title: Letter: Coons, Warner, Schumer, Reed and Warren to Commerce Secretary Lutnick on resuming Nvidia H20 sales to China
evidence.quote: We shouldn't be trading away key technological advantages as if they are concessions in a trade negotiation
evidence.what_it_shows: He objected to loosening chip export controls as part of trade talks with China.

evidence.title: Letter: Warner, Schumer, Reed, Shaheen, Coons and Warren to President Trump on the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China
evidence.quote: We again urge your administration to quickly reverse course and abandon this reckless plan to trade away U.S. technology leadership.
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked Trump to reverse the deal letting Nvidia and AMD sell AI chips to China for a cut of revenue.

evidence.title: Letter: Schumer and Warren lead Senate Democrats including Reed urging Lutnick and Rubio to reconsider the Saudi and UAE chip deals
evidence.quote: These deals greenlight the sale of sensitive U.S. technology in exchange for illusory promises of foreign investment.
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed on to the argument that the Gulf deals risk sensitive chips reaching China.

evidence.title: Brown, Reed, Menendez and Warner letter to President Biden urging a significant BIS funding increase in the FY2025 budget
evidence.what_it_shows: Senate Banking Chairman Brown and three senior Democrats asked the White House to seek a large increase for BIS export-control administration and enforcement.

members.signature: Top Democrat on Armed Services; co-author of the Responsible AI in Defense Act and a steady critic of selling advanced Nvidia chips to China.

quote.text: There was unanimous consensus that there should be federal regulation of AI and it should be done rapidly, but very carefully.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Risch treats AI-driven electricity demand as real and answers it with more nuclear power, including his 2026 ARC Act to help finance new reactors. No statements found on data center siting, ratepayer costs, or the Meta Kuna project as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: Risch touts significance of nuclear energy to growing energy demand (Senate Energy hearing remarks)
evidence.what_it_shows: At a July 2025 Senate Energy hearing he said he had been a doubter about forecasts of AI-driven electricity demand but now expects the country to be inundated with demand, and that nuclear power is how to meet it.

evidence.title: KMVT: Idaho leaders push for nuclear energy expansion with new task force, federal bill
evidence.quote: this huge demand we’re going to have for power in just a very few years because of AI and these other things coming online, they realize that it is going to take nuclear power
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties AI and data center power demand directly to his bipartisan Accelerating Reliable Capacity (ARC) Act, which would put $3.6 billion behind finishing new commercial reactors.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: His only AI-specific action is co-leading the TEST AI Act, which has the national labs and NIST build test beds to check whether AI systems are safe and trustworthy. It funds testing rather than rules, so it does not show a clear lean toward or against regulation.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1633 TEST AI Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-led a bipartisan bill directing the Energy Department and NIST to build test beds for measuring whether AI systems are safe and reliable.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3162 TEST AI Act of 2024 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the earlier version of the same AI testing bill, showing a sustained interest in federal AI evaluation capacity.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Bipartisan Senate bill looks to improve AI testing
evidence.what_it_shows: Names Risch as one of five senators introducing the TEST AI Act; the article carries a quote from Sen. Lujan on AI vulnerabilities and risks but no Risch quote.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Backs targeted rules for online platforms: he cosponsors the Kids Online Safety Act and the STOP CSAM Act and has long pushed against TikTok's Chinese ownership. No support found for Big Tech break-ups or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring social media and gaming platforms to build in safety tools for minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making platforms do more to report and remove child sexual abuse material and letting victims sue.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1409 Kids Online Safety Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed KOSA in the prior Congress too, a consistent kids' safety position.

evidence.title: KTVB: Idaho delegates vote on TikTok ban bill (Risch office statement)
evidence.quote: Senator Risch has long voiced concerns about TikTok given the CCP's ability to control the app.
evidence.what_it_shows: His communications director said he leaned toward the TikTok divest-or-ban bill and had written the FTC in 2023 about the app's influence on children.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: Voted with 98 other senators to strip the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from the 2025 budget bill, but that near-unanimous vote came after the deal collapsed and is not a stated position. No statements, letters, or bills on preemption found as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Senate roll call 363, Blackburn amendment striking the state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the 99-1 vote to remove the moratorium; because nearly every senator voted the same way, this alone does not show where he stands on preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: He signed a July 2026 letter pressing Apple not to buy memory chips from Chinese military-linked companies and has long attacked China's theft of Micron's technology. No statement found on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales to China or on the Chip Security Act.

evidence.title: MacRumors: Senators demand Apple commit to not buying Chinese memory chips (Risch a signer)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined Sen. Schumer's bipartisan letter asking Apple to commit not to use memory chips from China's CXMT or YMTC, a hawkish, Micron-friendly stance on Chinese chipmakers.

evidence.title: Press release: In hearing on worldwide threats, Risch points to Micron as example of technology, IP theft by China
evidence.what_it_shows: At a Senate Intelligence hearing he called China the real concern and used Chinese theft of Micron's memory chip technology as his prime example of why China must live by rule of law.

evidence.title: Press release: Crapo, Risch, Simpson, Fulcher support inclusion of chips permitting reform in defense bill
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a 115-lawmaker letter to keep NEPA permitting relief for U.S. semiconductor plants in the FY24 defense bill; this is about building chips at home, not export controls.

members.signature: Frames AI's electricity appetite as the case for an Idaho-led nuclear build-out; co-leads the TEST AI Act on federal AI safety testing.

quote.text: this huge demand we’re going to have for power in just a very few years because of AI and these other things coming online, they realize that it is going to take nuclear power

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Shaheen signed a January 2026 letter with five other New England senators pressing the regional grid operator to make tech companies, not families, pay for data center power demand. No statement calling for a pause or moratorium was found; the widely quoted 2026 'Shaheen' moratorium remarks come from her daughter Stefany Shaheen, the NH-1 candidate, not the senator.

evidence.title: Letter: six New England senators ask ISO New England how it will protect ratepayers from data center costs
evidence.quote: We believe it is necessary to require tech companies, not American families, to foot the bill for their load.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shaheen signed on to the view that the AI industry, not households, should pay for data center load and that the grid operator must shield residential ratepayers.

evidence.title: Six New England senators' letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada on protecting ratepayers from data center growth
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators asked the New England grid operator how it will keep tech companies, not families, paying for data center load, citing a 13% rise in residential prices in 2025 and PJM's capacity price spike as a warning.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Shaheen says Congress is doing too little on AI and hopes it does better than it did on social media; she backs targeted fixes like the TAKE IT DOWN Act and a ban on algorithmic price fixing. No call for licensing, binding safety testing or a pause was found.

evidence.title: WMUR town hall: Shaheen says Congress doing very little to address rise of AI
evidence.quote: I hope that Congress can do a better job of addressing the technology around AI than we've done to address the other technology companies that have been responsible for social media
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants Congress to act on AI, and in the same answer voiced sympathy for an AI company that insisted on safeguards against surveillance uses in its Pentagon dispute.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: TAKE IT DOWN Act (S.146), now law
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a federal crime for posting AI-faked intimate images and fast takedown rules, a targeted guardrail.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 (S.232)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stopping companies from using shared pricing algorithms to fix prices.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Shaheen backs targeted rules on tech platforms, especially for kids: the Kids Online Safety Act, STOP CSAM, the ECCHO Act and a ban on Chinese-linked connected cars. She talks about holding Big Tech accountable but has not pushed break-ups or a Section 230 repeal.

evidence.title: Press release: Shaheen-backed Kids Online Safety Act passes Senate
evidence.quote: For too long, Big Tech has put profits above all else and failed to protect kids online.
evidence.what_it_shows: She frames kids' online safety as holding Big Tech accountable for addictive and harmful content.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms toward minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (S.1829)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs letting victims sue platforms that fail to remove child sexual abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (S.4429)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected cars and software from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act, 118th Congress (S.1409)
evidence.what_it_shows: Her support for kids online safety rules spans two Congresses.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: Shaheen voted with nearly the whole Senate to strip the 10-year state AI law moratorium from the 2025 budget bill, but no statement, letter or bill was found showing her view on federal preemption of state AI laws as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium (Senate roll call 363)
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined the 99-1 vote to remove the moratorium, which by itself does not show a position on preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Shaheen, the top Democrat on Foreign Relations, is one of the Senate's loudest voices against selling advanced AI chips to China: she called the H200 decision a colossal failure, signed letters against the 15 percent fee deal and the Gulf chip deals, and cosponsors the SAFE Chips and AI OVERWATCH Acts. She pairs that with a bill to help allies buy American tech.

evidence.title: Statement: Shaheen leads national security Democrats against allowing Nvidia H200 exports to China
evidence.quote: The Trump administration’s announcement that it will allow the export of advanced H200 AI chips to China is a colossal economic and national security failure.
evidence.what_it_shows: She led the Senate Democrats' condemnation of letting Nvidia sell H200 chips to China and asked the president to reverse course.

evidence.title: Letter: six Senate Democrats urge Trump to reverse the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China (CNBC)
evidence.quote: The willingness displayed in this arrangement to 'negotiate' away America's competitive edge that is key to our national security in exchange for what is, in effect, a commission on a sale of AI-enabling technology to our main global competitor, is cause for serious alarm
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed the letter calling the fee-for-licenses deal a threat to national security.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Senate and House Democrats on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: AI chips must only be exported to trusted companies, in reasonable numbers, and in concert with credible security standards and assurances.
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed large Gulf chip exports without security assurances, warning the compute could reach China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: SAFE Chips Act of 2025 (S.3374)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs locking in current chip export limits on China so the White House cannot loosen them alone.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI OVERWATCH Act (S.4456)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports giving Congress a say before advanced AI chips are approved for sale to China and other risky countries.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Shaheen and Ricketts introduce the U.S. Tech PATH Act to help allies buy American cyber and digital technology
evidence.what_it_shows: She favors exporting American technology to trusted partners to undercut China, so her hawkishness is aimed at China rather than at exports generally.

evidence.title: Top Senate Democrats' letter to President Trump on the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China
evidence.what_it_shows: Six Senate Democrats urged Trump to reverse the deal letting Nvidia and AMD sell AI chips to China in exchange for a 15 percent cut, arguing it harms national security and that export law bars fees tied to licenses; they demanded answers by Aug. 22.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' statement introducing the SAFE Chips Act to lock in AI chip export limits on China
evidence.what_it_shows: Six senators introduced a bill to codify current chip export limits on China for 30 months, with Ricketts, Coons, Cotton, Shaheen and Kim quoted opposing any loosening for chips like the H200.

evidence.title: Banks and Warren joint statement introducing the AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A bipartisan group introduced the Senate AI OVERWATCH Act to codify the ban on exporting the most advanced AI chips to China; Warren said selling advanced chips to China is 'bad in the short run and worse in the long run.'

members.signature: Retiring Foreign Relations ranking member who leads Senate Democrats against selling advanced AI chips to China and signed the New England senators' letter on data center power costs.

quote.text: The Trump administration’s announcement that it will allow the export of advanced H200 AI chips to China is a colossal economic and national security failure.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Warner wants data centers built and calls a moratorium "idiocy" because China would move faster, but he also wants them to pay their own grid costs, disclose energy and water use, run on clean power, keep setbacks from homes, and meet efficiency standards to keep federal tax breaks. His position is a deliberate middle: build, but with real strings attached.

evidence.title: National Desk: Warner calls proposed data center moratorium "idiocy" at Axios AI summit
evidence.quote: That would be idiocy. A data center moratorium simply means China's gonna move quicker. This is one where we can't lose.
evidence.what_it_shows: He rejects the Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez moratorium and frames data centers as a race with China the US must win.

evidence.title: Cardinal News: Warner co-sponsors the Power for the People Act (data centers pay their own grid costs)
evidence.quote: If corporations are going to run data centers in Virginia, they should cover the cost of them. I'm proud to support the Power for the People Act to ensure that huge corporations are not pawning off costs to working Americans.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a bill directing states to make data centers, not households, pay for the power and grid upgrades they need.

evidence.title: S.5054, Data Center Tax Accountability and Disclosure Act of 2026 (Warner is sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would make large AI data centers publicly report energy, water, emissions and backup generation and tie federal bonus depreciation to efficiency standards.

evidence.title: Alexandria Brief: Warner unveils AI package, calls for federal minimum standards on data centers
evidence.quote: Communities should not be asked to shoulder the costs of the AI revolution without knowing what they're signing up for
evidence.what_it_shows: His floor speech and media call pushed disclosure of local incentive deals, no added cost to household electric bills, clean backup power, water standards and setbacks from neighborhoods.

evidence.title: ARLnow: Warner data center bill ties bonus depreciation to LEED Gold or Platinum certification
evidence.quote: America doesn’t have to choose between leading in AI and putting commonsense rules of the road in place. In fact, our leadership depends on getting this right.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames the data center and AI rules as compatible with US leadership rather than a brake on it; the bill was endorsed by the Chesapeake Bay Foundation, Sierra Club and Virginia LCV.

evidence.title: Potomac Local (via Fredericksburg Free Press): Warner seeks guardrails on data center power costs
evidence.quote: We're not going to stop artificial intelligence. We have to put guardrails on it. But I also think we need guardrails on data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: He pairs acceptance of AI growth with a call for limits on data centers' cost impacts.

evidence.title: CEPA commentary: Warner deems a data center moratorium "idiocy" while sponsoring clean-energy and cost-recovery mandates
evidence.what_it_shows: Outside analysts describe him as the model of a moderate Democrat who supports continued construction paired with pollution and rate protections.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Warner wants binding rules on the most powerful AI: his Secure AI Development Act would require mandatory security testing of frontier models before release, and he says Congress cannot rely on tech CEOs' goodwill. He also backs kids-and-chatbot age checks, AI labeling, AI layoff reporting and deepfake crackdowns. He calls himself pro-AI and pro-tech, opposes a pause, and cosponsored a financial-services AI sandbox bill, so his approach is strict on frontier safety but not anti-AI.

evidence.title: S.5061, Secure A.I. Development Act of 2026 (Warner is sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: A 47-page bill to improve tracking of AI security and safety incidents and, per Warner's description, require secure testing of the most advanced models before deployment.

evidence.title: Alexandria Brief: Warner calls for mandatory safety testing of AI models before public release
evidence.quote: We cannot just leave this to the goodwill of some of these tech CEOs.
evidence.what_it_shows: He compared pre-release AI testing to drug and car safety standards and cited an OpenAI model that broke out of its test environment as the reason binding rules are needed.

evidence.title: S.3062, GUARD Act (age checks and no AI companion bots for kids)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports binding rules on AI chatbot companies to keep children away from companion bots.

evidence.title: S.4915, AI Labeling Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports mandatory labels on AI-generated pictures, video and text.

evidence.title: S.3108, AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act (with Sen. Hawley)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require companies to report AI-caused layoffs to the Labor Department.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Warner and Hawley lead bipartisan letter demanding federal data on AI's labor market impact
evidence.quote: At a time when the U.S. workforce is approaching an inflection point due to the acceleration of artificial intelligence, adaptable and responsive federal statistical agencies are necessary
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI job disruption as imminent and wants government surveys changed to track it.

evidence.title: Fortune: Warner warns new-grad unemployment could hit 30 to 35 percent within two years
evidence.quote: I will bet anybody in the audience that goes to 30 or 35% within the next two years
evidence.what_it_shows: At the Hill and Valley Forum he described AI as "the battle of our time" while calling himself a pro-AI, pro-tech guy, showing alarm about disruption without opposing the technology.

evidence.title: Fortune: Gillibrand letter signed by Warner blasts the administration's "unfocused, ad hoc" approach to frontier AI oversight
evidence.quote: The Trump administration's unfocused, ad hoc approach to AI risks America's economic security and competitiveness
evidence.what_it_shows: He and four other Democratic senators demanded clear, consistent federal rules for frontier models instead of case-by-case White House directives.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Warner urges 17 AI and social media companies to crack down on election deepfakes before the midterms
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Google and others to add content credentials, watermarks and detection sharing ahead of the 2026 elections.

evidence.title: S.2528, Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act (regulatory sandbox)
evidence.what_it_shows: Contradictory signal: he joined a bill letting financial firms test AI tools with fewer rules, showing he is not uniformly pro-regulation.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Warner is one of the Senate's most persistent Big Tech critics. He cosponsors tougher antitrust law, the Kids Online Safety Act and a social media ban for children under 13, and his 2026 AI AGENT Act would force dominant platforms to let independent AI agents interoperate so the big companies do not lock in the next market. He says Congress failed on social media and should not repeat that mistake.

evidence.title: S.130, Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a major antitrust overhaul that would make it harder for giant companies, including Big Tech, to merge.

evidence.title: S.1748, Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms toward minors.

evidence.title: S.278, Kids Off Social Media Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban children under 13 from social media and limit algorithmic targeting of teens.

evidence.title: S.5051, AI AGENT Act of 2026 (Artificial Intelligence Access, Gatekeeper Exchange, and Nondiscriminatory Transfer Act)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would impose duties on consumer AI agents and require large gatekeeper platforms to allow competing agents access.

evidence.title: Alexandria Brief: Warner on why AI agents must be able to reach every model
evidence.quote: If we don't make sure that AI agents can access all the models, we could end up again where the big tech companies dominate
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI agent rules as a way to stop Big Tech from repeating its dominance of social media.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press analysis: Warner's AI AGENT Act is the first draft federal law on agentic AI power and follows the EU Digital Markets Act interoperability model
evidence.what_it_shows: Legal scholars read the bill as a structural, pro-competition intervention against dominant platforms, in line with Warner's earlier ACCESS Act on data portability.

evidence.title: S.686, RESTRICT Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He authored the bill giving the government power to review and block apps and tech from rival countries, the framework behind the TikTok debate.

evidence.title: S.1207, EARN IT Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported stripping platforms' Section 230 shield when they allow child abuse material to spread.

preemption.label: Mixed or conditional
preemption.summary: Warner has signaled he could accept a single federal AI standard if it comes with real guardrails, and he criticized the March 2026 White House framework, which included preemption of state laws, as lacking substance. No clear statement for or against overriding state AI laws was found, and his Yea vote to strip the 2025 moratorium was cast by 99 senators.

evidence.title: Politico Pro headline: "Warner open to federal AI standard with guardrails" (subscriber article, text not readable)
evidence.what_it_shows: A week after the White House framework, Politico reported Warner would consider one national AI standard so long as it carried meaningful protections; only the headline could be confirmed.

evidence.title: Fortune: Warner blasted the White House AI framework as lacking substance
evidence.quote: lacks significant substance
evidence.what_it_shows: He did not endorse the administration's preemption-centered framework and faulted it for thin consumer protections.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Warner voted Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted with 98 colleagues to remove the moratorium; because the vote was 99 to 1 after the deal collapsed, it does not by itself show opposition to preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Warner wants tighter control over advanced AI chips. He joined statements opposing Trump's Gulf chip deals without security assurances, cosponsored the Stop Stealing our Chips Act that passed the Senate in May 2026, and backs a longer statute of limitations for export-control violations. Even his data center argument is framed as denying China an edge.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Coons, Shaheen, Reed, Warner, Kelly, Himes and Krishnamoorthi on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: President Trump announced deals to export very large volumes of advanced AI chips to the UAE and Saudi Arabia without credible security assurances to prevent U.S. adversaries from accessing those chips.
evidence.what_it_shows: He warned the deals could leak compute to China through G42 and offshore the US AI buildout, while applauding limits on Nvidia exports to China.

evidence.title: S.1473, Stop Stealing our Chips Act (Rounds bill, Warner sole cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Creates a whistleblower reward program to catch illegal chip smuggling; the bill passed the Senate unanimously on May 20, 2026 per GovTrack.

evidence.title: GovTrack: S.1473 passed the Senate on May 20, 2026 and goes to the House next
evidence.what_it_shows: Confirms the Warner-backed anti-smuggling bill cleared the Senate.

evidence.title: S.5380, ten-year statute of limitations for export control violations
evidence.what_it_shows: Would give enforcers twice as long to punish illegal shipments of sensitive technology.

evidence.title: S.5382, China AI Power Report Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Requests a government report on how fast China's AI capability is growing.

evidence.title: National Desk: Warner says a data center moratorium would let China move quicker
evidence.quote: A data center moratorium simply means China's gonna move quicker
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI competition framing centers on keeping the US ahead of China.

evidence.title: Schumer and Warren-led Senate Democrats' letter to Lutnick and Rubio urging reconsideration of Middle East chip deals
evidence.what_it_shows: Eight Senate Democrats urged the administration to reconsider the Saudi and UAE AI chip deals absent enforceable protections against diversion to China, and raised Trump-family financial conflicts.

evidence.title: Top Senate Democrats' letter to Lutnick on decision to resume H20 (and AMD MI308) sales to China
evidence.what_it_shows: Five senior Senate Democrats expressed 'grave concern' at reversing the April 2025 H20 ban, said restricting leading-edge chips is the defining barrier to Chinese AI parity, and objected to trading export controls in trade talks without consulting Congress.

evidence.title: Top Senate Democrats' letter to President Trump on the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China
evidence.what_it_shows: Six Senate Democrats urged Trump to reverse the deal letting Nvidia and AMD sell AI chips to China in exchange for a 15 percent cut, arguing it harms national security and that export law bars fees tied to licenses; they demanded answers by Aug. 22.

evidence.title: Brown, Reed, Menendez and Warner letter to President Biden urging a significant BIS funding increase in the FY2025 budget
evidence.what_it_shows: Senate Banking Chairman Brown and three senior Democrats asked the White House to seek a large increase for BIS export-control administration and enforcement.

members.signature: Senate Intelligence vice chair with a sweeping July 2026 AI agenda (mandatory testing of frontier models, data center disclosure, AI agent rules, worker transition fund), a hard line on chip exports to China, and a blunt rejection of a data center moratorium as "idiocy."

quote.text: We cannot just leave this to the goodwill of some of these tech CEOs.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Gillibrand applauded Gov. Hochul's one-year pause on large data centers and says communities should be able to say no. She wants ironclad guarantees on power bills, water and air before projects move forward, and says data centers should bring their own power and use closed-loop cooling, but she also calls them a development opportunity and declined to oppose the Stream project.

evidence.title: Statement applauding Hochul's data center moratorium (WRGB/CBS6 Albany)
evidence.quote: Before we move forward, our communities need ironclad guarantees that their energy bills won't spike, their water will be protected, and their air will remain clean.
evidence.what_it_shows: She endorsed the state's one-year pause and set conditions on bills, water and air for any new project.

evidence.title: Statement applauding Hochul's data center moratorium (WRGB/CBS6 Albany), trust language
evidence.quote: This one-year moratorium is fundamentally about trust. Right now, New Yorkers aren't convinced these massive facilities benefit them.
evidence.what_it_shows: She framed the pause as temporary and about winning public trust rather than blocking data centers for good.

evidence.title: Press remarks on the Stream/STAMP data center (Batavia Daily News)
evidence.quote: It's up to the community to decide, and if the community does not want a data center, they should not have to have a data center in their community
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs local veto power, said new data centers should find their own energy rather than lean on ratepayers and use closed-loop cooling, called them a possible development opportunity, and declined to take a stand on the $19.5B Stream project.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Gillibrand wants binding rules for military AI, including a ban on AI in nuclear launch decisions, and has repeatedly attacked the Pentagon for punishing Anthropic over safety guardrails. She calls for clear federal rules of the road and protections for kids, seniors and workers, while also pressing the administration for predictable policy that does not push customers to Chinese models.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.4656, Secure and Accountable Military AI Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: She introduced binding limits on how the Pentagon may deploy AI, keeping humans in charge of life-and-death decisions.

evidence.title: Press release: Gillibrand introduces bill to regulate the Pentagon's use of AI
evidence.quote: Right now, the Pentagon is moving toward deploying incredibly powerful AI technology without commonsense guardrails in place, which could have catastrophic consequences that make all of us less safe.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words treat unguarded military AI as a potentially catastrophic danger requiring rules now.

evidence.title: Press release: Gillibrand statement on Secretary Hegseth's rejection of AI guardrails
evidence.quote: Removing guardrails doesn't produce efficiency; it guarantees a future of catastrophic harm.
evidence.what_it_shows: She sided with Anthropic's request for safety guardrails and called for AI safety procedures across military and civilian life with humans in control.

evidence.title: Fortune: Pentagon designates Anthropic a supply chain risk; Gillibrand reaction
evidence.quote: This reckless action is shortsighted, self-destructive, and a gift to our adversaries.
evidence.what_it_shows: She called the Pentagon's blacklisting of a safety-focused AI company a dangerous misuse of a tool meant for adversary technology.

evidence.title: Press release: Gillibrand and colleagues press AI companies on their engagements with DoD
evidence.quote: the Trump administration's reckless push to strip away safeguards and punish companies that insist on basic guardrails puts Americans' privacy and our national security at risk
evidence.what_it_shows: With five Democratic senators she demanded that xAI, OpenAI, Alphabet, Meta, AWS and Microsoft explain what protections govern military use of their models.

evidence.title: Fortune: Gillibrand-led letter calls administration's AI approach unfocused and ad hoc
evidence.quote: The American people and leading AI companies need clear rules, not constantly changing dictates from the White House.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants a public, durable federal framework and criticized opaque restrictions on models like Fable 5 and Mythos 5, a pro-clarity rather than pro-restriction stance.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3062, GUARD Act (age checks and no AI companion bots for kids)
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports binding rules keeping children away from AI companion chatbots.

evidence.title: LeadingAge: Senate Aging Committee hearing on AI deepfakes, chatbots and senior fraud
evidence.what_it_shows: As ranking member she co-led a July 29, 2026 hearing and report on AI scams and, with Sen. Kelly, wrote nine AI companies asking how their chatbot companions protect seniors.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Gillibrand favors targeted rules on tech platforms: she signed the 2026 letter demanding platforms remove sexualized AI deepfakes, cosponsors kids' safety bills like the GUARD Act and ECCHO Act, and backed the RESTRICT Act on foreign-controlled apps.

evidence.title: TechCrunch: Eight senators demand answers from X, Meta, Alphabet, Snap, Reddit and TikTok on sexualized deepfakes
evidence.quote: In practice, however, as seen in the examples above, users are finding ways around these guardrails. Or these guardrails are failing.
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed a letter pressing the largest platforms to explain and fix their handling of nonconsensual AI sexual images, including of minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3397, ECCHO Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports a new federal crime for pressuring kids online into self-harm.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.2912, Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs banning AI-driven lies about how to vote before federal elections.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): S.686, RESTRICT Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supported giving the government power to review and block apps from rival countries.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): S.1656, My Body, My Data Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports limits on collecting and selling reproductive health data.

evidence.title: Blunt Rochester-led letter of 8 senators to Alphabet, Meta, X, TikTok, Snap and Reddit on sexualized AI-generated images
evidence.what_it_shows: Eight Democratic senators demanded the platforms explain their policies for AI 'undressing' deepfakes, including of minors, preserve related documents, and describe how they remove images and notify victims.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found on federal preemption of state AI laws as of Sept 2026. Searched for statements on the 2025 moratorium fight, the Dec 2025 executive order and the Mar 2026 White House framework, and for cosponsorship of the States' Right to Regulate AI Act; found only her Yea on the 99-1 vote, which nearly every senator cast.

evidence.title: Roll call 363 (Jul 1, 2025): Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted with 98 colleagues to remove the moratorium; because the vote was 99-1 after the deal collapsed, it is not by itself evidence of opposing preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Gillibrand signed the May 2025 Senate Democratic letter urging the administration to rethink Saudi and UAE chip deals without protections against diversion to China. She has not taken a lead role on chip export bills, and her Aug 2026 letter also warned that unpredictable US restrictions push customers toward Chinese models.

evidence.title: Senate Democrats' letter to Lutnick and Rubio on Middle East AI chip deals (Gillibrand signer)
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined eight Democrats saying the Saudi and UAE chip deals lacked enforceable protections to keep advanced chips from reaching China.

evidence.title: CyberScoop: Senators warn Trump's AI interventions could drive users to Chinese models
evidence.quote: The Administration's ad hoc and unpredictable approach undermines U.S. competitiveness, heightening market incentives to adopt open weight models from vendors based in the People's Republic of China (PRC),
evidence.what_it_shows: Her letter argues that opaque export-control style restrictions on US models help Chinese competitors, a competitiveness concern that cuts against blunt controls.

members.signature: Backs New York's one-year data center pause and local veto power, and wrote the Senate's first bill to put binding limits on Pentagon AI.

quote.text: Removing guardrails doesn't produce efficiency; it guarantees a future of catastrophic harm.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Coons wants the US to build out AI computing but says that should not mean higher power bills or lost ground on climate. His answer is efficiency technology, co-leading a bill to study liquid cooling for data centers, not limits on new projects. No statement found on the proposed Delaware City data center itself.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Coons and McCormick introduce the Liquid Cooling for AI Act
evidence.quote: Leading the world in AI innovation shouldn't have to mean skyrocketing energy bills for American families or giving up ground in the fight against climate change
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports the AI buildout and the AI race but wants federal research to cut data center energy use and costs for families.

evidence.title: S.3269 Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 (original co-lead with Sen. McCormick)
evidence.what_it_shows: Directs a federal assessment of liquid cooling so AI data centers use less power; an efficiency approach rather than a pause or ratepayer mandate.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Coons backs a long list of specific AI rules: a federal right against AI voice and face copies, whistleblower protections, age checks for AI companion bots, bans on deceptive election deepfakes, and human control over military AI. At the same time he calls AI a race with China that America must win and attacked the Pentagon for punishing Anthropic and the White House for pulling frontier models offline without clear rules. He wants durable rules, not a pause.

evidence.title: S.4591 NO FAKES Act of 2026 (sponsor; also sponsored S.1367 in 2025 and S.4875 in 2024)
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature AI bill creates a legal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice or likeness; advanced out of Senate Judiciary in June 2026.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Senate Judiciary advances Coons's NO FAKES Act by voice vote
evidence.quote: Every American should have the right to decide how their voice and likeness will be used, especially when generative AI can create highly realistic digital replicas
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words at markup, he frames deepfake protection as a personal right that needs a binding federal law.

evidence.title: S.1792 AI Whistleblower Protection Act (cosponsor with Grassley)
evidence.what_it_shows: Protects AI company employees who report safety problems to the government, a targeted safety rule.

evidence.title: S.3062 GUARD Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require AI chatbot companies to verify ages and keep minors off AI companion bots.

evidence.title: Schatz-led letter from 10 senators to Meta CEO Zuckerberg on AI chatbots and children (Coons signed)
evidence.quote: The wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a bipartisan demand that Meta explain chatbot policies that allowed romantic talk with minors and add safeguards.

evidence.title: S.4707 Responsible Artificial Intelligence Defense Act of 2026 (sponsor with Reed)
evidence.what_it_shows: Sets rules for military AI that keep humans responsible for the use of force; the Senate Armed Services Committee folded its core into the FY2027 defense bill.

evidence.title: Press release: Ranking Member Coons statement on Pentagon-Anthropic dispute
evidence.quote: The Trump administration's decision to label Anthropic a supply chain risk to national security weakens free enterprise, harms innovation, and makes Americans less safe.
evidence.what_it_shows: He defended Anthropic's refusal to let its models be used for mass surveillance or fully autonomous weapons without a human off switch, calling those commonsense limits.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons statement on Anthropic's launch of Project Glasswing
evidence.quote: Now, Congress needs to step up and do our job: creating clear rules that encourage and support innovation and growth, while ensuring AI can't be used to threaten Americans.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants Congress to write clear AI rules, pairing innovation with guardrails and keeping the technology away from China.

evidence.title: Fortune: Gillibrand, Coons, Kelly, Schiff and Warner letter on the administration's 'unfocused, ad hoc' approach to frontier AI
evidence.quote: Without consistent policy governing American models, consumers and businesses would be incentivized to migrate to models from foreign vendors, including those based in the People's Republic of China.
evidence.what_it_shows: He criticized secret, sudden federal restrictions on frontier models and asked for a public, durable framework; his concern is predictability and competitiveness as much as safety.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons and Cotton introduce resolution affirming America's AI dominance
evidence.quote: The United States' prosperity and safety rests on our ability to win the AI race
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows his innovation-and-China framing; he wants frontier AI built in America by American companies, which tempers his guardrail stance.

evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Coons favors specific fixes for big platforms rather than break-ups: he cosponsors the Kids Online Safety Act and child-abuse-material bills, sponsors a bill forcing social media companies to open their data to researchers, and joined the letter pressing Meta on chatbots and kids. No support found for repealing Section 230 or breaking up companies.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor; also cosponsored S.1409 in the 118th)

evidence.title: Press release: Coons and colleagues introduce the bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act

evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words, platforms have value but need mandated safeguards and more transparency about their effect on children.

evidence.title: S.3292 Platform Accountability and Transparency Act (sponsor with Cassidy; also S.1876 in the 118th)

evidence.title: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (cosponsor)

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Blumenthal wants data centers to pay their own way. His GRID Act with Hawley would force new large data centers to supply their own power and make existing ones cover any costs they push onto the grid, and he is investigating the secrecy deals developers sign with towns. He says data centers have an upside and does not call for a moratorium.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: GRID Act (S.3852), Hawley-Blumenthal bill to keep data center costs off consumers' electric bills
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-led the main bipartisan Senate bill making data centers, not households, pay for the power they use.

evidence.what_it_shows: He introduced his own bill aimed at stopping big new electricity users like data centers from raising family power bills.

evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words, the goal is protecting ratepayers by making data center owners absorb the costs they create.

evidence.title: News 12 Connecticut: Blumenthal backs bipartisan effort to prevent data centers from driving up electricity prices
evidence.quote: These data centers that Big Tech wants to construct will raise the prices of electricity and water and other utilities. They should be forced to pay for them and that's what my legislative proposal would do
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames data centers as a cost Big Tech should bear, not a project to block outright.

evidence.what_it_shows: He distinguishes himself from moratorium supporters like Sanders and says the country needs data centers, just not on ratepayers' backs.

evidence.what_it_shows: In March 2026 he launched an investigation into NDAs that hide data centers' energy use, water needs and community impacts, arguing communities deserve transparency; North Dakota regulators told him they lack authority to answer (Broadband Breakfast, Apr 20 2026).

evidence.what_it_shows: Senators urged FERC to reject transmission filings that spread data-center costs across regions, investigate cost allocation and PJM practices, resist queue-jumping for large fossil generators, standardize load forecasting, and prioritize residential ratepayers in the DOE-requested large-load interconnection rulemaking.

evidence.title: Six New England senators' letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada on protecting ratepayers from data center growth
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators asked the New England grid operator how it will keep tech companies, not families, paying for data center load, citing a 13% rise in residential prices in 2025 and PJM's capacity price spike as a warning.

evidence.what_it_shows: Two days after the White House's voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge, the senators called it 'vague and insufficient' and asked state utility regulators' association what guidance it gives PUCs to reject rate filings that make households subsidize data centers.

evidence.what_it_shows: Three senators opened an investigation demanding the companies explain how much of their data centers' grid and generation costs are passed to households, and pressed them to pay a greater share up front; responses were due Jan 12, 2026.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Blumenthal treats advanced AI as a serious danger and wants binding rules now. He co-wrote the AI Risk Evaluation Act, which would bar the most powerful AI systems from release until they pass federal safety evaluation, demanded answers from OpenAI after its agents went rogue, and co-leads the GUARD Act to keep kids away from AI companion chatbots.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act (S.2938)
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill would require developers of advanced AI to submit systems to a federal evaluation program before deployment, a mandatory pre-release safety gate.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley, Blumenthal introduce bipartisan AI evaluation legislation
evidence.quote: AI companies have rushed to market with products that are unsafe for the public and often lack basic due diligence and testing.
evidence.what_it_shows: His own framing: AI products are unsafe and need a federal watchdog scrutinizing models for threats to infrastructure, labor markets and civil liberties.

evidence.quote: This demonstrates the need for vigorous, mandatory independent auditing and oversight such as would be required in the Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats loss-of-control incidents as real and uses them to push mandatory audits and pre-deployment oversight.

evidence.title: NENC / WSHU: CT leaders demand answers from OpenAI over rogue AI agents
evidence.quote: It is absolutely chilling. It sounds like science fiction, but it's real, it's serious, and it is an imminent present threat to public safety, as well as civil liberties, privacy and our national security
evidence.what_it_shows: He describes autonomous AI agents evading safeguards as a present threat and said he plans more legislation to expand AI regulation.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: GUARD Act (S.3062), banning AI companions for minors and requiring age checks

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech

evidence.what_it_shows: He co-introduced a bill making data centers pay for the transmission upgrades they require and creating a data center interconnection queue.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: H.R. 8241 Power for the People Act of 2026 (verified on GovTrack cosponsor list)
evidence.what_it_shows: Formal backing for a FERC rule that data centers pay the local grid costs they cause.

evidence.quote: We're not opposed to data centers. We just want to make sure that if we're going to put a data center on a federal facility, that federal facility is not going to be degraded by the data center
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames his position as conditions on base data centers, not a ban.

evidence.title: E&E News: The Pentagon wants to build data centers. Congress would like a word.
evidence.quote: As we enter the period of AI, which requires very serious data centers, data facilities, that are extraordinary consumers of both energy and water, the question arises as to whether they should be on military bases
evidence.what_it_shows: He proposed a sweeping FY27 NDAA amendment requiring DOD to assess energy, water, noise, light and security impacts before data center deals; Armed Services Republicans rejected it.

evidence.title: Federal News Network: Congress ramps up scrutiny of Pentagon AI data center plans
evidence.what_it_shows: Reports his committee amendment on base data centers was voted down, with Republicans arguing it would hurt AI dominance over China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 9183 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a federal study of AI's electricity, water and pollution footprint with voluntary reporting.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act permitting-reform bill (House roll call 356)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted against the Republican permitting-reform bill, an indirect signal against a build-faster approach. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Garamendi cosponsored the bill to keep humans, not AI, in charge of nuclear launch decisions and signed a letter saying AI-specific risks need common-sense guardrails. He has no AI safety bills of his own and rarely speaks on the topic.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 2894 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a legal rule that a human must always decide on a nuclear launch.

evidence.quote: We strongly support innovation, and it is simply wrong to accept the premise that identifying and addressing AI-specific risks, and setting common-sense guardrails, is incompatible with U.S. leadership in AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed on to the view that AI harms like deepfakes, scams and chatbot risks justify guardrails now.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: His only relevant action found is cosponsoring the Connected Vehicle Security Act, which bans internet-connected cars and software from companies tied to China and other adversaries. No statements on Big Tech, Section 230 or kids' online safety were found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8730 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a national-security ban on connected-car technology from adversary-linked companies.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Garamendi signed the 81-member Matsui letter telling congressional leaders not to revive a moratorium on state AI laws in the NDAA or through an executive order. He did not sign the Clarke letter or cosponsor the GUARDRAILS Act, and no statement of his own was found.

evidence.title: Signer: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned executive order (signature confirmed in letter PDF)
evidence.quote: Trying to revive the same flawed policy in the NDAA, or through executive action, is an attempt to quietly jam through an idea that has already been rejected
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the House Democrats' formal opposition to preempting state AI laws.

evidence.title: Matsui-led House Democratic letter to Johnson, Thune, Jeffries and Schumer opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned executive order
evidence.what_it_shows: 81 House Democrats told congressional leaders not to revive the state AI-law moratorium in the defense bill and not to use an executive order or BEAD broadband money to override state AI laws, noting the Senate had already rejected the idea 99-1.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Grassley says he mostly hears from Iowans who dislike data centers and cites land and water worries, but treats them as something that is coming and that people adjust to. He says siting is a state or local call and nothing in Congress addresses it.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Grassley backs targeted guardrails: he wrote the AI Whistleblower Protection Act, demanded oversight after judges used AI to draft faulty orders, and wants transparency and accountability in the AI sector. evidence.title: Judiciary Committee release: Grassley on free enterprise and his whistleblower bill
evidence.quote: I believe in the free enterprise system. And of course, that causes me to support pro-business, pro-growth policies. I don't see my whistleblower protection interest in any way violating that
evidence.what_it_shows: He limits his approach to whistleblower protection rather than broad AI mandates, describing government as a referee within free enterprise.

evidence.quote: Whistleblowers are one of the best ways to ensure Congress keeps pace as the AI industry rapidly develops.
evidence.what_it_shows: His stated rationale is that whistleblowers help Congress keep up with a fast-moving industry, a transparency-first form of oversight.

evidence.what_it_shows: After his letters to two federal judges, he said oversight would continue until courts adopt firm and transparent policies on AI use.

evidence.quote: There's people developing it trying to scare us that in a few years we'll have 30% of people unemployed
evidence.what_it_shows: He is skeptical of alarming job-loss claims, says AI is still hard for him to digest, and compares the debate to buggy makers and the automobile.
