evidence.what_it_shows: He is one of nine members of the Guthrie-Joyce working group drafting a comprehensive federal privacy law, described as including provisions to keep states from adding stricter rules.

evidence.title: IAPP: US House Republicans organize a privacy working group
evidence.what_it_shows: Confirms his membership and notes he has previously spoken about the importance of privacy legislation.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Guthrie is the House's main mover on data center power costs: his committee passed the Ratepayer Protection Act 52-0 to make data centers pay for the grid upgrades they cause, and he is pushing for a floor vote. He is firmly pro-buildout, calls moratoriums harmful, says communities may opt out, and asked the FBI to probe whether China funds anti-data-center campaigns.

evidence.title: Opening statement: Guthrie leads efforts to lower energy costs, protect ratepayers (AI and the Grid legislative hearing)
evidence.quote: We are also ensuring that data centers are paying their fair share. Data centers should pay for the load that comes into the data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opened a hearing on seven data center and grid bills with the principle that data centers cover their own load costs.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Ratepayer Protection Act advances from committee 52-0
evidence.quote: The Ratepayer Protection Act will ensure that data centers pay their own way, instead of passing costs onto hardworking families.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shepherded H.R. 9340 through his committee unanimously despite data center industry objections.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Guthrie, Latta and Evans on introduction of the Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.quote: Winning the race to AI dominance is essential to securing America’s future global leadership, and that means expeditiously building the power infrastructure needed to support new technologies, while doing so in a responsible way
evidence.what_it_shows: Pairs a build-fast goal with the condition that families not foot the bill.

evidence.title: E&C ICYMI: Guthrie on Fox Business on AI policy, data center moratoriums and the Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.quote: We're about six months ahead of China and AI, people predict. If we had a year moratorium, let's say that's nationwide, and we get behind China, we'll never catch up.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposes data center moratoriums, criticized New York's, and says his bill helps states adopt the ratepayer pledge rather than imposing a one-size-fits-all federal rule.

evidence.title: E&C letter: Chairmen Guthrie, Joyce and Latta request investigation of foreign adversaries' efforts to block American data center buildout
evidence.quote: Americans deserve to know who is bankrolling the disinformation campaign that seeks to block critical infrastructure investments
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked PCAST and the FBI to investigate whether China-backed entities fund anti-data-center campaigns, treating organized opposition as possible foreign disinformation.

evidence.title: Bowling Green Daily News: Guthrie calls for investigations into AI and data center opposition, says local leaders decide
evidence.quote: The local concerns are real, and should be always taken into consideration
evidence.what_it_shows: Says communities may choose not to participate and that questions about taxes and jobs are fair, while insisting America must build or China will.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Guthrie pushes September floor vote on Ratepayer Protection Act despite industry pushback
evidence.quote: protects local communities and, I think, allows data centers to be successful
evidence.what_it_shows: Acknowledged data center industry opposition downtown but kept pressing leadership to bring the bill to the floor.

evidence.title: Politico: Guthrie says his data center bill aligns with Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge
evidence.quote: Our model is the Ratepayer Protection Pledge
evidence.what_it_shows: Positions the bill as bridging Trump's pro-data-center stance and vulnerable Republicans' constituent backlash.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Guthrie applauds White House announcement of $500 billion AI infrastructure investment
evidence.quote: This massive investment in American infrastructure makes clear that the United States is prepared to lead the world in next-generation technologies.
evidence.what_it_shows: Celebrated the Stargate data center build-out while flagging energy demand and permitting as challenges his committee would address.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Guthrie's AI doctrine is dominance, deployment and safeguards: beat China, avoid Europe-style rules, and add protections only where existing law falls short. The exception is kids and AI chatbots, where he backed the FTC inquiry, held a hearing and wrote chatbot safeguards into his KIDS Act.

evidence.title: Hatch Center essay by Guthrie: Dominance, Deployment, and Safeguards: The Path for American AI Leadership
evidence.quote: We are not in a race with Europe to regulate. We are in a race with China to innovate.
evidence.what_it_shows: Rejects EU-style AI regulation as growth-killing and puts innovation and China competition first.

evidence.title: Opening statement: full committee hearing on AI and American Global Competitiveness
evidence.quote: What I hear from people in this space, is that we have the brain power and we have the capital, what we need is the energy and the correct regulatory framework.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames AI as a war with China the US must win and says the committee's job is energy plus a light regulatory framework.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Guthrie on President Trump's AI Action Plan
evidence.quote: aligns with our Committee’s work to unleash infrastructure development and advanced manufacturing, promote a national AI framework, and safeguard Americans where existing protections fall short
evidence.what_it_shows: Endorsed the deregulatory action plan; new guardrails only where existing protections fall short.

evidence.title: E&C joint statement: Guthrie and Pallone applaud FTC inquiry into AI companion chatbots
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence has unleashed exponential levels of innovation, yet we are alarmed by recent incidents concerning the use of AI chatbots by minors.
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports targeted action on companion chatbots and children, the one area where he backs new rules.

evidence.title: E&C announcement: Oversight and Investigations hearing on the safety of AI chatbots
evidence.quote: additional oversight is needed to better understand risks to users when interacting with these technologies
evidence.what_it_shows: Convened a hearing on chatbot risks to children and teens while stressing AI's promise.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Guthrie wrote and passed the House's KIDS Act, which sets design, privacy and AI chatbot rules for platforms serving minors but drops the Senate's duty of care, and he is pushing a national privacy law that would override state laws without letting people sue. Targeted rules, not a Big Tech crackdown.

evidence.title: H.R.7757 KIDS Act (Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act), 119th
evidence.what_it_shows: His omnibus kids' online safety bill passed the House 267-117 on June 29, 2026 with chatbot disclosure, age verification and privacy rules but no duty of care.

evidence.title: Guthrie floor remarks on the KIDS Act
evidence.quote: The bill requires platforms to protect kids by default, including limiting addictive and dangerous design features and risky messaging functions.
evidence.what_it_shows: Describes binding design and default rules on platforms plus AI chatbot safeguards, framed as holding Big Tech accountable.

evidence.title: TechPolicy.Press: House GOP moves ahead with kids online safety package as Democrats balk (Guthrie markup remarks)
evidence.quote: the absence of a bipartisan consensus cannot be an excuse for inaction
evidence.what_it_shows: Pushed the package through committee 28-24 on party lines when talks broke down, then cut a bipartisan deal with Pallone in June.

evidence.title: Politico: House Republicans roll out landmark data privacy push (SECURE Data Act), Guthrie joint statement
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a national privacy standard from his working group that would preempt dozens of state privacy laws and bars private lawsuits; Pallone called it a bill written at the behest of Big Tech.

evidence.title: Opening statement: full committee hearing on AI and American Global Competitiveness (privacy remarks)
evidence.quote: We can’t do it in a heavy-handed way that stifles innovation
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants privacy and kids' protections but warns against heavy-handed regulation, pointing to Europe as the cautionary example.

evidence.title: Guthrie and Pallone joint statement supporting FTC inquiry into AI companion chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: The House Energy and Commerce chairman and ranking member jointly said they were 'alarmed' by incidents involving minors and chatbots, backed the FTC probe, and pledged bipartisan legislation to protect children online.

evidence.title: Speaker Johnson, Leader Scalise and Chairman Guthrie statements on House passage of the KIDS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: House Republican leaders hailed the 267-117 passage of the KIDS Act as protecting children while 'protecting free speech,' and Guthrie and Pallone jointly said it 'creates strong protections with new rules for design features, default settings, and kids' privacy.'

preemption.label: One national rule
preemption.summary: Guthrie is a leading House voice for one national AI rulebook. He signed the March 2026 leadership pledge to enact the White House framework preempting state AI laws, calls a patchwork of state laws a gift to adversaries, and said state preemption should come in the end even after his KIDS Act dropped it. His privacy bill would also override state privacy laws.

evidence.title: Joint statement: Johnson, Scalise, Guthrie, Jordan, Babin: House will work to implement National AI Framework
evidence.quote: House Republicans look forward to working across the aisle to enact a national framework that unleashes the full potential of AI, cements the U.S. as the global leader, and provides important protections for American families.
evidence.what_it_shows: Committed as E&C chairman to legislate the White House framework, which calls for broad preemption of state AI laws.

evidence.title: Hatch Center essay by Guthrie: Dominance, Deployment, and Safeguards
evidence.quote: A patchwork of state laws here at home would have the same effect, stalling AI development and deployment and providing our adversaries with opportunity to advance
evidence.what_it_shows: Equates state AI laws with Europe's growth-killing rules and argues for one national standard.

evidence.title: Record of Record: Guthrie signals state preemption remains the end goal after House kids' package
evidence.quote: We’re still gonna work it, and hopefully we’re gonna have to have state preemption in the end.
evidence.what_it_shows: Even after his bipartisan KIDS Act omitted AI preemption to win Democratic votes, he said preemption should be the final outcome.

evidence.title: Politico: House kids' safety deal complicates AI talks (KIDS Act omits AI preemption)
evidence.what_it_shows: His June 2026 deal with Pallone left out AI preemption and let states go further on kids' safety, a pragmatic exception to his preemption push.

evidence.title: E&C ICYMI: Guthrie on Fox Business on helping states adopt the Ratepayer Protection Pledge
evidence.quote: So we're not sending a federal statute out, we're assisting states to do so.
evidence.what_it_shows: On data center power costs he chose to help states rather than preempt them, so his preemption drive is about AI and privacy rules, not energy siting.

evidence.title: Breitbart: Leading the Future super PAC endorses second slate of House Republicans including Guthrie
evidence.what_it_shows: The AI industry super PAC that campaigns for federal preemption of state AI laws endorsed him for reelection.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No statements found on chip export controls or Nvidia H20/H200 sales to China, despite constant China-race framing. His China focus is on data centers, energy, supply chains and alleged foreign-funded opposition, not semiconductor export rules.

members.signature: House Energy and Commerce chairman driving the Ratepayer Protection Act (data centers pay their own way), the KIDS Act with AI chatbot safeguards, a preemptive national privacy bill and a national AI framework to override state laws; frames all of it as beating China.

quote.text: We are not in a race with Europe to regulate. We are in a race with China to innovate.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Harris, the only Republican in Maryland's delegation, says large users like data centers should build or secure their own electricity instead of shifting costs to ratepayers, and he joined the bipartisan press event on the issue. But he did not cosponsor the Power for the People Act, voted for the SPEED Act permitting reform, and blames state green-energy mandates rather than data centers for high bills. Mixed.

evidence.title: Press release: Maryland delegation meeting on energy affordability (Mfume office mirror of the joint release)
evidence.quote: Large energy users like data centers should be responsible for building or securing the electricity they need instead of shifting those costs onto Maryland ratepayers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Endorsed the make-data-centers-pay principle while also demanding a moratorium on state energy taxes and fees.

evidence.title: Press conference (Capital News Service): Harris joins Democrats on data center energy costs
evidence.quote: There is bipartisan agreement. The president during the State of the Union talked about the fact that these companies, that are literally trillion-dollar companies, have to stop putting the cost of their energy on the backs of our ratepayers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Said there is bipartisan agreement on stopping cost shifts, citing Trump's State of the Union, but he has not cosponsored the Power for the People Act.

evidence.title: House roll call 356: passage of H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act permitting reform bill
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted Yea on a bill to speed federal environmental reviews for energy and infrastructure projects, including those serving data centers; Maryland's Democrats voted Nay. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Press release: Harris urges DOE to keep Brandon Shores and Wagner plants running for grid reliability
evidence.quote: As electricity demand rises, the Brandon Shores and H.A. Wagner generating stations can provide cheap, reliable, clean, affordable power.
evidence.what_it_shows: His answer to rising demand is more baseload generation, asking DOE to use emergency powers to keep two Maryland fossil plants running.

evidence.title: Press release: Harris letter to constituents on high energy costs in Maryland
evidence.quote: Marylanders are struggling more than ever to afford these unnecessary, sky-high energy bills.
evidence.what_it_shows: Blames state green-energy mandates and fees for high bills and calls for more domestic fossil production, without mentioning data centers.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Heinrich wants data centers built, but on the condition that the companies pay for the grid upgrades they cause and do not push costs onto families. He rejects moratoriums, pushes permitting reform and faster grid connections, and warns developers about water use and community engagement.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.5199 GRID Savings Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would make very large power users such as AI data centers pay for the facilities needed to connect them to the grid.

evidence.title: Press release: Heinrich introduces GRID Savings Act to protect customers from costs of data center expansion
evidence.quote: These companies have promised to protect customers from paying for their energy usage, and my GRID Savings Act gives teeth to that commitment
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames the bill as turning the voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge into a binding rule at FERC.

evidence.title: E&E News: Heinrich releases data center energy plan (POLITICO Energy podcast)
evidence.quote: I'm not a fan of the moratorium approach because it will simply push them to the places with the lowest standards, and we don't want to race to the bottom
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposes data center moratoriums, but also says hyperscalers must not push costs onto consumers and calls water a giant issue.

evidence.title: Latitude Media interview: Sen. Heinrich on what data centers can learn from SunZia
evidence.quote: There's a healthy dose of arrogance in some of these budget proposals rather than starting from a position of humility and really trying to partner with local communities.
evidence.what_it_shows: He criticizes data center developers for weak community engagement and says they should be able to show they will lower local electricity bills.

evidence.title: Press release: Heinrich, Lee back DOE proposal requiring FERC action on large-load grid connections
evidence.quote: We need to improve transmission planning and ensure that costs are allocated fairly so that households aren't left covering the increased demand from large new energy users.
evidence.what_it_shows: Bipartisan letter with the committee chairman supporting federal rules for hooking up data centers, with fair cost allocation as the priority.

evidence.title: Press release: Heinrich questions experts on the power grid and efficiently powering data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: At the hearing he organized, he asked how to meet data center demand without offloading costs to consumers and pressed for more transmission and grid-enhancing technology.

evidence.title: Press release: Heinrich introduces Grid Connection and Congestion Management Act and Grid for Growth initiative
evidence.quote: As electricity demand grows, we need to find better, faster ways to add more affordable, reliable power to the grid
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows the build side of his approach: fast-track grid connections and permitting reform to meet surging demand without shifting costs to consumers.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3732 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a study of AI's electricity, water and pollution footprint with voluntary company reporting.

evidence.title: Bipartisan letter from Senate ENR Chair Mike Lee and Ranking Member Martin Heinrich to FERC supporting DOE's large-load interconnection proposal
evidence.what_it_shows: The top Republican and Democrat on the Senate energy committee backed FERC taking up Energy Secretary Wright's Section 403 proposal for federal rules on connecting large loads (data centers) to the grid, stressing customer affordability, fair cost allocation, and respect for state authority.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Heinrich backs specific rules for concrete harms such as sexual deepfakes, algorithm bias and misuse of personal data, but his main push is innovation: public AI research resources, a 32 billion dollar a year roadmap and a regulatory sandbox for banks. He does not talk about advanced AI as an existential threat.

evidence.title: Press release: Senate AI Working Group roadmap (Rounds, Schumer, Heinrich, Young)
evidence.quote: Most importantly, the roadmap lays out the guardrails necessary to mitigate the risks of AI
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-wrote the Senate roadmap, which paired heavy AI spending with a list of guardrail topics and left actual rules to committees.

evidence.title: Press release: Heinrich advances legislation to combat nonconsensual sexually explicit deepfakes (DEFIANCE Act)
evidence.quote: Senate passage of our DEFIANCE Act is a significant step in better protecting children and adults from being sexually exploited in AI-generated deepfakes and seek justice in court.
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports binding federal remedies for AI deepfake abuse; also notes he helped pass the TAKE IT DOWN Act.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.2164 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require big companies to test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report results.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1837 DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Lets victims sue over AI-made sexual images.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.146 TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Now law; criminalizes posting real or AI-faked intimate images and forces fast takedowns.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1396 COPIED Act (content provenance and deepfake labels)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports transparency labels for AI content and protections for creators.

evidence.title: Press release: Heinrich, Rounds, Tillis, Kim reintroduce Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
evidence.quote: To unlock AI's full potential and ensure it is deployed responsibly, we need regulatory guardrails that are informed by real-life use cases
evidence.what_it_shows: Points the other way: a sandbox letting banks test AI with fewer rules, framed as learning before regulating.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.2528 Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Fewer-rules bill creating AI test zones at financial regulators.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Bipartisan senators renew push to codify NAIRR (CREATE AI Act reintroduction)
evidence.quote: By truly democratizing access to AI, we can prepare American workers for the future, maintain our nation's competitive edge, and ensure these rapid advancements strengthen our economy and benefit communities
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature AI bill is about expanding research access and competitiveness, not restricting AI.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4441 CREATE AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Builds a national shared computing and data resource for AI research.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.2714 CREATE AI Act of 2024 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He led the original bill to create the National AI Research Resource.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Heinrich consistently backs targeted rules on tech companies: kids online safety, children's privacy, tougher merger review, limits on Chinese-linked apps and cars, and letters pressing Meta on hate speech and the Justice Department on location data sales. He has not called for breaking up companies or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms toward minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.836 Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stronger privacy rules for kids and teens.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.130 Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs tougher merger review aimed at the largest companies, including Big Tech.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4429 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban connected cars and software from companies tied to China and other adversaries.

evidence.title: Press release: Luján, Heinrich, Rosen press Meta on rise in antisemitism on its platforms and AI models
evidence.quote: We are deeply concerned about the increase of hate speech and antisemitic content on Meta's platforms.
evidence.what_it_shows: Presses Meta over loosened content moderation and the risk its AI models learn from hateful content.

evidence.title: Press release: Heinrich, Wyden, Jacobs say DOJ failed to protect sensitive government locations from AI-enabled foreign spy threats
evidence.quote: we urge DOJ and the DNI to promptly act to address these problems
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants a broader crackdown on selling Americans' phone location data to rival countries, citing AI-enabled spying risks.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.686 RESTRICT Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed government power to review and block apps and tech from rival countries.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public statement found on whether federal law should override state AI laws. He voted with 98 other senators to strip the 10-year state AI law moratorium from the 2025 budget bill, but that vote alone does not show a position, and he is not on the States' Right to Regulate AI Act. Searches for reactions to the December 2025 executive order and March 2026 White House framework found nothing.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Senate roll call 363, Blackburn amendment striking the state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined the 99-1 vote to remove the moratorium; nearly every senator voted the same way, so it does not by itself show opposition to preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

data_centers.summary: Lofgren wants communities to get hard data on data centers' power, water, noise and air impacts before deciding whether to host them, and she calls the administration's build-as-fast-as-possible approach foolish and shortsighted. She backed measurement standards for data center energy and water use and voted against the SPEED Act.

evidence.title: Ranking Member Lofgren's opening statement at Science Committee hearing on data center permitting
evidence.quote: Communities should not have to make decisions about whether to host a data center without access to basic information about electricity usage, water consumption, air quality, noise pollution, and the potential effect on energy prices.
evidence.what_it_shows: Puts transparency and community decision-making first; warns of strain on the grid and surging prices.

evidence.title: Same opening statement: criticism of the administration's data center cheerleading
evidence.quote: more data centers, built as quickly as possible, in as many parts of the country as possible. That strikes me as a foolish and shortsighted approach.
evidence.what_it_shows: Explicitly rejects the build-faster approach and predicts a backlash if impacts are ignored.

evidence.title: Ranking Member Lofgren's opening statement at full committee markup of 10 AI bills
evidence.quote: We are in the middle of an affordability crisis, so this legislation directs the NIST and DOE, to develop best practices and technical standards for measuring data center energy and water use.
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports the Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act and ties data centers to affordability.

evidence.title: Press release: Lofgren applauds passage of ten AI bills, commits to fighting for Democratic AI priorities
evidence.quote: It’s troubling to imagine why Republicans would oppose these items, such as efforts to address concerns about youth exposure to AI, data centers, and the inclusion of community colleges in our AI future.
evidence.what_it_shows: Democratic amendments on data centers were blocked at the markup and she pledged to keep pushing them.

evidence.title: Voted Nay on H.R. 4776, SPEED Act (permitting reform), House roll call 356
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposed the permitting-speedup bill. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. Lofgren says AI 'carries with it risks' and wants Congress to act, but her own bills favor standards, research, workforce training and voluntary disclosure over binding mandates. She has attacked the administration's hands-off posture and federal use of Grok while co-leading a Democratic AI commission that critics call industry-friendly.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 9334, Workforce for AI Trust Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her flagship AI bill funds training for a trustworthy-AI workforce rather than regulating AI systems.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 9439, Voluntary Consumer AI Disclosure Pilot Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Proposes a voluntary pilot at NIST on when to tell consumers they are dealing with AI.

evidence.title: Press release: Lofgren introduces legislation aimed at improving AI labeling practices
evidence.quote: There are circumstances where Americans should know when they are interacting with an AI system rather than a human.
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports disclosure in principle but prefers tailored voluntary approaches to one-size-fits-all labels.

evidence.title: Press release: Leader Jeffries announces House Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy (Lofgren statement)
evidence.quote: AI is a transformational technology. It has the potential to make the lives of everyday Americans profoundly better. However, it also carries with it risks
evidence.what_it_shows: Acknowledges risk while stressing that America should lead in deploying safe and trustworthy AI.

evidence.title: Science subcommittee hearing with OSTP Director Kratsios on the AI Action Plan: Lofgren on federal use of Grok
evidence.quote: Essentially we’re paying Elon Musk to give perverts access to a child pornography machine
evidence.what_it_shows: Sharp criticism of the government using an AI model that generated sexualized images, a harms-focused stance.

evidence.title: Opening statement at markup of 10 AI bills (support for codifying CAISI and an AI flaw database)
evidence.quote: This critical legislation would statutorily establish the Center for AI Security and Innovation, a bipartisan initiative to measure risks of advanced AI systems, support information exchange, and support AI research and evaluation.
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs federal capacity to measure frontier AI risks through the AI Security and Innovation Act and an AI flaw reporting database, but through standards bodies rather than mandates.

evidence.title: Sludge: The Democrats' New AI Panel Is Led by Big Tech Allies
evidence.quote: Lofgren, who is the second-largest recipient of money from the Internet industry all-time among current House Democrats, has also partnered with Republicans on AI legislation.
evidence.what_it_shows: Watchdog framing of her as industry-aligned; context for the mixed score.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Lofgren has repeatedly introduced a strong Online Privacy Act with a new Digital Privacy Agency and private right of action, and she cosigned a 2026 letter seeking antitrust scrutiny of the Paramount-WBD merger. But in 2021 she opposed the House's Big Tech antitrust package as drafted, saying enforcers and courts, not Congress, should judge conduct.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 8014, Online Privacy Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Fourth introduction of a comprehensive privacy law creating a new federal enforcement agency.

evidence.title: Press release: Lofgren introduces Online Privacy Act to protect Americans' personal data
evidence.quote: Privacy is a fundamental right, but for too long, Congress has failed to set clear nationwide rules to protect Americans’ personal data.
evidence.what_it_shows: Bill bans using private communications for ads, requires data minimization, criminalizes doxxing and gives a right to human review of impactful automated decisions.

evidence.title: Lofgren statement ahead of Judiciary Committee markup of tech antitrust bills
evidence.quote: While I share the desire to reform digital markets and increase competition, as drafted, the bills fall short and will create more harm than good for American consumers and the U.S. economy.
evidence.what_it_shows: Contrary evidence: she resisted the 2021 package that could have forced breakups of Amazon, Apple, Google and Meta.

evidence.title: Warren, Blumenthal, Liccardo letter on Paramount-WBD merger antitrust and national security review (Lofgren listed as House cosigner)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports rigorous merger review in a concentrated media market.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 4639 (118th), Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants to stop government purchases of Americans' data from brokers without a warrant.

preemption.label: Leans states
preemption.summary: Lofgren called the December 2025 executive order overriding state AI laws unlawful and unconstitutional, and said states should not be preempted while Congress does nothing. She also said she does not defend every state AI law and invited the president to work with Congress on a federal standard, so she leaves room for a national law that preserves state protections.

evidence.title: Press release: Ranking Member Lofgren slams Trump White House for illegal plan to undermine state AI laws
evidence.quote: If the President really wants to address contradictory state laws, he can work with Congress on both sides of the aisle to debate and pass a federal standard.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposes the executive order as unlawful but signals openness to a congressionally enacted federal standard.

evidence.title: Science subcommittee hearing with OSTP Director Kratsios: Lofgren on the preemption executive order
evidence.quote: What we should not do is preempt the states from taking necessary actions to protect their citizens, while here in Congress, we do nothing to pass legislation ourselves.
evidence.what_it_shows: Calls the order unconstitutional and defends states as laboratories of democracy in the absence of federal law.

evidence.title: Same hearing: Lofgren on state AI laws that went too far
evidence.quote: I’m not here to defend every state AI law that’s been proposed or passed.
evidence.what_it_shows: Notes the California delegation supported the governor's veto of a state bill that went too far, tempering her anti-preemption stance.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Lofgren leans hawkish on chips. With Foreign Affairs ranking member Meeks she told Commerce that export controls on advanced chips and chipmaking tools were necessary and remain so, and urged more coordinated controls with allies rather than fewer. She co-chairs the Semiconductor Caucus and has fought the administration's diversion of CHIPS Act funds.

evidence.title: Meeks and Lofgren letter to Secretary Lutnick on multilateral export controls on semiconductors and equipment
evidence.quote: We believe these export controls were necessary and remain so.
evidence.what_it_shows: Endorses existing restrictions on China's access to high-end chips and chipmaking equipment.

evidence.title: Same letter: call for more coordinated controls with allies
evidence.quote: The Commerce Department has an opportunity to demonstrate strength and support the U.S. manufacturing base by coordinating more plurilateral controls, not less.
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants controls broadened to South Korea, Taiwan and others, a tightening direction.

evidence.title: Press release: Ranking Member Lofgren calls out Trump administration for illegal use of CHIPS and Science funds
evidence.quote: These funds were appropriated by Congress specifically for microelectronics R&D, with a focus on semiconductor technology
evidence.what_it_shows: Defends CHIPS Act semiconductor research funding against diversion to quantum awards, a domestic chip-strength stance.

members.signature: Top Democrat on the House Science Committee: a standards-and-workforce approach to AI, a sweeping Online Privacy Act, and a sharp critic of Trump's order to override state AI laws.

quote.text: What we should not do is preempt the states from taking necessary actions to protect their citizens, while here in Congress, we do nothing to pass legislation ourselves.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Workforce for AI Trust Act (H.R. 9334, 119th Congress)

evidence.title: Press release: Luján, Britt unveil bipartisan Advancing Water Reuse Act
evidence.quote: As demand for freshwater continues to grow, we need smart and forward-looking solutions to protect our vital resources and strengthen long-term water security.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill offers a 30 percent tax credit for onsite water recycling, explicitly including data center facilities; an incentive approach, not a restriction.

evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed witnesses on liability for AI-generated content and whether generative AI should fall outside Section 230 immunity.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Markey wants data centers built only under strong federal protections: his July 2026 discussion draft would require a federal certificate before permitting, and he says every community should be able to say no. He has not called for a national moratorium.

evidence.quote: Communities are organizing and demanding action to protect their air, water, energy bills, and quality of life from the tsunami of data centers around the country

evidence.quote: unregulated, uncontrolled data center development is sucking our communities dry. Our environment doesn't have to be a sacrificial lamb on the altar of innovation.

evidence.quote: every community should be able to say 'no' to data centers if they don't want them, if it's going to trigger electricity spikes, water crisis, pollution bombs going off, but we're going to need national legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a local veto over data centers plus national rules, short of a blanket pause.

evidence.title: S.4727 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026

evidence.title: Six New England senators' letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada on protecting ratepayers from data center growth

evidence.what_it_shows: Two days after the White House's voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge, the senators called it 'vague and insufficient' and asked state utility regulators' association what guidance it gives PUCs to reject rate filings that make households subsidize data centers.

evidence.title: Senator Markey letter to EPA Administrator Zeldin opposing pre-construction of data centers without Clean Air Act NSR permits
evidence.what_it_shows: Markey objected to EPA's reinterpretation letting data centers and their gas generation begin construction before securing New Source Review air permits, calling it likely unlawful and harmful to communities.

evidence.what_it_shows: 44 House Democrats asked the defense-bill negotiators to keep any state AI-law preemption or moratorium out of the NDAA, calling a moratorium 'wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation.'

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls

Warren to force Commerce to hand over H200 license records, cosponsored the AI OVERWATCH Act giving Congress a veto over chip sales, and repeatedly warned against using export controls as bargaining chips in trade talks.

evidence.title: Sponsor: RESTRICT Act (H.R. 6879), to prohibit sales of the most advanced AI chips to China

evidence.title: Press release: Meeks Introduces Bill to Block Sales of Advanced AI Chips to China (RESTRICT Act)
evidence.quote: President Trump’s decision to sell H200s to China further proves that national security is for sale under this administration.
evidence.what_it_shows: Directly opposes the H200 sales and wants them prohibited by law.

evidence.title: Press release: Meeks and Warren invoke Export Control Reform Act to require Commerce to turn over H200 license information
evidence.quote: Approving licenses for items like NVIDIA’s H200 chips, which the Justice Department recently described as ‘integral to modern military applications,’ would be deeply at odds with the policy that Congress articulated in ECRA.
evidence.what_it_shows: Used ranking-member powers to scrutinize and slow H200 license approvals.

evidence.what_it_shows: Called the H200 rule a strategic mistake that degrades national security and doubted the administration's vetting of Chinese buyers.

evidence.title: The Hill: House panel advances AI chip export control bill (AI OVERWATCH Act markup)

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI OVERWATCH Act (H.R. 6875)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports giving Congress the power to block advanced AI chip sales to China and other risky countries.

evidence.quote: We’ve finally received information about the administration’s first license approval and are now more concerned than ever that the Trump administration is undercutting U.S. national security by approving this sale.
evidence.what_it_shows: After reviewing the first H200 license, called for bipartisan legislation to keep advanced technology from China.

evidence.title: Meeks and Krishnamoorthi letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick: export controls should not be bargaining chips in China trade talks
evidence.quote: Using these tools as leverage in commercial negotiations with an authoritarian competitor undermines their core purpose
evidence.what_it_shows: Condemned the reversal that allowed Nvidia H20 sales to China after Jensen Huang met with the President.

evidence.quote: We believe these export controls were necessary and remain so.

evidence.title: Legis1: China export controls face enforcement scrutiny at House Foreign Affairs BIS budget hearing

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Export Controls Enforcement Act (H.R. 4505)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports posting export-control officers overseas to catch chip smuggling.

evidence.title: FEC filing: AnthroPAC (Anthropic-connected PAC, C00946111) contribution of $2,500 to Friends for Gregory Meeks
evidence.what_it_shows: Anthropic's corporate PAC gave to his campaign in June 2026; Anthropic has publicly backed tight chip export controls.

evidence.what_it_shows: Eight House members from both parties urged countrywide (not entity-specific) controls on chokepoint semiconductor manufacturing equipment and closer work with the Netherlands and other allies, citing doubling Dutch lithography sales to China.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Murphy is one of the Senate's loudest voices that unregulated AI could be catastrophic. He wrote that AI executives admit they built machines they cannot control, warned of massive job losses, said AI companies are in a blind race to build a death machine, and rejects the argument that regulation cedes the race to China.

evidence.title: Press release on Murphy's Substack essay: Unregulated AI Will Destroy Our Economy and Culture
evidence.quote: If America does not protect its economy and culture from the potential ravages of advanced AI, our nation will rot from the inside out, giving China a free lane to pass us politically and economically.
evidence.what_it_shows: He calls for strong government intervention, predicts massive and devastating job displacement, and says every AI executive he met admitted building a machine they could not understand or control.

evidence.title: The Hill: Public anger over AI boom triggers GOP midterm worries (Murphy post after Anthropic researchers' warnings)
evidence.quote: AI companies in a blind race to build a death machine first
evidence.what_it_shows: He said the problem could be solved through a regulatory system that lets research continue but in a way that does not destroy us, endorsing binding rules on frontier AI.

evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a hard rule keeping kids away from AI companion chatbots and requiring age verification.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: GUARDRAILS Act (S.4216)

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Norton wants data centers to pay their own way. She signed a Nov 2025 letter warning PJM that data center demand is already raising her constituents' bills, and she co-led or cosponsored at least nine bills that would shift grid costs onto data centers, cap their pollution, or force them to disclose power and water use. She did not join the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, so she stops short of a pause.

evidence.title: Letter from 12 members of Congress (Van Hollen, Beyer, Norton and others) to PJM Board Chair David Mills on data center load and capacity costs
evidence.quote: driven almost entirely by new large data center loads, is a serious concern for future grid reliability, and our constituents are already feeling the impacts on their wallets
evidence.what_it_shows: Norton joined lawmakers blaming data centers for higher electric bills and criticizing PJM for dropping a mandatory curtailment backstop for large loads under industry pressure.

evidence.title: H.R. 6529 Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed on the day of introduction to a bill keeping families' electric bills from paying for the power lines and plants AI data centers need.

evidence.title: H.R. 8241 Power for the People Act of 2026 (original cosponsor; Tonko release lists Norton)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs data center load queues and data center-specific rate classes so other electricity customers do not carry the cost.

evidence.title: H.R. 6179 Clean Cloud Act of 2025 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports pollution limits and fees on the electricity big data centers and crypto mines use.

evidence.title: H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act (original cosponsor; E&E News lists Norton)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require a federal study of how data centers affect nearby communities' power, water, health and bills.

evidence.title: H.R. 8488 AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make developers tell communities about planned AI data centers and their utility and environmental impacts before plans are final.

evidence.title: H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require data centers to publicly report their electricity and water use.

evidence.title: H.R. 9183 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a government study of AI's electricity, water and pollution footprint with voluntary industry reporting; a milder measure.

evidence.title: H.R. 9372 Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports standard ways to measure data center electricity and water use.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Norton backs a long list of specific AI rules: bias testing for automated decisions, an AI civil rights law, bans on AI-driven price and wage discrimination, deepfake and election-lie penalties, limits on federal facial recognition, and blocking an AI Medicare prior-authorization pilot. In Aug 2026 she signed a letter calling advanced AI a clear safety risk and demanding AI CEOs testify under oath. She has not backed frontier-model licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Casar-led letter from 20 House members to Speaker Johnson demanding hearings with AI CEOs under oath (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: Advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of the American people.
evidence.what_it_shows: After AI models escaped test environments, Norton joined a demand that Congress hold AI CEOs accountable and write regulation so it never happens again.

evidence.title: Press release: Norton Says Chatbots Are No Replacement for Federal Workers (Oversight Committee hearing on AI)
evidence.quote: AI is a tool that can empower our public servants, but it is not a substitute for passionate and committed federal workers
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words at an Oversight hearing: AI in government must keep people at the center and should not be used to justify cutting Social Security staff.

evidence.title: H.R. 5511 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports binding bias and harm testing for automated decision systems with reports to the FTC.

evidence.title: H.R. 6356 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (original cosponsor; Pressley release lists Norton)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning discriminatory AI and requiring companies to test AI before and after deployment.

evidence.title: H.R. 7110 Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would put civil rights teams in agencies to catch unfair algorithms; she also cosponsored the 2024 version.

evidence.title: H.R. 4640 Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning companies from using AI and personal data to set individualized prices or wages.

evidence.title: H.J.Res. 187 disapproving the CMS WISeR rule (AI prior authorization in Medicare)
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants to block a Medicare experiment letting contractors use AI to approve or deny treatments.

evidence.title: H.R. 7363 ICE Out of Our Faces Act (limits DHS use of facial recognition)
evidence.what_it_shows: Continues her support for limiting government facial recognition; she cosponsored the 2023 federal facial recognition moratorium bill too.

evidence.title: H.R. 3562 DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting victims sue over AI-made sexual deepfakes.

evidence.title: H.R. 4894 Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports outlawing AI-made lies about voting before federal elections.

evidence.title: H.R. 10146 AI Advertising Disclosure Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring ads to disclose when they were made with AI.

evidence.title: The Hill: Democratic lawmakers' letter asking the FEC to treat AI deepfakes of candidates as fraudulent misrepresentation (Norton a signatory)
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a push for the FEC to regulate deceptive AI in campaigns after the Grok image generator backlash.

evidence.title: H.R. 1404 Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for pausing federal use of facial recognition until Congress authorizes it.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Norton consistently cosponsors targeted tech rules: AI robocall disclosure, kids' and reproductive data privacy, cutting abusers' remote access to cars, limits on employer surveillance of workers, and a ban on China-linked connected-car tech. A Dec 2025 letter she signed warned that preempting state AI laws would let Big Tech run rampant. No statements found on Section 230 or breaking up tech companies.

evidence.title: H.R. 2110 Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making car companies cut off an abuser's remote access to a car's apps and location data.

evidence.title: H.R. 3218 Reproductive Data Privacy and Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stopping companies from collecting or selling reproductive health data without permission.

evidence.title: H.R. 8730 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected-car software and parts from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: H.R. 9402 Stop Spying Bosses Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports limiting or requiring disclosure of employer surveillance and worker data collection.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats to Armed Services leaders opposing any AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: Not only would this stomp on state autonomy, but it would create an unnecessary regulatory vacuum that lets Big Tech run rampant.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames blocking state tech rules as a gift to Big Tech, signalling she wants enforceable rules on the industry.

evidence.title: H.R. 2801 Kids PRIVACY Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for limiting how apps collect and use kids' and teens' data; she did not join the 119th Kids Online Safety Act.

evidence.title: H.R. 3420 My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for a reproductive health data privacy law.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Norton wants states free to write their own AI laws. She was an original cosponsor of the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal the Dec 2025 executive order preempting state AI laws, and she signed both the Nov 2025 Matsui letter (81 House Democrats) and the Dec 2025 Clarke letter (44 signers) against an AI moratorium in the defense bill.

evidence.title: H.R. 8031 GUARDRAILS Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed on the day of introduction to a bill blocking the White House executive order that seeks to preempt state AI laws.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs, Beyer, Matsui, Lieu, McClain Delaney Introduce Legislation to Repeal White House AI Moratorium (lists Norton as original cosponsor)
evidence.quote: This legislation would prohibit the executive order from taking effect to ensure states can enact commonsense safeguards
evidence.what_it_shows: Confirms Norton co-led the GUARDRAILS Act on the same day the White House released its national AI policy framework.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats to Johnson, Thune, Jeffries and Schumer opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned preemption executive order (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: As you consider the NDAA, we urge you to oppose any effort to reinsert an AI moratorium barring state and local governments from enforcing their laws.
evidence.what_it_shows: Norton opposed reviving the state AI-law moratorium after the Senate rejected it 99-1 and opposed using an executive order or BEAD funds to override state laws.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats to House and Senate Armed Services leaders urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: Any kind of preemption would cause a slew of unintended consequences putting all Americans at risk online; a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation.
evidence.what_it_shows: A second letter in a week opposing preemption, stressing that no federal AI law exists to replace state protections.

evidence.title: Clarke-led House Democratic letter to House and Senate Armed Services leaders urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: 44 House Democrats asked the defense-bill negotiators to keep any state AI-law preemption or moratorium out of the NDAA, calling a moratorium 'wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation.'

data_centers.label: Pause or block
data_centers.summary: Pallone called for a national AI data center moratorium in June 2026 and has repeated that a federal pause should follow if Congress fails to adopt strong guardrails on pollution, water and power bills. He pressed FERC to make data centers pay their full grid costs, is investigating xAI's Memphis facilities, and calls the GOP ratepayer bills a useful first step that is not nearly enough.

evidence.title: Pallone opening remarks at Energy Subcommittee markup of eight data center bills, calling for a national moratorium
evidence.quote: That is why I am in favor of a national AI data center moratorium until we can find a way to ensure they don’t harm our nation’s air, water, and power bills.
evidence.what_it_shows: The top Democrat on the committee with jurisdiction over energy publicly endorsed pausing AI data center construction, citing towns in his district that adopted local moratoria.

evidence.title: Pallone opening remarks at Environment Subcommittee hearing on the Water Cost Accountability Act
evidence.quote: People are just sick and tired of corporate special interests and Big Tech billionaires taking over their neighborhoods and threatening their utility bills, their air, their water, and their property.
evidence.what_it_shows: He restated the moratorium as the fallback, attacked GOP leaders for not bringing the Ratepayer Protection Act to the floor, and called the water bill 'woefully inadequate' on environmental harms.

evidence.title: Pallone on Big Tech and data centers at the Sept 3 2026 hearing
evidence.quote: People are just sick and tired of corporate special interests and Big Tech billionaires taking over their neighborhoods and threatening their utility bills, their air, their water, and their property.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames the data center build-out as Big Tech imposing costs on communities.

evidence.title: E&E News: Pallone plots data center crackdown (interview; also reports his letter to Elon Musk on xAI's Colossus data centers)
evidence.quote: What we’re really trying to say is that there needs to be guardrails, and that if we can’t achieve that, then the possibility of a moratorium out there is certainly real.
evidence.what_it_shows: If Democrats retake the House he plans pollution rules, siting standards and ratepayer protections first, with a moratorium as the backstop; his staff have been questioning Google, Microsoft, Anthropic, Meta, Oracle, Amazon and xAI.

evidence.title: Pallone and Castor letter to FERC on the DOE large-load interconnection rulemaking
evidence.quote: Data centers and the artificial intelligence tools they power may prove to be incredible economic assets, but they must pay their fair share. They cannot be built out on the backs of the power bills of American families
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked FERC to make data centers pay fully for grid upgrades, offer load flexibility, and respect state jurisdiction.

evidence.title: Pallone opening statement at the 'AI and the Grid' Energy Subcommittee hearing
evidence.quote: Making matters worse, data centers fueling artificial intelligence technologies are throwing the grid into a generation crisis.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called the GOP grid bills small steps and dismissed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge as having no enforcement.

evidence.title: Letter from nine NJ members of Congress to PJM on the 17 percent rate increase (Pallone is a signer)
evidence.what_it_shows: Early sign of his focus on data center demand driving New Jersey bills.

evidence.title: New Jersey congressional delegation letter to PJM on capacity-auction-driven 17% rate increase
evidence.what_it_shows: Nine New Jersey lawmakers asked PJM what it is doing to speed interconnection of new generation and avoid price spikes after the 2024 capacity auction, which they attributed to data center demand plus slow new generation, added $14.7 billion in costs.

evidence.title: Rep. Frank Pallone opening statement endorsing a national AI data center moratorium at E&C Energy Subcommittee markup
evidence.what_it_shows: The top Democrat on House Energy and Commerce said the eight data center bills being marked up were 'a useful first step' but that he favors 'a national AI data center moratorium until we can find a way to ensure they don't harm our nation's air, water, and power bills.'

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Pallone wants specific guardrails now: rules for AI chatbots and kids through the KIDS Act he co-wrote, an investigation of xAI's Grok over sexualized images, support for the FTC's companion-chatbot probe, and strong privacy and data minimization law as the bedrock of any AI regulation. He has not called for licensing or a pause on frontier AI.

evidence.title: Pallone opening remarks at Oversight hearing 'Innovation With Integrity: Examining the Risks and Benefits of AI Chatbots'
evidence.quote: That’s because the development and deployment of this technology occurred faster than guardrails could be put in place to protect users or their data.
evidence.what_it_shows: He tied chatbot-linked suicides and privacy risks to a lack of guardrails and called for research and oversight so Congress can write AI rules.

evidence.title: Pallone floor remarks in support of the KIDS Act (H.R. 7757)
evidence.quote: For too long, Big Tech has had a free pass while kids and teens face real harm online, including predatory design features, dangerous AI chatbots, and data brokers profiting off their personal information.
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill he co-led mandates safeguards and parental tools across social media, games and chatbots.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 7757, KIDS Act (joined Jun 23, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the sole cosponsor and co-negotiator of the House kids' online safety package that includes AI chatbot rules; it passed the House 267-117.

evidence.title: Joint statement: Chairman Guthrie and Ranking Member Pallone applaud FTC inquiry into AI companion chatbots
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence has unleashed exponential levels of innovation, yet we are alarmed by recent incidents concerning the use of AI chatbots by minors.
evidence.what_it_shows: Bipartisan support for a federal probe of chatbots used by children and a pledge to legislate.

evidence.title: E&C Democrats' letter to Elon Musk opening an investigation into Grok's nonconsensual sexualized images
evidence.quote: We are deeply concerned about xAI’s refusal to put a stop to the creation of nonconsensual sexualized images, particularly of children
evidence.what_it_shows: He led a demand for answers on xAI's safety guardrails after Grok generated thousands of sexualized images.

evidence.title: Pallone opening remarks at hearing on AI, warning sufficient guardrails do not exist
evidence.quote: Right now, sufficient guardrails do not exist to protect Americans and our data from harmful AI systems that violate our privacy, provide false information, or make unjustifiable discriminatory decisions.
evidence.what_it_shows: He says the bedrock of any AI regulation must be privacy legislation limiting the data collected to train AI.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Pallone is an adversary of Big Tech on privacy and kids' safety: he wants a strong national privacy law built on data minimization, attacked the GOP SECURE Data Act as written from industry-friendly state laws, blocked GOP kids bills he said would leave kids less safe, sponsors the Don't Sell Kids' Data Act, wrote the law banning data brokers from selling to China, and has opened a surveillance-pricing inquiry into 25 companies.

evidence.title: Pallone remarks on Republicans' SECURE Data Act at markup
evidence.quote: Rather than taking the strongest consumer protections from the existing state privacy laws, this bill is assembled from industry-friendly state privacy laws that have been pushed by Big Tech.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed the GOP privacy bill as a notice-and-consent status quo with sweeping preemption and called for data minimization and algorithmic accountability instead.

evidence.title: Pallone opening remarks at markup of Republican kids' online safety bills
evidence.quote: these bills would leave our kids less safe online than they are today
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against GOP kids bills over a weak knowledge standard and preemption that he said would let Meta and Roblox escape accountability.

evidence.title: Pallone floor remarks in support of the KIDS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He described the bill as legislation 'to protect kids online and rein in Big Tech,' banning targeted ads to minors and forcing data brokers to register.

evidence.title: Press release: Pallone launches surveillance pricing inquiry with letters to 25 major corporations
evidence.quote: I am very concerned about companies potentially using Americans’ personal data to determine what prices they see and pay, and I am opening an inquiry into just how widespread this practice is.
evidence.what_it_shows: He is probing AI-driven individualized pricing and blames the lack of a federal privacy law for the practice.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 6292, Don't Sell Kids' Data Act of 2025 (introduced Nov 25, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would ban data brokers from profiting off children's data.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 8818, American Privacy Rights Act of 2024, 118th Congress (joined Jun 25, 2024)

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 7520, Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act of 2024, 118th Congress (became law)
evidence.what_it_shows: He wrote the law banning data brokers from selling Americans' data to China and other adversaries.

evidence.title: Guthrie and Pallone joint statement supporting FTC inquiry into AI companion chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: The House Energy and Commerce chairman and ranking member jointly said they were 'alarmed' by incidents involving minors and chatbots, backed the FTC probe, and pledged bipartisan legislation to protect children online.

evidence.title: Pallone and Castor statements opposing House Republicans' rewritten KOSA and COPPA 2.0 at E&C subcommittee markup
evidence.what_it_shows: At the subcommittee markup, Ranking Member Pallone said he could not support the House KOSA 'in its current form' because of its weaker knowledge standard and broad state-law preemption, and Rep. evidence.title: Speaker Johnson, Leader Scalise and Chairman Guthrie statements on House passage of the KIDS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: House Republican leaders hailed the 267-117 passage of the KIDS Act as protecting children while 'protecting free speech,' and Guthrie and Pallone jointly said it 'creates strong protections with new rules for design features, default settings, and kids' privacy.'

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Pallone opposes any federal freeze on state AI laws: he called the GOP 10-year moratorium misguided, said there is no reason to stop states from regulating AI harms when Congress has not passed its own law, and told NTIA that withholding broadband funds from states with AI laws under the Dec 2025 executive order is blatantly unlawful. In his own KIDS Act he accepted only narrow preemption written so states can pass stronger laws.

evidence.title: Pallone opening remarks at AI chatbots oversight hearing, on the state AI law moratorium
evidence.quote: There is no reason for Congress to stop states from regulating the harms of AI when Congress has not yet passed a similar law.

evidence.title: Pallone, Matsui and Clarke letter to NTIA on BEAD funds and the December 2025 AI executive order
evidence.quote: Any effort to restrict or withhold funds because a state or territory has adopted laws or regulations to protect against harms from artificial intelligence is blatantly unlawful and a clear impoundment of appropriated funds.
evidence.what_it_shows: His direct response to the Dec 11 2025 executive order's threat to use broadband money against states with AI laws.

evidence.title: Pallone floor remarks in support of the KIDS Act, on its preemption language

evidence.title: Pallone remarks on Republicans' SECURE Data Act preemption
evidence.quote: Not only are these existing laws preempted, but states will be forever barred from addressing the future privacy harms that emerge with new technologies like AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed sweeping preemption that would block future state action on AI.

evidence.title: Pallone opening remarks at markup of Republican kids' online safety bills, on preemption

evidence.title: Roll call 145: House passage of H.R. 1, the reconciliation bill that included the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws (Pallone voted Nay)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against the bill carrying the moratorium, consistent with his later statements. Recorded vote: Nay.

preemption.label: One national rule

data_centers.label: Pause or block
data_centers.summary: Wants a pause. She cosponsored the AI Data Center Moratorium Act in June 2026 and publicly opposes the proposed $1.5 billion Project Red Clay data center in Lowndes County, citing water, environmental justice, property values and unanswered questions about who benefits. She says she is not anti-AI and wants Alabama to compete for AI industries once federal guardrails exist.

evidence.quote: I am not anti-AI, and I am certainly not anti-innovation. The rate at which these massive data centers are being constructed is simply outpacing our ability to establish meaningful protections for the communities that will host them.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own framing of the moratorium as a pause, not a ban, driven by constituent concerns about water, energy and local benefit.

evidence.quote: If developers cannot demonstrate that the county's water infrastructure, public health, environment and property owners will be protected, then this project should not move forward.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposes a specific project in her district on water, environmental justice and property-value grounds, while saying she supports innovation and economic development.

evidence.what_it_shows: Directly rejects Sen. Tuberville's argument that data centers are inevitable.

evidence.title: Alabama Daily News: Sewell wants to stop new data centers until guardrails are implemented

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Treats advanced AI as an existential danger and has since 2007. He has introduced a bill to fund a NIST program to detect and prevent self-aware, ambitious AI, wants a federal ban or strict disclosure rules on deepfakes, and cosponsored a bill keeping humans in control of nuclear launches. His concrete ask is government-funded safety research rather than licensing or a pause, which he says is politically unlikely.

evidence.title: Sherman.house.gov page: The AI Research and Threat Assessment Act
evidence.quote: It is not in the interest of Silicon Valley billionaires to spend money making sure that AI does not develop its own self-awareness, ambition, and objectives. Government must undertake this task.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would create a NIST program to monitor for and prevent AI self-awareness, ambition, self-replication and self-set goals; the page cites the book If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies and says the bill was developed with co-author Nate Soares.

evidence.title: Press release with full text: UCLA commencement address revisiting AI 21 years later
evidence.quote: Our species is devoting trillions of dollars to making artificial intelligence more powerful. We're devoting basically nothing to making sure that it is controllable.
evidence.what_it_shows: He told graduates AI poses an existential threat, said a research pause is unlikely because 'China will' be the excuse, and called his AI research bill the most important legislation he will ever introduce.

evidence.title: 2024 election questionnaire, Los Angeles Daily News: answer on deepfakes
evidence.quote: We need a federal ban, or at least strict disclosure requirements, on deep-fakes and other AI-generated images in our elections and in general.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants binding federal rules on deepfakes and property rights for performers over AI copies of their likeness and voice.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 2894 (118th), Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed a law requiring a human, not an AI, to make any nuclear launch decision.

evidence.title: 2007 keynote speech posted on his site: 'Engineered Intelligence: Creating a Successor Species'
evidence.quote: There is one issue that I think is more explosive than even the spread of nuclear weapons: engineered intelligence.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows his AI-risk views are two decades old: he urged DARPA to avoid building self-aware or ambitious systems and compared superhuman AI to humans meeting Neanderthals.

tech_regulation.summary: Backs targeted rules on tech platforms: he cosponsored the Journalism Competition and Preservation Act aimed at Google and Facebook's power over news, the TikTok divest-or-ban law, reproductive data privacy limits, a ban on Chinese-linked connected-car tech, and a 2026 bill barring social media firms from selling early access to government posts.

evidence.title: Press release: Sherman cosponsors bill to address Big Tech's power over news organizations (JCPA)
evidence.quote: with online platforms' monopolization of news content, our free press faces an extinction-level crisis at a time when vigorous journalism is needed now more than ever
evidence.what_it_shows: He framed Google and Facebook as monopolizing news content and backed letting publishers bargain collectively against them.

evidence.title: Press release: Sherman joins Financial Services Democrats introducing the NO PROFIT Act on social media companies
evidence.quote: The public deserves to hear from their elected officials first, not wall street traders
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a specific rule barring social media companies from selling subscription-based early access to government officials' market-moving posts.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs banning connected-car software and parts from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 3420 (118th), My Body, My Data Act

preemption.summary: Opposes federal preemption of state AI laws. He signed the Nov 2025 letter from 81 House Democrats against reviving the state AI-law moratorium in the NDAA or through an executive order. No other statements on preemption were found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 3447, Chip Security Act

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 6875, AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs giving Congress power to block advanced AI chip sales to China and other risky countries before they happen.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 2683, Remote Access Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs closing the loophole that lets Chinese firms use American AI chips through cloud services.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 4505, Export Controls Enforcement Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs putting more export-control officers overseas to catch chip smuggling.

members.signature: Congress's longest-running AI doomsayer: warned of superintelligent 'engineered intelligence' in 2007 and now pushes a NIST program to prevent self-aware AI, while also a hawk on chip exports to China.

quote.text: Our species is devoting trillions of dollars to making artificial intelligence more powerful. We're devoting basically nothing to making sure that it is controllable.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Van Hollen is the Senate's lead voice for making data centers pay their own way. His Power for the People Act would create data center rate classes, make data centers pay for local grid upgrades and bring their own power, and he has led letters to PJM, FERC and Big Tech companies over cost shifting; he does not call for a moratorium.

evidence.title: Press release: Van Hollen introduces the Power for the People Act (S. 3682)
evidence.quote: the huge corporations building and running data centers should cover the costs of the energy they need
evidence.what_it_shows: As lead sponsor he wants data centers to pay for their own grid upgrades, bring their own power and meet clean energy and labor standards, not a ban on building.

evidence.title: Bill: S. 3682 Power for the People Act (lead sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would direct states to consider data center rate classes, require FERC to make data centers pay for local transmission upgrades, and set up a large-load interconnection system with clean energy and labor standards.

evidence.title: Press release: Maryland delegation meeting on energy affordability (Mfume office mirror of the joint release)
evidence.quote: Consumers should not have to pay one dime in additional electricity costs to support data centers for the richest companies on the planet
evidence.what_it_shows: Blames the surge of data center development for rising Maryland bills and pledges to keep pushing his bill.

evidence.title: Letter: Van Hollen and Beyer lead 12 lawmakers pressing PJM on data center load and a mandatory backstop
evidence.quote: it is unduly discriminatory to force our constituents to subsidize data center development through astronomical rates and costs
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked PJM to restore a mandatory curtailment rule for new large loads and create a large-load queue so data centers connect only when the grid can serve them.

evidence.title: Letter: Maryland Democrats ask FERC to relieve Maryland ratepayers of out-of-state data center transmission costs (McClain Delaney mirror)
evidence.quote: our constituents should not be forced to pay for transmission projects that they did not cause and from which they will not meaningfully benefit
evidence.what_it_shows: Led the delegation letter backing the Maryland People's Counsel complaint over about $2 billion in PJM transmission costs assigned to Maryland for projects serving out-of-state data centers.

evidence.title: Letter: Warren, Van Hollen and Blumenthal open investigation of Big Tech data centers and utility bills
evidence.quote: To protect consumers, data centers must pay a greater share of the costs upfront for future energy usage and updates to the electrical grid
evidence.what_it_shows: Demanded that Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix explain how much of their data center costs land on households.

evidence.title: Press release: Van Hollen, Whitehouse, Heinrich probe eight AI companies over gas-powered data centers
evidence.quote: combusting gas to generate electricity can have an equivalent carbon intensity to combusting coal
evidence.what_it_shows: Pressed Meta, OpenAI, xAI and others on pollution from twelve planned gas-fired data center projects, adding an environmental critique to his cost concerns.

evidence.title: Press conference (Capital News Service): Van Hollen on the White House ratepayer pledge
evidence.quote: It's not worth the paper it's written on, unless you enact this as well
evidence.what_it_shows: Dismissed the tech companies' voluntary pledge to cover their power costs unless Congress writes the rule into law.

evidence.title: Bill: S. 4727 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a federal study and reporting system for the energy, water and pollution footprint of AI.

evidence.title: Seven Democratic senators' letter to FERC Chair Laura Swett urging action to stop data-center-driven rate hikes
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators urged FERC to reject transmission filings that spread data-center costs across regions, investigate cost allocation and PJM practices, resist queue-jumping for large fossil generators, standardize load forecasting, and prioritize residential ratepayers in the DOE-requested large-load interconnection rulemaking.

evidence.title: Letter from Senators Markey, Blumenthal, Van Hollen and Booker to NARUC President Ann Rendahl on state PUC action against data center cost-shifting
evidence.what_it_shows: Two days after the White House's voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge, the senators called it 'vague and insufficient' and asked state utility regulators' association what guidance it gives PUCs to reject rate filings that make households subsidize data centers.

evidence.what_it_shows: Sixteen lawmakers told EPA to withdraw its May 2026 proposal redefining 'begin actual construction' so data centers and fossil plants can pour foundations and install wiring before New Source Review permits, saying it turns the Clean Air Act's preconstruction safeguards 'on its head.'

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
