After September 2026 warnings from AI researchers he said it was time to pump the brakes and called for mandatory safeguards and a comprehensive testing regime, and he pressed OpenAI to give federal cybersecurity agencies access to its model safety data. The key quotes come through press reports of his posts and letters rather than his own release text.

evidence.quote: time to pump the brakes & take action NOW
evidence.what_it_shows: After a researcher warned AI could kill everyone within a decade, he called on Congress for mandatory safeguards, a comprehensive testing regime and urgent dialogue with China.

evidence.title: PBS News: Van Hollen presses OpenAI CEO Sam Altman after the Hugging Face breach
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked Altman to immediately give federal cybersecurity agencies the information needed to assess the safety and risks of OpenAI's models, treating frontier models as a security risk needing government oversight.

evidence.what_it_shows: Co-signed a letter questioning the Pentagon's adoption of xAI's Grok after its antisemitic output and deepfake pornography problems.

preemption.label: Let states regulate

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Schatz has not taken a stand for or against building data centers. evidence.quote: we've got all this AI data center load coming up ... There are not enough electrons on the grid. What happens when there's not enough of something? The people selling that thing raise the price.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI data center demand as a real driver of higher bills but frames the fix as more solar and clean energy, not slowing data centers.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Schatz is one of the Senate's most active Democrats on specific AI guardrails: labels on AI-made content, parental controls and limits on chatbots for kids, whistleblower protections, bias testing, and safety disclosures from frontier AI companies. He is also drafting an AI excise tax to fund worker retraining. He has not called for licensing or a pause on advanced AI.

evidence.quote: if any digital content is made by AI, it should be labeled so that people are aware and aren't fooled or scammed

members.signature: Senate Commerce Democrat behind the AI Labeling Act, the Kids Off Social Media Act, the CHATBOT Act with Cruz, and the GUARDRAILS Act to protect state AI laws; a leading critic of H200 chip sales to China.

data_centers.summary: Barr, the Republican Senate nominee, celebrates the $100 billion Paducah AI energy hub, wrote a permitting bill to build transmission lines for data centers faster, and campaigns on restarting coal plants to power AI. He is not a cosponsor of the House Ratepayer Protection Act, and no ratepayer conditions from him were found.

evidence.title: WUKY: Barr speaks at the Paducah American Energy Hub announcement with Energy Secretary Wright
evidence.quote: Here in Paducah, we're proving that America's AI future won't just be in Silicon Valley. It will be built in places like Western Kentucky
evidence.what_it_shows: He headlined the announcement of a 1.8 gigawatt hyperscale data center campus and called it historic.

evidence.title: Press release: Reps. Barr and Peters introduce the SPEED and Reliability Act to speed transmission permitting
evidence.quote: AI data centers and advanced manufacturing are at the core of America's economic future, but they can't run without reliable, affordable power.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill cuts red tape for power lines explicitly to serve AI data centers and stay ahead of China.

evidence.title: Campaign press release: Barr unveils plan to revive Kentucky coal jobs and power technologies of the future
evidence.quote: Support AI data centers and advanced manufacturing that depend on affordable, nonstop power
evidence.what_it_shows: His Senate platform lists supporting AI data centers among his legislative priorities and proposes restarting coal plants to meet their demand.

evidence.title: WYMT: Barr promotes coal-powered AI plan during Harlan County visit
evidence.quote: The race for AI is now. It's not 10, 20 years in the future. It's right now
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames data center power demand as a national security race with China that justifies more coal generation.

evidence.title: Forward Kentucky opinion piece: 'Data centers, coming to a town near you, thanks to Andy Barr'
evidence.quote: Central Kentucky is competing on a national stage for the next generation of manufacturing and technology investment
evidence.what_it_shows: Critics note he secured $2 million in federal funding for the Mercer County site planned for a hyperscale data center; the quote is from his own announcement as reproduced in the piece.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Barr talks about AI almost entirely as a race with China that America is at risk of losing, and the AI industry super PAC Leading the Future backs his Senate bid. He voted for the TAKE IT DOWN Act and once cosponsored a commission to study AI child exploitation, but no calls for safety testing, licensing or liability were found.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Barr at House Foreign Affairs hearing 'Winning the AI Arms Race Against the Chinese Communist Party'
evidence.quote: Because of this, we are on the precipice of losing the AI race
evidence.what_it_shows: He tied China's coal plant construction to the AI race and argued for more coal power, an innovation-first framing.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter: Leading the Future super PAC lists Barr's Senate bid among Republicans it supports
evidence.quote: Other Republicans it has supported this cycle include Rep. Andy Barr (R., Ky.) in his Senate bid
evidence.what_it_shows: The AI industry's main pro-innovation super PAC has spent on his behalf.

evidence.title: WYMT: Barr says the U.S. is 'nanoseconds ahead of China' on AI
evidence.quote: We have to have it in order for us to win the race for the future technologies.
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI message is about winning the race, not about managing risks from advanced AI.

evidence.title: House roll call 104 (2025): Yea on S. 146 TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He did support the near-unanimous law against AI sexual deepfakes. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 8005 Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence Expert Commission Act of 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a study commission on AI and child exploitation, a modest step short of new rules.

In 2021 he blasted Big Tech for banning conservatives but proposed no remedy. He did not vote on the KIDS Act. evidence.what_it_shows: He attacked platform content moderation as censorship, but called for national unity around free speech rather than legislation.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Warren's line is that tech companies, not families, must pay for data center power. She opened an investigation of seven hyperscalers over utility bills, won a mandatory federal energy survey of data centers with Sen. Hawley, and proposes an excise tax on data center energy use. She has not backed a moratorium.

evidence.title: Press release: Warren, Van Hollen and Blumenthal open investigation into Big Tech data centers and utility costs
evidence.quote: Through these utility price increases, American families bankroll the electricity costs of trillion-dollar tech companies.
evidence.what_it_shows: Letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix demanding they pay a greater share of grid costs up front.

evidence.title: The Verge: Warren-Hawley letter asks EIA for mandatory annual data center energy reporting
evidence.quote: establish a mandatory annual reporting requirement for data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: A bipartisan push for transparency so the public can check the Ratepayer Protection Pledge.

evidence.title: Press release: Warren, Hawley secure mandatory energy-use reporting requirements for data centers
evidence.quote: Americans deserve to know how much energy data centers are sucking up and what that's doing to their utility bills
evidence.what_it_shows: EIA agreed to a mandatory data center survey in response to her request.

evidence.title: Time op-ed: Why We Need to Tax AI
evidence.quote: By imposing a reasonable excise tax on the energy used by data centers, families could recoup some of the gains of AI, while America continues to stay competitive in the AI race.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants to tax data center energy use while keeping the US competitive, a protect-ratepayers-first stance rather than a pause.

evidence.title: Seven Democratic senators' letter to FERC Chair Laura Swett urging action to stop data-center-driven rate hikes
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators urged FERC to reject transmission filings that spread data-center costs across regions, investigate cost allocation and PJM practices, resist queue-jumping for large fossil generators, standardize load forecasting, and prioritize residential ratepayers in the DOE-requested large-load interconnection rulemaking.

evidence.title: Warren-Hawley bipartisan letter to EIA Administrator Tristan Abbey urging mandatory annual energy-use reporting by data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: A left-right pair asked the Energy Information Administration to require data centers and other large loads to report hourly and peak consumption, prices paid, deposits, demand flexibility, AI vs. cloud energy use, and who pays for triggered grid upgrades, so the public can check compliance with the voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Warren treats AI mainly as a financial-stability and civil-rights problem: she warns the AI investment boom could trigger a 2008-style crash, sponsors an AI Bubble Transparency Act, and cosponsors bills requiring bias testing of automated systems. She has not called for licensing or a pause on advanced AI.

evidence.title: The Verge: Warren says an AI failure could trigger the next financial crisis (Vanderbilt Policy Accelerator remarks)
evidence.quote: the first big stumble will have everyone running for the exits, potentially triggering destabilizing losses in the financial sector and another 2008-style financial crisis.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her AI risk framing is about debt, opaque financing and systemic risk, and she says Congress should step in.

evidence.title: S.4743 AI Bubble Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make companies disclose their AI exposure to investors.

evidence.title: S.2164 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require big companies to test automated decision systems for bias and harm.

evidence.title: S.3308 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports binding anti-discrimination rules and bias testing for AI.

evidence.title: CNBC: Warren questions Pentagon's supply chain risk label on Anthropic
evidence.quote: appears to be retaliation
evidence.what_it_shows: She challenged the Defense Department's blacklisting of a safety-focused AI company, an oversight action rather than a stance on model risk.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Warren is among the most aggressive Big Tech critics in the Senate: she has proposed a new federal regulator for online platforms, backs breaking up Google's ad business and blocking AI cloud monopolies in defense contracts, and wants to tax AI companies.

evidence.title: Press release: Warren, Graham unveil bipartisan Digital Consumer Protection Commission Act
evidence.quote: For too long, giant tech companies have exploited consumers' data, invaded Americans' privacy, threatened our national security, and stomped out competition in our economy
evidence.what_it_shows: Proposed a new commission with power to regulate online platforms alongside the FTC and DOJ.

evidence.title: S.1060 AMERICA Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would break up conflicts of interest in the digital ad market dominated by Google.

evidence.title: S.1775 Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would stop the Pentagon from handing AI and cloud contracts to a few giants without competition.

evidence.title: Press release: Schakowsky and Warren press USTR on whether Big Tech is using the USMCA review to block AI rules
evidence.quote: They are now attempting to use trade deals to preempt even the federal government from effectively regulating AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: She sees Big Tech lobbying on trade as an end run around AI regulation.

evidence.title: Time op-ed: Why We Need to Tax AI
evidence.quote: But it starts by acknowledging: it's time to tax AI and invest in people.
evidence.what_it_shows: Calls for taxing AI companies and data centers and a wealth tax to share AI's gains.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports the major kids online safety bill.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Warren co-led the November 2025 letter urging Senate Democrats to reject any defense bill with a state AI-law moratorium, and she has warned that trade deals could be used to preempt federal and state AI rules.

evidence.title: The Hill: Markey-Warren Dear Colleague letter against an AI moratorium in the NDAA
evidence.quote: Democrats have direct control over whether the AI moratorium is enacted into law. Our message should be simple: Congress should not give Big Tech a multi-year holiday from state oversight
evidence.what_it_shows: She organized against reviving the state AI-law moratorium.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the state AI-law moratorium (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted with 98 others to strip the moratorium from the reconciliation bill. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Press release: Schakowsky and Warren letter to USTR on Big Tech using USMCA to stop AI regulation
evidence.what_it_shows: The letter warns a digital trade strategy could bar federal and state governments from regulating AI.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Warren is a leading chip hawk. She cosponsors the GAIN AI, SAFE Chips, Chip Security and AI OVERWATCH Acts, attacked the approval of Nvidia H200 sales to China as a threat to national security, and tried to get Jensen Huang to testify about Nvidia's China business.

evidence.title: S.3150 GAIN AI Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make chipmakers serve US buyers before shipping advanced chips to China.

evidence.title: S.3374 SAFE Chips Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would lock in export limits so the White House cannot loosen them alone.

evidence.title: S.1705 Chip Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require location verification on advanced chips sold abroad.

evidence.title: S.4456 AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would give Congress a say before advanced AI chips are sold to China.

evidence.title: Meeks-Warren statement on Trump administration approval of advanced AI chip sales to China
evidence.quote: are now more concerned than ever that the Trump administration is undercutting U.S. national security by approving this sale
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposes the H200 license approvals and calls for legislation to block China's access.

evidence.title: CNBC: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declines Warren's invitation to testify on China and export controls
evidence.quote: the American people deserve answers in a public forum
evidence.what_it_shows: She is pressing Nvidia publicly over its China sales.

evidence.title: Warren letter to Lutnick urging Commerce to block Nvidia H20 exports to China
evidence.what_it_shows: Warren pressed Commerce to proceed with restricting H20 chip exports after reports it paused the plan following a Nvidia CEO dinner with Trump.

evidence.title: Schumer and Warren-led Senate Democrats' letter to Lutnick and Rubio urging reconsideration of Middle East chip deals
evidence.what_it_shows: Eight Senate Democrats urged the administration to reconsider the Saudi and UAE AI chip deals absent enforceable protections against diversion to China, and raised Trump-family financial conflicts.

evidence.title: Top Senate Democrats' letter to Lutnick on decision to resume H20 (and AMD MI308) sales to China
evidence.what_it_shows: Five senior Senate Democrats expressed 'grave concern' at reversing the April 2025 H20 ban, said restricting leading-edge chips is the defining barrier to Chinese AI parity, and objected to trading export controls in trade talks without consulting Congress.

evidence.title: Top Senate Democrats' letter to President Trump on the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China
evidence.what_it_shows: Six Senate Democrats urged Trump to reverse the deal letting Nvidia and AMD sell AI chips to China in exchange for a 15 percent cut, arguing it harms national security and that export law bars fees tied to licenses; they demanded answers by Aug. 22.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' statement introducing the GAIN AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Six senators from both parties introduced the standalone GAIN AI Act after the Banks-Warren amendment passed the Senate in the NDAA on Oct. 9, 2025, arguing US customers should not wait behind Chinese tech giants for advanced chips.

evidence.title: Warren, Schumer and colleagues' letter to Lutnick on the decision to allow Nvidia H200 sales to China
evidence.what_it_shows: Seven Senate Democrats said approving H200 exports disregarded DOJ warnings that these chips are building blocks of AI superiority, and questioned Nvidia lobbying and donations preceding the decision.

evidence.title: Banks and Warren joint statement introducing the AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A bipartisan group introduced the Senate AI OVERWATCH Act to codify the ban on exporting the most advanced AI chips to China; Warren said selling advanced chips to China is 'bad in the short run and worse in the long run.'

evidence.title: Warren statement on Commerce easing export controls on AI chips to the UAE (G42/MGX)
evidence.what_it_shows: Warren called the license-free access for G42 a 'corrupt deal' tied to the UAE royal's stake in the Trump family crypto firm and demanded Lutnick and Kessler testify.

evidence.title: Warren letter to BIS Under Secretary Kessler invoking ECRA to compel documents on the Foundry Due Diligence loophole
evidence.what_it_shows: Warren used her statutory authority under the Export Control Reform Act to demand records on gaps created by the AI Diffusion Rule rescission, especially whether BIS is enforcing the worldwide licensing requirement that stopped Huawei from ordering millions of TSMC chips via a shell company.

members.signature: Senate Banking ranking member who leads the Democratic push to keep advanced chips out of China, investigates Big Tech data centers' effect on power bills, and warns of an AI financial bubble.

data_centers.label: No public position found
data_centers.summary: No public position on data centers found as of Sept 2026. His related actions are indirect: a June 2026 letter asking FERC to reject the NextEra-Dominion utility merger to protect New England ratepayers, and a March 2026 refusal to join permitting reform talks while the administration cancels wind and solar projects. His office did not respond to a Dec 2025 question about a national data center moratorium.

evidence.quote: The combination would create the largest electric utility in the United States, concentrating an unprecedented mix of merchant generation, rate-based generation, and transmission assets in the hands of a single company
evidence.what_it_shows: A ratepayer and competition argument about grid power; it does not mention data centers.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: King treats the most powerful AI models as a national security danger and wants binding federal oversight. He co-authored a 2024 framework for oversight of frontier AI hardware, development and deployment, cosponsored a bill creating an AI Safety Review Office to test frontier models before release, and cosponsored the AI LEAD Act letting people sue AI makers. He also backs deepfake and chatbot-adjacent guardrails, and personally uses Claude while warning to be careful with its analysis. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: Sources support strong federal oversight of frontier models (Safety Review Office, CFIUS-style pre-deployment evaluations, data center reporting), but every King source frames it narrowly: safeguards 'would apply to only

evidence.title: Press release: King, Colleagues Unveil Bipartisan Framework to Identify, Minimize Artificial Intelligence Risks
evidence.quote: This AI framework provides critical guidelines for federal oversight of AI technology so that it cannot be misused by bad actors looking to cause harm.
evidence.what_it_shows: With Romney, Reed and Moran he proposed federal oversight of frontier model hardware, development and deployment to guard against biological, chemical, cyber and nuclear threats.

evidence.title: Press release: King, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Preserving American Dominance in AI Act
evidence.quote: This bipartisan Preserving American Dominance in AI Act provides critical guidelines for federal oversight of AI technology so that it cannot be misused by bad actors looking to cause harm.
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill would create an AI Safety Review Office with pre-deployment evaluations of frontier models and reporting by the largest training data centers.

evidence.title: Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 (S.5616, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Cosponsored setting up a government office to check the most powerful AI models for serious dangers before release.

evidence.title: AI LEAD Act (S.2937)
evidence.what_it_shows: Cosponsored letting people hurt by an AI system sue the company that made it, like any other faulty product.

evidence.title: Press release: King warns of AI harming access to veteran benefits in VA Secretary confirmation hearing
evidence.quote: I want to make something very clear. I don't want AI to decide if one of my veterans is entitled to the benefits they have earned, period. Capisce?
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed the VA nominee to keep humans, not AI, in charge of benefit decisions, citing bad experience with AI in insurance.

evidence.title: DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (S.1837)
evidence.what_it_shows: Cosponsored letting victims sue people who make or share AI sexual deepfakes of them; he cosponsored the 2024 version too.

evidence.title: Press release: 'How Feasible is Watermarking of AI-Generated Images?' King asks in Senate Intelligence hearing
evidence.what_it_shows: He questioned an AI scientist about the need for regulation and liability for computer-generated content, per the release summary.

evidence.title: NOTUS: Lawmakers on Capitol Hill Are Learning to Love AI (King uses Claude to prep for hearings)
evidence.quote: You have to be careful with it, particularly when it's talking about analysis. But for data, it's very useful,
evidence.what_it_shows: He is an active user of AI tools, which shows his guardrails stance is not hostility to the technology itself.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

He has also backed banning apps controlled by China. He has not called for breaking up Big Tech or repealing Section 230.

evidence.quote: The bipartisan Kids Off Social Media Act would limit the harmful impacts of social media by establishing reasonable guardrails such as age minimums for new accounts and restrictions on targeting content to children under the age of 17.

evidence.quote: This is somewhat tongue-in-cheek, but it's not entirely: if there are going to be killer robots, I'd rather they be American killer robots and not Chinese killer robots.
evidence.what_it_shows: He said AI needs rules and guardrails but called slowing development an impossible endeavor; China competition trumps caution.

evidence.title: Al Jazeera: Cruz on ABC's The View says AI needs guardrails, cites bill with Klobuchar and Thune
evidence.quote: We've got to put some guardrails on it
evidence.what_it_shows: A shift in tone after the Anthropic researcher warnings; he now endorses some federal rules for catastrophic harm.

evidence.title: Semafor: Cruz posts on X that he is working with Klobuchar and Thune on catastrophic AI risk legislation
evidence.quote: on legislation to address catastrophic risks involving biological or nuclear threats
evidence.what_it_shows: He is co-leading the only Senate AI safety bill seen as viable before 2027; text not yet public.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Cruz introduces the CHATBOT Act with Schatz, Curtis and Schiff
evidence.quote: The rapid development of sophisticated chatbots has left many parents in the dark as powerful AI systems enter children's lives. Congress has an opportunity to put parents back in control.
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports binding rules for AI chatbots that interact with kids: family accounts, parental consent, default protections.

evidence.title: S.4407 CHATBOT Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His own targeted AI guardrail for children; advanced by voice vote at his Aug 5, 2026 Commerce markup.

evidence.title: The Hill: Cruz votes for Hawley's GUARD Act in Judiciary but says it needs revisions
evidence.quote: some revisions
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed the AI companion ban for minors while worrying it could sweep in all chatbots for kids, showing his preference for narrower rules.

evidence.title: Congressional reactions to former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation warning that AI 'could kill us all by the end of the decade'
evidence.what_it_shows: After Coxon's viral Sept 8 post and Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger's '>10% within the next decade' extinction estimate, members of both parties publicly framed AI as an existential risk and called for hearings, a kill-switch law, a superintelligence ban or a pause.

evidence.title: Cruz says AI warning 'scary as hell,' calls for 'substantially more regulation' but opposes slowing U.S. AI versus China
evidence.what_it_shows: The Senate Commerce chairman, long an opponent of AI regulation, said he takes catastrophic AI risk seriously (citing Elon Musk's 10-20% estimate that AI destroys humanity within 10 years) and that his committee may mark up a bill with Thune and Klobuchar on AI-enabled biological and nuclear threats, while warning that shutting down U.S. AI would let China 'catch up in six months and soar ahead.'

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Targeted, not sweeping. He wrote the TAKE IT DOWN Act, sponsors the CHATBOT Act and Kids Off Social Media Act, backs KOSA and ad-tech antitrust (AMERICA Act), and wants to punish government jawboning of platforms. But he opposes a full Section 230 repeal and generally favors deregulation.

evidence.title: S.146 TAKE IT DOWN Act (sponsor; now law)
evidence.what_it_shows: Criminalizes posting real or AI-faked intimate images and forces platforms to remove them within 48 hours.

evidence.title: Senate Commerce hearing on 30 years of Section 230, Cruz opening statement (Tech Policy Press transcript)
evidence.quote: I'm concerned that a full repeal or sunset would lead platforms to engage in worse behavior, to engage in more censorship, to protect themselves from litigation
evidence.what_it_shows: Despite past calls for repeal, he now opposes ending Section 230 and prefers narrower reforms.

evidence.title: Reason: Cruz and Wyden introduce the JAWBONE Act against government pressure on platforms
evidence.quote: the Biden administration weaponized the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to pressure Big Tech into 'canceling' Americans who spoke out against vaccine mandates and election fraud.
evidence.what_it_shows: His Big Tech concern centers on speech and government coercion of platforms, not market power.

evidence.title: S.1060 AMERICA Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would break up conflicts in Google-style digital ad markets, a targeted antitrust measure.

evidence.title: S.278 Kids Off Social Media Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Bans under-13s from social media and limits algorithmic targeting of teens.

evidence.title: IAPP: Cruz reaffirms support for KOSA and promises the Senate will pass it again
evidence.what_it_shows: Reporter's account that he publicly recommitted to the Kids Online Safety Act in May 2026 and scheduled a kids-safety markup.

evidence.title: Cruz and Klobuchar statements marking one year of the TAKE IT DOWN Act as FTC enforcement begins
evidence.what_it_shows: The law's authors said platforms must now remove nonconsensual intimate images and deepfakes within 48 hours, with Cruz saying 'Big Tech can no longer look the other way' and Klobuchar noting platforms can no longer 'turn a blind eye.'

preemption.label: One national rule
preemption.summary: The Senate's leading advocate for one national AI rule. He wrote the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws in the 2025 budget bill, defended it under the Commerce Clause, made preventing a state patchwork a pillar of his AI framework, and stood with Trump at the December 2025 executive order signing.

evidence.title: The Hill: Cruz defends the state AI law moratorium as within Congress's Commerce Clause power
evidence.quote: The Constitution gives Congress the authority to regulate commerce between the states, and AI is quintessentially commerce between the states
evidence.what_it_shows: He rejected states' rights objections and said a patchwork of 50 standards would devastate AI development.

evidence.title: Nextgov: Cruz statement defending the moratorium before the 99-1 vote to strike it
evidence.quote: [The AI moratorium] preserves the rights of states to protect consumers and content creators without giving the Left a backdoor to push their woke social agenda through AI regulation
evidence.what_it_shows: Even as the deal collapsed he defended blocking state AI laws; his Yea on the strike vote came after negotiations failed.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1 (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted to strike his own provision once the compromise fell apart; the 99-1 vote is not evidence he opposes preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Cruz backs Trump's executive order on state AI laws, attends Oval Office signing
evidence.quote: would cede ground to China
evidence.what_it_shows: He said those who disagreed with the order to challenge state AI laws would cede ground to China and stood beside Trump at the signing.

evidence.title: Covington summary: Cruz AI Policy Framework pillar on preventing a state patchwork
evidence.quote: Prevent a Patchwork of Burdensome AI Regulation
evidence.what_it_shows: One of the five pillars of his framework calls on Congress to enact federal standards that prevent burdensome state AI regulation.

evidence.title: S.2750 SANDBOX Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: The model for the regulatory sandbox in the White House's March 2026 national AI framework that calls for broad preemption.

evidence.title: Sen. Ted Cruz AI Policy Framework announcement (five pillars incl. a national standard) with SANDBOX Act introduction
evidence.what_it_shows: Cruz released a light-touch AI framework and said 'executive orders alone aren't sufficient,' introducing the SANDBOX Act as its first bill; the framework's pillars include preempting the state 'patchwork.'

china_chips.label: Leans sell more
china_chips.summary: Leans toward selling American AI abroad. As Commerce chairman he attacked Biden's AI diffusion rule on chips and model weights and said allies should buy American; his framework opposes excessive foreign regulation. No verified position found on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales to China specifically.

evidence.title: Senate Commerce hearing 'Winning the AI Race', Cruz opening statement (Tech Policy Press transcript)
evidence.quote: Biden's misguided midnight AI diffusion rule on chips and model weights would've crippled American tech companies ability to sell AI to the world.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed the Biden export framework and said he lobbied for months to kill it, favoring wider sales of US AI technology.

evidence.title: Covington summary of Cruz AI Policy Framework: counter excessive foreign regulation
evidence.what_it_shows: His framework pairs preemption of state laws with pushing back on foreign rules that limit American AI companies, a diffusion-first stance.

members.signature: Senate Commerce chairman and architect of the failed 2025 state AI law moratorium and the SANDBOX Act; Stargate booster who blames Chinese misinformation for data center backlash; author of the TAKE IT DOWN and CHATBOT Acts; now drafting a catastrophic-risk bill with Thune and Klobuchar.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Weber wants to build the power for AI while shielding household electric bills. He also cosponsors the Ratepayer Protection Act, which pushes data centers to pay their own grid costs.

evidence.title: Opening statement of Chairman Randy Weber at Science Committee hearing on subsurface science and American energy and mineral dominance
evidence.quote: Energy demand is skyrocketing as we are not only onshoring manufacturing, but also electrifying our lives and working to stay ahead of the Chinese Communist Party in the artificial intelligence race.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI-driven demand as a reason to speed up new baseload energy like geothermal, a build-more framing.

evidence.title: H.R. 9340, Ratepayer Protection Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the bipartisan E&C bill (cleared committee 52-0) that has state regulators consider making data centers pay their own way instead of shifting costs to families.

evidence.title: Legis1 preview: House Panel Examines U.S. Leadership in Advanced Nuclear Reactors
evidence.what_it_shows: Identifies Weber as chairman of the Energy Subcommittee holding the hearing and notes surging AI and data center electricity demand is drawing billions into advanced nuclear.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Weber shows concern about AI chatbots and kids but has not called for specific new AI rules. At a November 2025 hearing he pressed experts on whether anyone monitors chatbot replies to children or suicidal users and whether chatbots should be catalogued, and he called AI grading AI a fox guarding the henhouse. At the same time he frames energy policy around beating China in the AI race.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: House E&C Oversight hearing on the risks and benefits of AI chatbots (Weber questioning)
evidence.quote: So there's nobody watching this process? I'm focusing on kids, of course, first and foremost, or somebody who's suicidal, anybody that would need help. There's really nobody watching those kinds of replies to see, to categorize them, catalog them, or to act on them, is that accurate?
evidence.what_it_shows: He questioned whether anyone oversees chatbot responses to vulnerable users, asked if someone should be tasked with cataloguing all chatbots, and called using an LLM to judge LLM outputs a fox guarding the henhouse.

evidence.title: House roll call 104 (2025): Yea on S. 146, TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted for the AI deepfake takedown law. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.what_it_shows: Cosponsored the House deepfake intimate-image bill in the last Congress.

evidence.quote: working to stay ahead of the Chinese Communist Party in the artificial intelligence race
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows the beat-China framing that sits alongside his kids-and-chatbots concerns.

tech_regulation.summary: Weber consistently backs targeted rules for kids and consumers online. He cosponsors the SCREEN Act requiring age checks on adult sites, the Foreign Robocall Elimination Act and the Connected Vehicle Security Act; he cosponsored the Kids Online Safety Act, Sammy's Law and TAKE IT DOWN in the last Congress; and he voted for TAKE IT DOWN and the KIDS Act.

evidence.what_it_shows: Voted for the kids online safety package while 32 Republicans voted no. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: House roll call 104 (2025): Yea on S. 146, TAKE IT DOWN Act (passed 409-2)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted for the deepfake and nonconsensual image takedown law. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a crackdown on scam robocalls from abroad.

evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning connected-car technology from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: H.R. 7891 (118th), Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Cosponsored the House KOSA, along with Sammy's Law, in the last Congress.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails

evidence.title: The Hill: Gallego letter to Thune and Schumer urging a bipartisan Senate Select Committee on AI
evidence.quote: Congress does not need to resolve every disagreement among experts about timelines or probabilities to recognize that both the upside and the downside of this technology warrant an urgent and comprehensive response
evidence.what_it_shows: After an Anthropic researcher's extinction warning, he asked for a dedicated Senate committee on AI starting next Congress, treating advanced AI as a serious risk needing a full response.

evidence.title: DefenseScoop: Gallego letter to Hegseth questioning the Pentagon's rushed rewrite of autonomous weapons policy
evidence.quote: Any update that significantly reduces safeguards and disrupts rigorous reviews risks friendly fire and civilian harm incidents affecting U.S. servicemembers, partner or allied militaries, or host nation civilians.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants existing safety reviews on autonomous and AI-enabled weapons kept, not loosened on a 90-day timeline.

evidence.title: S.3062 GUARD Act (cosponsored 2025-10-29)

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Treats rogue frontier AI as a real catastrophic danger. He wrote the bipartisan AI Kill Switch Act to force the biggest AI developers to keep a working shutdown ability and to let the government order a slowdown or shutdown, has called for mandatory disclosure of safety test results, and earlier wrote the law keeping humans in charge of nuclear launches. He says most everyday AI uses need no government attention.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 9917 AI Kill Switch Act

evidence.title: Op-ed in Fox News: AI is already too powerful, we need a kill switch before disaster strikes

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 6152, Foreign Robocall Elimination Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a specific rule against scam robocalls entering the United States.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No statement found on preempting state AI laws. He voted for the House version of H.R. 1 in May 2025, which contained the 10-year state AI moratorium, but that was a vote on the whole tax and spending package and he has not spoken about the AI provision.

evidence.title: House passage of H.R. 1 (reconciliation bill including the state AI moratorium), May 22, 2025: Bost voted Yea
evidence.what_it_shows: A package vote that included the moratorium; nearly all Republicans voted yes for many reasons, so it is weak evidence of his view on preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China. Searches for Bost with chips, Nvidia, export controls and TikTok returned only unrelated items.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Mixed by design. Moulton rejects a data center moratorium and says blocking data centers would cede AI leadership to China, but he also wants 'tight restrictions' so data centers do not raise electricity bills or drain water, and he signed two House Democratic letters pressing regulators and industry on ratepayer costs.

evidence.title: Tufts Daily interview: Moulton asked whether Congress should pause data center construction
evidence.quote: we can’t have data centers coming in and just raising everybody’s electricity bills and taking everybody’s water and everything else. But to basically cede leadership on AI to China would be incredibly dangerous
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked about a Sanders-style moratorium, he refused to pause construction but said data centers must not push costs onto households.

evidence.title: Tufts Daily interview: Moulton on AI companies and communities
evidence.quote: That doesn’t mean that we should give free reign to the AI companies. I think there should be tight restrictions on what they’re able to do in our communities.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pairs support for AI growth with a call for tight local restrictions on AI companies.

evidence.title: Letter from 20 House Democrats led by Rep. Kevin Mullin to FERC, Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs (Moulton co-signed)
evidence.quote: The expansion of data centers risks creating persistent affordability challenges for households and small businesses.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined colleagues asking regulators, utilities and the industry how grid upgrade costs will be kept off household bills.

evidence.title: New Democrat Coalition letter to House appropriators requesting a DOE National Strategic Data Center Plan (Moulton signed)
evidence.quote: Rapidly increasing demand for data centers, driven by cloud computing and AI, is vital for America's economy and competitiveness. However, this expansion strains electricity grids, land, water, and community infrastructure
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames data centers as vital but calls for managed growth and a national plan covering grid, water and consumer cost impacts.

evidence.title: House roll call 356 (Dec 18 2025): H.R.4776 SPEED Act permitting reform, Moulton voted Nay
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against the Republican permitting bill that supporters said would speed energy and data center projects. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Moulton says AI is here to stay and America should lead it, but he wants protections around AI tools, has backed targeted rules (no AI control of nuclear launches, bans on AI election lies) and says government must be ready to help workers displaced by AI. He does not talk about AI as an existential danger.

evidence.title: WCVB debate coverage: Moulton attacks Markey's AI answer in the final Senate primary debate
evidence.quote: if you don't even know what you're using on your phone or your iPad, like this is why we need a new generation of leaders to regulate these technologies
evidence.what_it_shows: He framed regulating AI as necessary and cast himself as the generation that should write the rules.

evidence.title: New Bedford Light debate coverage: Moulton on using AI tools
evidence.quote: These are tools that can help, but they’re also tools that need protections
evidence.what_it_shows: He says he uses AI himself and supports protections around it.

evidence.title: Tufts Daily interview: Moulton on AI job displacement
evidence.quote: we need to be prepared for massive disruptions in our economy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He agrees with Rep. Ro Khanna that government should be ready to help workers, such as paralegals, who lose jobs to AI.

evidence.title: 118th H.R.2894 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a rule that a human, not an AI, must make any nuclear launch decision.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.4894 Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning AI-made lies about voting in the two months before a federal election.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.2385 CREATE AI Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a public computing resource so researchers can build AI, a pro-innovation measure.

evidence.title: Press release: Moulton joins Hurd, Kelly resolution to create a national AI strategy
evidence.quote: I'd rather the future be defined by our values, not theirs.
evidence.what_it_shows: Early framing of AI as a race with China and Russia that America must lead.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Moulton wants more accountability for big tech companies and has cosponsored a long list of targeted bills: the Kids Online Safety Act, kids privacy updates, Sammy's Law, hidden-camera disclosure for smart devices, reproductive data privacy and the TikTok divestiture. He is a founding member of the Congressional Antitrust Caucus but has not called for break-ups or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Brookline.News joint interview: Moulton on surveillance technology and regulating AI
evidence.quote: It just went too far in saying, ‘Hey, this is just a laissez-faire world where there’s no accountability.’
evidence.what_it_shows: He criticized the hands-off 1996 Telecommunications Act and said Congress left too little accountability for major technology companies.

evidence.title: 118th H.R.7891 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed the House version of KOSA requiring apps to protect kids from harmful content and addictive design.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.2657 Sammy's Law (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make big social media sites let parents use safety apps to monitor kids' accounts.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.859 Informing Consumers about Smart Devices Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require disclosure when a smart device contains a hidden camera or microphone.

evidence.title: House roll call 86 (Mar 13 2024): H.R.7521 TikTok divestiture bill, Moulton voted Yea (he was also a cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to force TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a ban. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Press release: Moulton, Congressional Antitrust Caucus lead letter to FTC on corporate consolidation
evidence.what_it_shows: As a founding member of the Congressional Antitrust Caucus he asked the FTC to review how consolidation hurts workers, consumers and small businesses.

preemption.label: Leans states
preemption.summary: In a July 2026 interview Moulton said states should be allowed to adopt their own AI rules while Congress writes broader federal standards. He did not sign the two Nov and Dec 2025 House Democratic letters opposing a state AI law moratorium, and no direct quote on preemption was found.

evidence.title: Brookline.News joint interview: Moulton on state versus federal AI regulation (reporter's summary)
evidence.quote: Moulton said he supports allowing states to adopt their own AI regulations while Congress develops broader federal standards.
evidence.what_it_shows: A reporter's paraphrase, not his own words, but it places him against blocking state AI laws before federal rules exist.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Moulton sits on the House China Select Committee and has cosponsored bills to block the most powerful chips from going to China and to remove DeepSeek from government devices, and he says ceding AI leadership to China would be dangerous. No statement on the Nvidia H20 or H200 sales was found.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.5022 No Advanced Chips for the CCP Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would block the most powerful AI chips from being sold to China.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.1121 No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would remove the Chinese AI app DeepSeek from federal devices.

evidence.title: Tufts Daily interview: Moulton on AI competition with China
evidence.quote: to basically cede leadership on AI to China would be incredibly dangerous to the United States of America
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats the AI race with China as a national security matter.

members.signature: Lost the Sept 1 2026 Senate primary to Markey after making generational leadership on AI regulation a campaign theme; a New Democrat who says America must lead on AI but wants tight restrictions on data centers and AI companies.

quote.text: With all due respect, Senator, if you don't even know what you're using on your phone or your iPad, like this is why we need a new generation of leaders to regulate these technologies

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Cosponsors two bills to shield households from data center power costs and keep siting decisions local, but no public statement from him on Michigan's data center fights was found. He also voted for House energy bills that critics tie to faster grid buildout.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.9340 Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs keeping regular customers' electric bills from rising to pay for data center power needs.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (Barrett)
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants local towns, not federal agencies, to decide whether data centers get built.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Treats AI mainly as a national security race with China rather than a safety problem, but he cosponsored protections for AI company whistleblowers and an NSA playbook for securing frontier models, and a pro-safeguards PAC ran ads praising his record on AI accountability. No statement found on frontier model risk, licensing or liability. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: Every AI item is adversary-facing: export controls on AI systems (ENFORCE Act), restricting Chinese models used by U.S. companies, chip controls. The PFA praise cites only China-focused bills (Chip Security Act, GAIN AI

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.3460 AI Whistleblower Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs protecting AI company workers who report safety problems.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.3919 Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants the NSA to write a playbook for protecting frontier AI systems from theft by rivals.

evidence.title: Press release: Moolenaar introduces the ENFORCE Act to let Commerce control exports of AI systems
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is a foundational technology of the future with the potential to reshape our economy, our way of life, and our national security
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI framing is about keeping American models out of adversaries' hands rather than domestic safety rules.

evidence.title: Public First Action (Anthropic-backed) names Moolenaar among 12 Republicans in its $15 million Conservative AI Consensus ad campaign
evidence.quote: 12 Republican members of Congress who are leading on AI security and accountability
evidence.what_it_shows: A pro-safeguards AI PAC network is spending to praise his record rather than attack it.

evidence.title: Letters: Moolenaar and Garbarino open probe of Airbnb and Anysphere over use of Chinese AI models
evidence.quote: Airbnb and Anysphere's decisions to build their products on Chinese Communist AI models threaten critical infrastructure Americans use every day
evidence.what_it_shows: He sees Chinese open-weight models as a security and data risk and is using committee oversight on U.S. companies that adopt them.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Targeted, national security rules: helped force TikTok's split from ByteDance and keeps pressing on the algorithm deal, wrote the House ban on Chinese connected cars, and is investigating U.S. companies that build on Chinese AI models. Not a general Big Tech antitrust or Section 230 critic.

evidence.title: Op-ed: Social Media Legislation Protects National Security (on the TikTok divestiture law)
evidence.quote: TikTok is another element of the CCP's nefarious activities in the United States.
evidence.what_it_shows: He championed the law forcing ByteDance to sell TikTok or face a U.S. ban.

evidence.title: Press release: TikTok breaks commitment to answer questions on its algorithm's ties to China
evidence.quote: TikTok has backed out of its commitment to appear at the Committee's September roundtable to answer questions on China's influence over TikTok's algorithm and its access to Americans' data.
evidence.what_it_shows: He is still using committee oversight to police the TikTok deal, including child safety and data access.

evidence.title: Press release: Questions need to be answered on TikTok deal
evidence.quote: The Chinese Communist Party cannot be allowed to weaponize an app to divide and weaken our country.
evidence.what_it_shows: He demanded assurances that China has no influence over the algorithm in the ByteDance-licensed deal.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R.8730 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Wrote the House bill banning connected cars and parts from China, Russia, Iran and North Korea.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.7521 Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Cosponsored the TikTok divestiture law itself.

preemption.label: Mixed or conditional
preemption.summary: Mixed and thin. He voted for the House version of H.R. 1 with its 10-year pause on state AI laws, but a pro-safeguards PAC later credited him with helping keep AI preemption out of the defense bill, and he cosponsors a bill barring federal override of local data center zoning. No statement from him on preemption was found.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on House roll call 145, passage of H.R. 1 including the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the reconciliation bill while it still contained the state AI-law moratorium; an omnibus vote, so a weak signal. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Public First Action ad campaign credits Moolenaar and 11 others with keeping AI preemption out of the NDAA
evidence.quote: as well as work to keep federal preemption of state AI laws out of the National Defense Authorization Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A PAC's characterization, not his own words, that he resisted the late-2025 push to add preemption to the defense bill.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs blocking federal agencies from overriding local zoning on data centers, a local-control instinct.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: The House's leading export-control hawk on AI chips. Objected to resuming Nvidia H20 sales, told Commerce that approving H200 sales risks undercutting the U.S. lead, and demanded enforcement even if it blocks H200 exports entirely. Sponsors the GAIN AI Act and the SCALE Act, and cosponsors the Chip Security Act, AI OVERWATCH Act and Remote Access Security Act.

evidence.title: Letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick objecting to resumed Nvidia H20 sales to China
evidence.quote: The Commerce Department made the right call in banning the H20. Now it must hold the line
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed the July 2025 reversal allowing H20 exports and proposed a floating technical benchmark pegged just above China's own chips.

evidence.title: Letter to Lutnick on Nvidia H200 chips: U.S. winning the AI race against a weak Chinese chip sector
evidence.quote: Approving the sale of cutting-edge chips to Chinese companies risks undercutting the extraordinary strategic advantage that President Trump achieved in his first term
evidence.what_it_shows: He pushed back on the December 2025 H200 decision and requested a Commerce briefing.

evidence.title: Letter to Lutnick: Nvidia products used by DeepSeek and the People's Liberation Army
evidence.quote: even if such enforcement effectively prevents H200 exports to the PRC altogether
evidence.what_it_shows: He said rigorous enforcement of the H200 military-use certification is essential even if it ends H200 exports to China, and asked for tighter limits on Chinese AI models.

evidence.title: Press release: Moolenaar introduces SCALE Act to create objective chip export standards
evidence.quote: ensuring American companies never sell the best chips in the world to China
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would cap exports at 110 percent of what China can already make at scale, with a presumption of denial above a share threshold.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R.5885 GAIN AI Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require chipmakers to offer advanced AI chips to American buyers before selling to China.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R.8306 SCALE Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill tightening rules on advanced chip sales to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.3447 Chip Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs location verification on exported AI chips to catch smuggling.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.6875 AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants Congress to be able to block advanced AI chip sales to China before they happen.

evidence.title: Press release: Moolenaar backs Stop Stealing Our Chips Act (whistleblower rewards for chip smuggling)
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is the defining technology of the new Cold War. Whether the U.S. or China wins this race will be determined in large part by who has more and better chips.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames chip export enforcement as the decisive front in the AI race with China.

evidence.title: Press release: House passes Remote Access Security Act closing the cloud loophole
evidence.quote: The CCP's AI ambitions are being fueled by its access to American chips housed in data centers located outside of China
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants export controls to cover remote cloud access to U.S. chips, not just physical shipments.

evidence.title: Letter to Commerce's Kessler urging enforcement of the chip due-diligence rule after the Huawei/Sophgo case (Yahoo News)
evidence.quote: to close the loophole that Huawei and Sophgo exploited
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed the Trump administration to enforce a Biden-era rule requiring chipmakers to scrutinize orders that may be fronts for sanctioned Chinese firms.

evidence.title: House Select Committee on the CCP report 'DeepSeek Unmasked' and letter to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
evidence.what_it_shows: Bipartisan committee report found DeepSeek funnels US data to China, censors output, and was built on tens of thousands of Nvidia chips possibly obtained around export controls; leaders sent Nvidia a letter demanding sales data for China and Southeast Asia.

evidence.title: Moolenaar statement: DOJ chip-smuggling indictment shows urgent need for the Chip Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: After DOJ indicted three Chinese nationals for routing chips through Thailand and Malaysia to China, Moolenaar called for passing the Chip Security Act's location-verification mandate, noting 30 bipartisan cosponsors.

evidence.title: Moolenaar and Mast bipartisan letter to Rubio and Lutnick supporting stronger allied export controls on chipmaking tools
evidence.what_it_shows: Eight House members from both parties urged countrywide (not entity-specific) controls on chokepoint semiconductor manufacturing equipment and closer work with the Netherlands and other allies, citing doubling Dutch lithography sales to China.

evidence.title: House Select Committee report 'Buy What It Can, Steal What It Must: China's Campaign to Acquire Frontier AI Capabilities'
evidence.what_it_shows: Committee investigation found China remains the largest buyer of chipmaking equipment, lawfully buys large volumes of AI chips, runs sophisticated smuggling networks, and distills US frontier models at industrial scale; it recommends passing the MATCH Act (H.R.8170) and AI OVERWATCH Act (H.R.6875).

evidence.title: Moolenaar statement backing House Foreign Affairs passage of export-control bills (MATCH Act, Stop Stealing Our Chips Act, Deterring American AI Model Theft Act)
evidence.what_it_shows: Moolenaar praised the committee's bipartisan approval of bills restricting chipmaking-equipment sales, rewarding chip-smuggling whistleblowers, and sanctioning AI model theft.

evidence.title: Moolenaar and Garbarino letters to Airbnb and Anysphere launching investigation into use of Chinese AI models
evidence.what_it_shows: The chairs of the China Select Committee and Homeland Security opened a joint probe into US companies' use of PRC-developed models (DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot, MiniMax), citing distillation of US frontier models and cybersecurity risk.

evidence.title: Moolenaar and Whitesides letter to Lutnick urging Commerce not to allow US purchases of Chinese memory chips
evidence.what_it_shows: A bipartisan pair urged Commerce to hold firm against letting Apple and other US firms buy DRAM from Chinese, military-linked memory makers despite the AI-driven memory shortage, and to expand export controls on Chinese memory producers.

members.signature: Chairman of the House China Select Committee and the House's most active voice for tightening AI chip export controls (GAIN AI Act, SCALE Act, opposition to Nvidia H20 and H200 sales); also cosponsors ratepayer and local-control data center bills.

quote.text: Artificial intelligence is the defining technology of the new Cold War. Whether the U.S. or China wins this race will be determined in large part by who has more and better chips.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Dingell has fought for a transparent process and ratepayer protection on the Saline Township Stargate project and the University of Michigan and Los Alamos data center in Ypsilanti Township. She says the Saline project could be an economic boon if approved, but only with no rate increases and real public hearings, and she has called U-M's handling of Ypsilanti Township unacceptable.

evidence.title: WEMU: Lawmakers push back against DTE's request to fast-track Saline Township data center (Dingell joined letter to Michigan PSC)
evidence.quote: The community deserves and must have a seat at the table, so you need a transparent process.
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed DTE skipping public hearings and, per the report, said approval should require that ratepayers see no increases; she also called the project an economic boon if approved.

evidence.title: Press release: Dingell statement on Los Alamos project site selection (U-M picks Ypsilanti Township)
evidence.quote: It is deeply disturbing that the University of Michigan has chosen this site for the Los Alamos data center project despite the clear opposition of Ypsilanti Township residents and local leaders
evidence.what_it_shows: She sided with residents against siting the $1.2 billion computing center over local opposition and noted the township would see little tax benefit.

evidence.title: Letter to U-M President Grasso demanding a real two-way town hall on the Ypsilanti Township data center (press release with letter text)
evidence.quote: Key concerns include water use, such as how much water the facility will require, where it would come from, and what safeguards are in place to protect long-term regional supply.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her concerns are water, grid strain, who pays, emissions and local services; she wants open scrutiny before the project proceeds.

evidence.title: Letters from 20 House Democrats led by Rep. Kevin Mullin to FERC, Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs (Dingell co-signed)
evidence.quote: These staggering figures underscore the urgent need to protect ratepayers, both in the region served by PJM and nationwide.
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a push to keep grid upgrade costs for data centers off household bills and to make utility contracts transparent.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7977 (Casten bill to keep data center grid costs off household electric bills; original cosponsor, confirmed in govinfo bill status)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs making data centers pay their own energy costs.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Dingell supports targeted AI guardrails: transparency rules for chatbots, a halt to Meta's AI companion bots for minors, bans on AI price discrimination and wage fixing, and laws against sexual deepfakes. She has described AI's risks in terms of privacy, bias, deepfakes and foreign adversaries, not existential danger, and has not called for licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Hearing: Dingell remarks at House Energy and Commerce full committee hearing on AI and American global competitiveness (Tech Policy Press transcript)
evidence.quote: we cannot afford to let America's data and personal information be weaponized by China or other adversaries or allow AI to spread unchecked through deep fakes, robocalls and deceptive ads
evidence.what_it_shows: She lists data privacy, bias, deepfakes and adversary exploitation as the AI dangers she wants addressed, pointing to her TAKE IT DOWN Act work.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7985 CHATBOT Act (transparency rules for AI chatbot companies)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports rules to keep people from being harmed by AI chatbots.

evidence.title: Castor-led letter from six Energy and Commerce Democrats to Mark Zuckerberg urging Meta to halt AI companion bots for users under 18 (Dingell signed)
evidence.quote: These inappropriate AI systems pose significant safety risks to children and teenagers who use Meta's platforms.
evidence.what_it_shows: She pressed a major AI deployer to pull a product from minors over safety concerns.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4640 Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning companies from using AI and personal data to set different prices or wages for different people.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3562 DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (civil suits over AI sexual deepfakes)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports liability for makers and sharers of nonconsensual AI sexual images.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 633 TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed the now-law crackdown on AI-faked intimate images.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Dingell has a long list of targeted tech rules: she sponsored a bill making carmakers cut off abusers' remote access to a survivor's car, and cosponsored the TAKE IT DOWN Act, a bill making social media companies fight fentanyl sales, and a ban on Chinese-linked connected cars. She also pressed Meta on AI companion bots for kids. No calls for break-ups or Section 230 repeal were found in this pass.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 2110 Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own bill puts a duty on carmakers to protect domestic violence survivors from connected-car tracking.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6259 No Fentanyl on Social Media Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports new duties on platforms to report and remove drug sales.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8730 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected-car tech from China and other adversaries.

evidence.title: Castor-led letter to Meta urging a halt to AI companion bots for minors (Dingell signed)
evidence.what_it_shows: Direct pressure on a Big Tech platform over child safety.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Dingell signed the November 2025 letter from 81 House Democrats opposing any state AI-law moratorium in the NDAA and the planned executive order to preempt state AI laws. She also voted against H.R. 1 when it carried the 10-year moratorium.

evidence.title: Letter: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats to Johnson, Thune, Jeffries and Schumer opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order (Dingell is a signer)
evidence.quote: We write to express our strong opposition to any effort in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would reintroduce a sweeping moratorium on the ability of states and local governments to enforce their own artificial intelligence (AI) laws
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a direct statement against federal preemption of state AI laws, whether by law, executive order or by conditioning BEAD funds.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill), House passage, which at the time contained the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: A vote against the whole package, weak on its own, but consistent with her letter. Recorded vote: Nay.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Dingell leans hawkish on Chinese AI: she cosponsored the bill to remove DeepSeek from government devices and has warned about China weaponizing Americans' data. No statement on Nvidia chip export controls or H20/H200 sales was found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 1121 No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning the Chinese AI app from federal devices.

evidence.title: Hearing: Dingell remarks at Energy and Commerce AI hearing on foreign adversaries and U.S. data (Tech Policy Press transcript)

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Babin wants data centers built faster. As Science Committee chairman he held a hearing on permitting delays as the main barrier to AI infrastructure, and in September 2026 he opened a probe into whether foreign money is behind local opposition to data centers. His committee also blocked a Democratic amendment on data centers' community impacts.

evidence.quote: Permitting delays for power generation and transmission, environmental review bottlenecks, and regulatory uncertainty slow the construction and expansion of critical infrastructure.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames data centers as the physical backbone of winning the AI race with China and permitting reform as the fix.

evidence.title: E&E News: House Science Committee takes on data center permitting
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence will define the next era of economic and national security leadership, but it cannot advance without reliable, abundant energy

evidence.quote: Advancing AI capabilities and ensuring energy resilience are essential to U.S. national security and economic competitiveness
evidence.what_it_shows: He sent letters to NSF, Sierra Club, 350.org, Indivisible and Oil Change International seeking documents on foreign funding of organized opposition to data centers.

evidence.title: Press release: Chairman Babin praises administration's strategy for American AI leadership

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Protect ratepayers and communities first. Beyer urged Fairfax County to reject a data center substation in a residential area, co-signed letters pressing FERC, utilities and the industry to keep grid costs off household bills, cosponsors the main cost-shifting bills, and wrote the AI Environmental Impacts Act to force data centers to report energy and water use. He says he recognizes the infrastructure supports the region's economy, so he is not seeking a moratorium.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Strict rules now. Beyer says the risks from frontier AI models are real, calls the administration's approach a dangerous 'wild west', and wants Congress to set comprehensive, binding standards for model evaluation and deployment. His own bills are mostly transparency and human-control measures (foundation model disclosure, human authority over autonomous weapons, a voluntary AI flaw-reporting system), so the score reflects his rhetoric and goals more than enacted mandates.

Beyer wrote the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal Trump's December 2025 executive order against state AI laws, signed the Matsui and Clarke letters against a moratorium, and says the White House wants to kill state AI laws without setting even minimal federal guardrails. He supports a federal framework eventually but insists states keep their power until Congress acts.
