evidence.title: The Hill: Public anger over AI boom triggers GOP midterm worries
evidence.quote: There's this irrational response. 'Data centers are bad.' Are they really? If they're off-the-grid, they have power generation, they're silent, they capture their own water and use it for cooling, that's bad?
evidence.what_it_shows: He defends data centers and calls the backlash irrational, but ties his defense to projects that are off the grid with their own power and water.

evidence.title: The Hill: Tillis on wanting a sustainable data center base in North Carolina
evidence.quote: I hope we just get reasonable so we can have a good, sustainable commercial base of data centers in and around North Carolina.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants more data centers built in and around his state and says Republicans need to educate the public.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Tillis backs specific AI guardrails: a federal right to stop AI copies of a person's voice or face, tracking of AI security incidents, and a role for Congress in limiting military AI that could enable mass surveillance. He also cosponsored a bill letting financial firms test AI with fewer rules, so his record is targeted rather than sweeping.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: NO FAKES Act of 2025 (S.1367)
evidence.what_it_shows: Gives everyone the legal right to stop AI copies of their voice or face from being used without permission.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: NO FAKES Act of 2026 (S.4591)
evidence.what_it_shows: Renewed his support for a federal digital-replica right against unauthorized AI fakes.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Secure A.I. Act of 2024 (S.4230, with Sen. Warner)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would set up a system for tracking and reporting security problems and attacks on AI systems.

evidence.title: Axios: Congress rips Pentagon over Anthropic fight
evidence.quote: It's fair to say that Congress needs to weigh in if they have a tool that could actually result in mass surveillance,
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants Congress, not just the Pentagon and an AI company, to set limits on military AI that could enable mass surveillance, and called the public fight sophomoric.

evidence.title: IPWatchdog: Copyright Office oversight hearing chaired by Tillis
evidence.quote: While there's no question that the U.S. is in an AI race with China, the U.S. should not be in a race to the bottom.
evidence.what_it_shows: He rejects sacrificing creators' copyright protections in the name of winning the AI race.

evidence.title: Press release: Tillis, Hickenlooper urge action on AI cyber threats
evidence.quote: urging the White House to provide updates on efforts to reduce artificial intelligence's (AI) potential threat to the nation's cyber infrastructure
evidence.what_it_shows: Early bipartisan letter treating AI as a cybersecurity threat that the government must actively manage.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act (S.2528)
evidence.what_it_shows: Cuts the other way: would let banks and financial firms try out AI tools in special zones with fewer regulations.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Tillis repeatedly cosponsors targeted rules on tech platforms: kids' online safety, child abuse material, counterfeit goods and China-linked apps like TikTok. He has not pushed break-ups or a full repeal of Section 230.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748)
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires apps and platforms to build in safety tools and protect kids under 17; he also cosponsored the 2024 version.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (S.1829)
evidence.what_it_shows: Makes platforms do more to remove child sexual abuse material and lets victims sue them.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: EARN IT Act of 2023 (S.1207)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would strip platforms' Section 230 shield when they let child abuse material spread.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: RESTRICT Act (S.686)
evidence.what_it_shows: Lets the government review and block apps and tech from rival countries like China; the bill behind the TikTok debate.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: SHOP SAFE Act of 2023 (S.2934)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make online marketplaces liable for counterfeit goods unless they vet sellers carefully.

preemption.label: Mixed or conditional
preemption.summary: Tillis cast the only vote to keep the 2025 moratorium on state AI laws, but Time reported that a source said the 4 a.m. vote may have been a mistake, and he has not explained it publicly. No other statement on preempting state AI laws was found. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: The only evidence is a single post-4 a.m. vote that Time's source says may have been a mistake; the item itself calls it weak evidence. That is too thin to assign 'Leans national rule'.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium (Tillis voted Nay)
evidence.what_it_shows: He was the only senator, out of 100, who voted to keep the 10-year freeze on state AI laws in the budget bill. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: Time: Senators reject 10-year ban on state-level AI regulation
evidence.quote: Republican Senator Thom Tillis was the only lawmaker who voted to keep the moratorium in the bill
evidence.what_it_shows: Time added that the vote happened after 4 a.m. and that a person with knowledge of the matter said it may have been a mistake, so the vote is weak evidence of his view.

china_chips.label: Leans sell more
china_chips.summary: Mixed. Tillis cosponsors the Chip Security Act to track advanced chips so they cannot be smuggled to China, but he also signed a letter to scrap the Biden AI export rule and said he had no real problem letting Nvidia sell some chips to China if the U.S. knows where they end up. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: Both direct sources lean toward selling more: he told CNBC he has no real problem giving China some chips (with tracking conditions), and he signed the letter asking Commerce to withdraw the AI Diffusion Rule for a light

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Chip Security Act (S.1705)
evidence.what_it_shows: Advanced chips sold overseas would need a built-in way to prove where they are so they cannot be diverted to China.

evidence.title: CNBC: Trump's blessing of Nvidia AI chip sales to China gets a chilly reception from GOP
evidence.quote: I don't have a real problem with providing them some [chips],
evidence.what_it_shows: Unlike many GOP hawks, he accepted letting Nvidia sell some AI chips to China, adding that the U.S. has to know where the chips are and how they are used.

evidence.title: PYMNTS/CPI: Republican senators urge reversal of Biden's AI export controls (Ricketts-led letter to Lutnick)
evidence.quote: Signatories of the letter include Senators Pete Ricketts, Thom Tillis, Markwayne Mullin, Ted Budd, Roger Wicker, Eric Schmitt, and Tommy Tuberville.
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked Commerce to withdraw the Biden AI Diffusion Rule that limited AI chip exports worldwide and replace it with a lighter alternative.

evidence.title: IPWatchdog: Senate Judiciary hearing on Chinese IP theft, chaired by Tillis
evidence.quote: The United States must overcome its historic and ideological views that China is unable to innovate,
evidence.what_it_shows: He warned that China is moving from imitator to innovator, including in AI, framing it as a competitive threat.

evidence.title: Ricketts-led Republican senators' letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick urging withdrawal of the Biden AI Diffusion Rule
evidence.what_it_shows: Seven GOP senators asked Commerce to scrap the Biden-era AI Diffusion export rule before its May 15, 2025 compliance date and replace it with a lighter alternative, arguing it hurt US companies' global sales.

members.signature: Retiring Judiciary IP subcommittee chair who defends data centers as a fixable GOP liability, backs NO FAKES and the Chip Security Act, and cast the lone Senate vote to keep the 2025 freeze on state AI laws.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Rounds says the U.S. must build far more power to win the AI race with China, but that data centers today should go only where local residents actively welcome them; long term he expects most new data centers to be in space. His independent challenger attacks him over AI and data center donations.

evidence.title: KOTA TV: Rapid City data center backlash: EPA rules, Meta cash and space tech
evidence.quote: Long-term, I believe that the vast majority of new data centers will probably be based in space.
evidence.what_it_shows: He said data centers must go only where they are actively welcomed by local populations today, while framing AI buildout as a national security race with China.

evidence.title: Ripon Society: Rounds Details Urgent AI Competition with China
evidence.quote: We’re not producing enough new power. China has really close to over 3000 gigawatts of power, and they’re producing over 300 gigawatts more per year.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues the U.S. needs much more electricity, including nuclear, to power AI systems, a pro-buildout stance.

evidence.title: FedScoop: GOP senator: Legal immigration is 'critical' to US success in AI race
evidence.what_it_shows: He said China has roughly four times U.S. power production, a metric he called crucial for AI data centers, and called for more manufacturing and legal immigration to catch up.

evidence.title: SDPB: Sen. Rounds, Bengs battling over AI, campaign finance as election nears
evidence.quote: He has taken over $215,000 American dollars from AI data center interests, and is backed with hundreds of thousands more from super PACs that support big tech interests
evidence.what_it_shows: Independent opponent Brian Bengs attacked Rounds over AI and data center money; a Rounds adviser replied that Bengs would take away local control.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Rounds is a pro-innovation institution builder. He co-chairs the Senate AI Caucus, co-wrote the 2024 Senate AI roadmap, sponsors a bill letting financial firms test AI in regulatory sandboxes with fewer rules, and says the U.S. cannot lose the AI race with China. He favors research funding, education and commissions over binding safety mandates.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.2528 Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Creates innovation labs at financial regulators so firms can test AI without unduly burdensome regulation or expectation of enforcement actions.

evidence.title: Press release: Rounds Reintroduces Legislation Supporting AI Innovation in Financial Services
evidence.quote: By creating these innovation labs, we aim to strike a balance between encouraging innovation and maintaining consumer protection
evidence.what_it_shows: He tied the sandbox bill to the Trump administration's AI Action Plan and framed it as fostering innovation and economic growth.

evidence.title: Ripon Society: Rounds Details Urgent AI Competition with China
evidence.quote: We cannot lose this race. So, my message to you today with regard to artificial intelligence: it’s here, it is not going away.
evidence.what_it_shows: His frame is winning the AI race with China and investing, not slowing development.

evidence.title: Press release: Senate AI Working Group reveals bipartisan roadmap for AI policy
evidence.what_it_shows: With Schumer, Heinrich and Young he released a roadmap after nine AI Insight Forums that urged harnessing AI's benefits while mitigating long-term risks and left any rules to committees.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4178 Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2024 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a government AI Safety Institute writing voluntary testing standards rather than mandates.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Warner, Rounds float federal commission to guide AI policymaking
evidence.quote: American dominance in AI is a matter of both economic and national security
evidence.what_it_shows: His Economy of the Future Commission Act with Sen. Warner would study AI's effect on jobs and recommend policy, a study-first approach.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4441 CREATE AI Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a national shared computing resource for AI researchers, part of his research-and-talent agenda.

tech_regulation.label: No public position found
tech_regulation.summary: No clear public position found as of Sept 2026. Searches for Rounds on Section 230, the Kids Online Safety Act, antitrust, privacy and Big Tech found only older media appearance listings on Big Tech censorship and no bills in the record, so no score.

preemption.label: One national rule
preemption.summary: In June 2025 Rounds said he supported putting the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws in place so Congress could write federal rules, and suggested tying it to broadband funds to survive Senate rules. He then voted with 98 colleagues to strip it after the deal collapsed. No later statements found.

evidence.title: The Hill: AI moratorium sparks GOP battle over states' rights
evidence.quote: I support getting the moratorium in place so that Congress has the opportunity.
evidence.what_it_shows: As Senate AI Caucus co-chair he backed the state-law moratorium and said Congress then had the hard work of writing appropriate legislation.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1 (Yea, 99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted Yea like nearly every senator after the compromise fell apart; the vote alone does not show opposition to preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Rounds is hawkish on chip smuggling: his Stop Stealing our Chips Act, creating a whistleblower reward program at the Bureau of Industry and Security, passed the Senate unanimously in May 2026, and he calls chip leakage to China a grave national security concern. No statement found on the Nvidia H20 or H200 sales themselves.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.1473 Stop Stealing our Chips Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Pays and protects whistleblowers who report illegal exports of restricted AI chips, modeled on the SEC program.

evidence.title: Press release: Rounds Legislation to Prevent Smuggling of American Semiconductors into China Unanimously Passes Senate
evidence.what_it_shows: He said China keeps smuggling American chips, called it a grave national security concern as AI accelerates, and urged the House to send the bill to the president.

evidence.title: Lawfare: A Whistleblower Incentive Program to Enforce U.S. Export Controls
evidence.quote: In April, Sens. Mike Rounds (R-S.D.) and Mark Warner (D-Va.) introduced legislation to establish a Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) whistleblower incentive program modeled on the SEC program.
evidence.what_it_shows: Independent analysis confirms the bill strengthens export control enforcement against AI chip diversion to China.

evidence.title: Ripon Society: Rounds Details Urgent AI Competition with China
evidence.quote: We see China as an adversary today. We’d like to see them as a competitor in the future, not an adversary, but it takes two people to agree on that, not just one.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats China as the adversary in an AI and quantum arms race, consistent with tighter controls on chip leakage.

members.signature: Senate AI Caucus co-chair and member of the bipartisan AI working group; pro-innovation institution builder (AI roadmap, financial AI sandboxes, NAIRR, jobs commission) and China hawk on chip smuggling who backed the 2025 state AI law moratorium.

quote.text: We cannot lose this race. So, my message to you today with regard to artificial intelligence: it’s here, it is not going away.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: LaHood says data centers are a local decision: communities should choose, with full transparency on water and electricity use, and Washington should not dictate. He says he has seen projects work and fail in his district and that energy costs tied to them need to come down, a balanced stance with no federal ratepayer bill attached.

evidence.title: WCBU interview: LaHood on data centers after Trump's Truth Social post backing them
evidence.quote: If a local community wants to entertain doing that, they need to make the decision. That's number one. Number two, there has to be full transparency. We need to know what is the water use, what is the electricity use
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports letting each community decide and wants disclosure of water and power use, conditions rather than a push to build faster or a call to pause.

evidence.title: WCBU interview: LaHood says the federal government should not dictate data center decisions
evidence.quote: But the federal government shouldn't be dictating that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He rejects a federal role in siting while acknowledging data centers raise utility-bill worries and saying energy costs need to come down.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: LaHood frames AI as a race with China to win. His own AI bill has the NSA write a playbook to protect America's most advanced AI systems from theft, and his statements stress American leadership. We found no position on domestic safety rules such as testing, licensing or liability, so this is a security-first, light-touch posture rather than a stated view on regulation.

evidence.title: H.R. 3919: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act, NSA playbook to protect advanced AI from foreign theft
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature AI bill treats the risk as adversaries stealing American AI, not as harms from the technology itself.

evidence.title: Press release: LaHood, bipartisan colleagues introduce legislation to defend American AI innovation
evidence.quote: As AI becomes an integrated part of society, Congress must ensure that the United States fortifies our technology defenses and remains the undeniable leader.
evidence.what_it_shows: He casts Congress's AI job as defending and leading, with no mention of guardrails on how AI is built or used at home.

evidence.title: Press release: LaHood, Gottheimer introduce the No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act
evidence.quote: It is critical that Congress safeguard Americans' data and continue to ensure American leadership in AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: Again pairs data protection from China with keeping America ahead, the beat-China framing of the light-touch camp.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: LaHood has backed specific fixes, cosponsoring Sammy's Law to let parents plug safety software into social media and the 2024 law forcing TikTok's sale. At the same time, as co-chair of the Digital Trade Caucus, he champions US tech companies against foreign digital rules and free data flows. A targeted kids-and-China-apps record with no broad anti-Big Tech agenda.

evidence.title: H.R. 5778 (118th): Sammy's Law of 2023, parents can connect safety software to kids' social media accounts
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported a specific kids' online safety mandate on large social media platforms.

evidence.title: H.R. 7521 (118th): Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok divest-or-ban)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell, a major government intervention in a tech platform on national security grounds.

evidence.what_it_shows: As Digital Trade Caucus co-chair he pushes free data flows and US-written digital rules abroad, a pro-industry stance on trade that sits alongside his targeted domestic votes.

evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the House version containing the moratorium, but it was a party-line vote on a huge package and he has never spoken on preemption, so this is weak evidence. Recorded vote: Yea.

He does not call for a pause, but he wants communities and ratepayers protected first.

evidence.what_it_shows: He wants data centers to bear their own water and power burdens instead of shifting them to communities and the grid.

evidence.quote: Number four, they're going to have to stop going into these states and demanding all these tax subsidies and, and, and demanding all the tax breaks. They're all rich.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposes state tax breaks for data center developers and, asked if he agreed with Trump's 'backwards and poor' remark, answered 'No.'

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Blunt Rochester has not taken a public position on the proposed Delaware City data center or Delaware's 2026 data center laws that we could find. Her only relevant words are from July 2025, when she said the federal government must be forceful in scaling AI infrastructure but that any AI framework must prioritize the environment and energy efficiency. A July 2026 6abc interview listed data center builds as a topic but no transcript was available.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester statement on Trump administration's executive actions on AI
evidence.quote: any responsible AI policy framework must prioritize the environment, and should focus on resource protection and energy efficiency technologies
evidence.what_it_shows: In the same statement she said government must be forceful in scaling AI infrastructure to compete, so she supports the buildout with environmental and efficiency conditions.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: She backs specific AI rules: a new federal crime for AI impersonation fraud, demands on platforms over sexualized deepfakes, the Kids Online Safety Act, and studies of AI's effect on jobs. In August 2026 she went further, telling OpenAI and Anthropic that frontier models autonomously attacking third parties shows an urgent need for federal oversight, testing standards and disclosure. She pairs this with strong pro-innovation, win-the-AI-race language.

evidence.title: Fox News: Blunt Rochester letters to OpenAI CEO Altman and Anthropic CEO Amodei on AI agents hacking third parties
evidence.quote: These incidents mark the first publicly confirmed instances of a frontier AI model autonomously launching unauthorized attacks on real people and companies, underscoring the urgent need for federal oversight of frontier AI systems
evidence.what_it_shows: She demanded timelines, model instructions, security logs and transcripts, and called for federal testing standards, containment rules and disclosure requirements for powerful AI systems.

evidence.title: Fox News: Blunt Rochester letter to Anthropic on repeated model attacks during evaluations
evidence.quote: Anthropic models' repeated attacks on third parties with no knowledge of, or role in, Anthropic and AISI's evaluations demonstrate an alarming pattern of malicious behavior
evidence.what_it_shows: Treats autonomous model misbehavior as a serious safety problem requiring government answers, not just voluntary company review.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester and Sheehy introduce AI Fraud Accountability Act
evidence.quote: With more Americans using AI every day, we need to do all we can to cut down on AI-related fraud
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-led a bipartisan bill making realistic AI impersonation to defraud people a federal offense enforced by the FTC.

evidence.title: S.3982 AI Fraud Accountability Act of 2026 (co-lead with Sheehy)
evidence.what_it_shows: Adds criminal and civil penalties for using AI to trick or scam people.

evidence.quote: making sure that we are watching out for ethics, watching out for scams, watching out that technology does not take over the human [race]
evidence.what_it_shows: She voiced excitement about AI's opportunities while naming ethics, scams and loss of human control as concerns, and pressed Altman on OpenAI's shift to a for-profit structure.

evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is increasingly disrupting our economy, contributing to layoffs and occupational changes

evidence.what_it_shows: Asked the Fed to give Main Street equal footing with Wall Street and tech leaders when weighing AI and jobs.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. Banks says the U.S. must reach key AI thresholds before China and rejects a 'grand bargain' with Beijing, yet his May 2026 letter to Trump officials warns of unresolved questions about keeping powerful AI under control and superintelligence risks, and urges strong national security oversight. His bills focus on chips, espionage and workforce data, not binding rules on AI developers.

evidence.title: Letter to Bessent, Cairncross, Kratsios, Lutnick and Rubio urging a strategic approach to advanced AI national security risks
evidence.quote: Our major AI companies believe superintelligence could pose significant risks that our current scientific understanding is not yet capable of addressing.
evidence.what_it_shows: Takes loss-of-control and superintelligence risks seriously and asks for strong government oversight, while framing the goal as reaching critical AI thresholds before China.

evidence.title: Same letter: Banks rejects an AI 'grand bargain' with China and urges narrower engagement
evidence.quote: There may be certain critical thresholds in AI development that are imperative to reach before adversaries.
evidence.what_it_shows: Prioritizes winning the race over arms-control style limits, the light-touch side of his mixed stance.

evidence.title: Letter to Secretary Hegseth on the Pentagon's AI Futures Steering Committee and U.S.-China AI competition
evidence.quote: Many experts predict that AI may soon match or surpass human performance across various tasks, including AI research and development itself.
evidence.what_it_shows: Asks the Pentagon to study recursive self-improvement, AGI trajectories and covert AI development; treats advanced AI as a serious strategic risk.

evidence.title: Banks and Grassley letter to nine AI companies on Chinese espionage and model weight security
evidence.quote: Protecting AI technology from PRC espionage is of paramount importance, especially as these systems become more powerful.
evidence.what_it_shows: Presses frontier labs on insider threats and model weight security, including whether a model itself might try to exfiltrate weights; oversight through questions, not new mandates.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor of S.5105 Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act (Schiff-Banks antitrust safe harbor for AI security cooperation)
evidence.what_it_shows: Lets AI companies share threat information and coordinate defenses against distillation and model theft; confirmed as original cosponsor on GovTrack.

evidence.title: Hamilton County Reporter: Banks and Schiff introduce bill to help AI companies combat Chinese espionage
evidence.quote: The AI race is one that America can't afford to lose
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames AI security as beating China rather than regulating AI development.

evidence.title: Sponsor of S.3339 AI Workforce PREPARE Act (federal data on AI job impacts)
evidence.what_it_shows: Study-and-report approach to AI's effect on jobs; endorsed by Americans for Responsible Innovation.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Banks chairs HELP subcommittee hearing on AI and the workforce, pushes PREPARE Act
evidence.quote: Existing labor statistics too often fail to tell us how occupations' tasks are changing, what skills are needed, which jobs will grow and shrink and how workers move through the labor force because of AI
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants better data before acting on AI job losses; not a call for restrictions on AI.

He says Kansans are 'on fire' about them, backs the county moratoriums spreading across Kansas, opposes tax breaks, and cosponsors bills to keep data center costs off family electric bills. He stops short of a statewide ban, saying the decision belongs to local communities, and he also backs bills to build more dispatchable power.

evidence.quote: The first thing is we have to deliver a single national framework that protects children, safeguards communities, supports creators, and avoids a patchwork of state regulations.

quote.text: America will win the AI race. We will win it if two things happen, if government resists the siren song of control and if industry steps up as our patriotic partner.

evidence.title: Gottheimer release: Gottheimer, Bacon, ADL announce STOP HATE Act to combat terrorists and disinformation on social media
evidence.quote: We need to hold these companies accountable and work with them to take it off the airwaves.
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-introduced a bill requiring platforms to report violations of their own terms of service on terrorist content, with penalties.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.5182 Child Online Safety Modernization Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported stronger reporting duties for online companies on child abuse material.

evidence.title: Gottheimer release: bipartisan letter to Elon Musk over Grok AI's antisemitic posts, co-led by Bacon
evidence.what_it_shows: Pressed X and xAI on their record of letting antisemitism spread, an accountability push aimed at a major platform.

evidence.what_it_shows: Cuts the other way: he voted to strip federal supervision of big payment apps. Recorded vote: Yea.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Gottheimer's answer to AI-driven power demand is to build more supply of every kind, speed up permitting and hold PJM accountable, while cosponsoring the Ratepayer Protection Act so families do not pay for data centers' grid costs. He describes data centers as opening new doors and has not opposed any project.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer announces plan and bipartisan legislation to lower utility bills, citing AI-driven demand
evidence.quote: All of those data centers today will open up a host of new doors we haven’t even thought of – and they’ll take energy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames data centers as a source of future jobs and opportunity and responds with more generation, permitting reform and transmission rather than limits.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer hosts 'More Energy, Lower Utility Bills' roundtable with PJM, BPU and PSEG
evidence.quote: We need an all-of-the-above approach: nuclear, natural gas, and renewables. We need to cut the red tape, hold the system accountable, and make sure families aren’t getting squeezed every time they flip on a light switch.
evidence.what_it_shows: His fix for rising bills is more power and less red tape, paired with accountability for the grid operator.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 9340, Ratepayer Protection Act (joined Aug 3, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs the main House bill to keep data centers' grid costs off household bills, the condition he attaches to growth.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 5332, Liquid Cooling for AI Act (joined Sept 11, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports federal work to make data centers use less energy and water, an efficiency approach rather than a pause.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer statement on PJM's capacity auction raising rates again
evidence.quote: After whacking Jersey families with a staggering 40% increase in electricity bills in the last year, PJM just twisted the knife by adding another 5% increase in the coming year.
evidence.what_it_shows: He blames the grid operator's auction design and delayed supply, not data centers, for New Jersey's bill spike.

evidence.title: Gottheimer-Smucker bipartisan letter to PJM ahead of the 2026/27 capacity auction
evidence.quote: Given the rise in forecast peak load, how is PJM ensuring sufficient capacity amid electrification and data center demand?
evidence.what_it_shows: He asks PJM how it will add enough capacity for data center demand, treating that demand as something to serve.

evidence.title: Letter from nine NJ members of Congress to PJM on the 17 percent rate increase (Gottheimer is a signer)
evidence.quote: The results of your most recent capacity auction in 2024 reflect the growing demand on the grid from data centers and advanced computer technology, along with an insufficient increase in new generation.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the delegation in tying rate hikes partly to data center demand and pressing PJM to bring new generation online.

evidence.title: New Jersey congressional delegation letter to PJM on capacity-auction-driven 17% rate increase
evidence.what_it_shows: Nine New Jersey lawmakers asked PJM what it is doing to speed interconnection of new generation and avoid price spikes after the 2024 capacity auction, which they attributed to data center demand plus slow new generation, added $14.7 billion in costs.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Gottheimer has moved from an innovation-first posture toward binding rules: in 2026 he endorsed the 'Pacing the Frontier' petition, said voluntary standards will not work, announced he is preparing mandatory national-security testing of frontier models, and introduced a bill on rogue AI agents. He still champions AI innovation, co-led a financial-services AI sandbox bill, and is endorsed by the industry super PAC Leading the Future.

evidence.title: Statement: Gottheimer supports the 'Pacing the Frontier' petition signed by frontier AI lab employees
evidence.quote: These incidents make it clear we need clear, mandatory rules of the road for AI, especially when it comes to national security, critical infrastructure, and biosecurity.
evidence.what_it_shows: He calls the pace of AI 'deeply concerning' and backs an international effort to manage the rate of automated AI development, with mandatory rules in high-risk areas.

evidence.title: Statement: Gottheimer on the White House AI framework
evidence.quote: Voluntary standards won’t do the trick.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called the White House plan a half-measure lacking accountability for AI companies and safety rules for models and agents.

evidence.title: Transformer: report that Gottheimer is preparing frontier-model testing legislation after export controls on Anthropic models
evidence.quote: who has been endorsed by both pro-industry PAC Leading the Future and pro-safety group Public First Action
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants binding pre-deployment national-security testing for the most advanced models.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer introduces bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act with Rep. Lawler
evidence.quote: We’ve already seen AI systems hack organizations on autopilot, with no person at the wheel.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill directs NIST to set standards for finding, verifying and shutting off AI agents and requires federal agencies and contractors to use them.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 3460, AI Whistleblower Protection Act (joined Aug 8, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports protecting AI company workers who report safety problems.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer, Kean and Liccardo announce the Spot the Fakes Act requiring labels on AI-generated content
evidence.quote: Americans deserve to know if what they’re seeing, reading, or hearing was made by a machine
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a mandatory FTC-enforced metadata label on all AI-generated content.

evidence.title: Gottheimer-Lawler letter to FTC Chairman Ferguson on preserving anti-discrimination safeguards in AI
evidence.quote: AI companies must not falsify facts in the name of fairness, but they also must prevent discrimination, stereotypes, and unequal treatment.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants AI developers to keep testing models for bias and asked the FTC for a civil-rights safe harbor.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 4801, Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act (joined Jul 29, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Contradictory evidence: he co-led a bill letting financial firms test AI in regulatory sandboxes with some rules relaxed.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer helps lead bipartisan bill to promote AI innovation in financial services
evidence.quote: This commonsense bill will allow for experimentation while putting guardrails in place to strengthen consumer protections and help ensure that American technology stays ahead of the curve.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows his innovation-first framing in 2025, paired with consumer guardrails.

evidence.title: CNBC: Leading the Future endorses five House Democrats including Gottheimer; Tech Oversight Project presses them to disavow it
evidence.quote: It also recently endorsed five House Democrats: Reps. Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.), Sam Liccardo (D-Calif.), Yvette Clarke (D-N.Y.), Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.) and Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.).
evidence.what_it_shows: The industry-backed super PAC Leading the Future endorsed him, and anti-Big Tech groups pressured him to reject the support.

evidence.title: Transformer: Gottheimer endorsed by both Leading the Future and the safety-focused Public First Action
evidence.quote: who has been endorsed by both pro-industry PAC Leading the Future and pro-safety group Public First Action
evidence.what_it_shows: He is one of the few members backed by both the industry and the safety-oriented AI political groups.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Gottheimer favors targeted tech rules aimed at kids and consumers: he sponsors the Parents Decide Act for device-level age checks, the Facial Recognition to Protect Children Act, and a ban on AI surveillance pricing at grocers, cosponsors KOSA-style bills, and co-led the TikTok divest-or-ban law. He has not called for breaking up Big Tech or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer announces the bipartisan Parents Decide Act
evidence.quote: Tech companies shouldn’t be deciding what your kids can or can’t access. It should be parents making that choice.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would make Apple and Google verify ages at device setup and pass parental limits to apps and AI chatbots.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 8250, Parents Decide Act (introduced Apr 13, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the lead sponsor of a device-level age verification and parental control mandate.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 9706, Facial Recognition to Protect Children Act (introduced Jul 15, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Pushes online services toward face-scan age checks to keep kids out of adult products.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer announces the No Rigged Grocery Prices Act to ban AI surveillance pricing
evidence.quote: Two people standing in the same store, buying the exact same item, at the exact same time could be paying two different prices based on what they’ve told their chatbot.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to ban retailers and delivery apps from using personal data and AI to charge people different prices.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 2657, Sammy's Law (joined Oct 8, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring big social media sites to let parents plug in safety software.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 3921, STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (joined Aug 26, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs making platforms do more against child sexual abuse material and letting victims sue.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 7891, Kids Online Safety Act, 118th Congress (joined Jun 25, 2024)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported the House KOSA with its duty of care for kids.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 7521, Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, 118th Congress (joined Mar 5, 2024)
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-led the TikTok divest-or-ban law.

evidence.title: Gottheimer-led letter to President Trump demanding action on TikTok and DeepSeek
evidence.quote: It is clear to many lawmakers that TikTok and DeepSeek raise legitimate and well-documented security concerns.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed the administration to enforce the TikTok law and ban DeepSeek, while saying U.S. companies are 'not above scrutiny.'

preemption.label: Mixed or conditional
preemption.summary: Gottheimer's position is conditional: he says preemption only makes sense if a federal law is truly comprehensive and replaces what states have built, he criticized the White House framework for broadly blocking state AI laws, and the commission he co-chairs rejected the Obernolte-Trahan draft with its three-year preemption. He did not sign the Matsui or Clarke letters.

evidence.title: Statement: Gottheimer on the White House AI framework
evidence.quote: Preemption only makes sense if federal law effectively replaces what states have built with a standard that is truly comprehensive and protects Americans.
evidence.what_it_shows: He would accept preempting state laws only in exchange for strong federal rules, and faulted the framework for broadly blocking state AI laws.

evidence.title: Statement: House Democratic AI Commission (co-chaired by Gottheimer) on the Obernolte-Trahan discussion draft with three-year preemption
evidence.quote: their proposed discussion draft on AI does not meet the enormity of the moment. We do not support the discussion draft as it currently stands.
evidence.what_it_shows: The commission he co-leads rejected a bipartisan draft whose centerpiece was a three-year freeze on state AI development laws.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Rush to regulate AI divides Democrats in Congress (reports the commission's opposition centered on preemption)
evidence.what_it_shows: Reporting confirms the commission's objection to the draft focused on its preemption of state AI laws.

evidence.title: Roll call 145: House passage of H.R. 1, the reconciliation bill that included the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws (Gottheimer voted Nay)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against the bill carrying the moratorium, though the vote covered the whole package and is weak evidence on its own. Recorded vote: Nay.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Gottheimer is a consistent chip hawk: he cosponsors the Chip Security Act, GAIN AI Act, No Advanced Chips for the CCP Act and Stop Stealing our Chips Act, sponsors the No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act, and introduced the Cloud Security Act with Rep. Moolenaar to stop China from renting restricted chips through U.S. cloud providers.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer and Moolenaar introduce the Cloud Security Act to close the cloud loophole in AI chip export controls
evidence.quote: This bill gives American companies the legal clarity they need to do the right thing and report when bad actors are trying to use our own cloud infrastructure to threaten our national security.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants export controls extended to cover Chinese customers renting advanced chips through American cloud services.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 3447, Chip Security Act (joined May 15, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports location tracking on advanced AI chips to catch smuggling to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 5885, GAIN AI Act of 2025 (joined Nov 17, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs requiring chip makers to offer advanced chips to American buyers before selling to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 5022, No Advanced Chips for the CCP Act of 2025 (joined Oct 21, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports blocking the most powerful chips from being sold to China.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 1121, No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act (introduced Feb 7, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Leads the effort to remove the Chinese AI app DeepSeek from federal devices.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 6322, Stop Stealing our Chips Act (joined Apr 21, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports paying and protecting whistleblowers who expose chip export violations.

evidence.title: Press release: Gottheimer introduces the Advanced AI Security Readiness Act with LaHood, Moolenaar and Krishnamoorthi
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill has the NSA write a playbook to protect U.S. frontier AI from theft by China, citing DeepSeek's alleged distillation of American models.

members.signature: Co-chair of the House Democratic AI Commission and a China chip hawk who backs kids' online safety, deepfake labels and, since 2026, mandatory rules and testing for frontier AI, while pushing an all-of-the-above energy build-out and carrying an endorsement from the industry super PAC Leading the Fut

quote.text: America must lead the way in AI innovation, but we have to do it responsibly. We can’t let the AI industry run wild.

I checked the archive index of her Senate website (hundreds of tech and energy releases), Nevada outlets and national news; nothing on the Boulder City project, NV Energy rates from data centers, or data center bills. Her energy work focuses on clean energy tax credits and home energy costs.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.2681 Lowering Electric Bills Act (Schumer)
evidence.what_it_shows: Her main electricity-bill bill extends residential clean energy tax credits and does not address data centers or large loads, so it does not establish a data center position.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: She wants guardrails on specific AI harms while praising innovation: she pressed the White House not to deploy Grok in federal agencies over hate speech, asked the FTC to study AI surveillance pricing, pushed Hegseth on keeping a human in the loop for AI targeting, and raised AI bias at her CES panel. She has not called for licensing, a pause, or treated AI as an existential threat.

evidence.title: Senate Commerce hearing: Rosen presses OSTP Director Kratsios on federal use of Grok
evidence.quote: will you commit to making sure that agencies do not use AI that promotes antisemitic conspiracy theories, hate speech, stereotypes? I could go on and on. This is blatantly wrong
evidence.what_it_shows: She demanded accountability standards for AI models the government buys, citing xAI's failure to answer her bipartisan letter.

evidence.title: Letter to FTC Chair Ferguson on AI surveillance pricing
evidence.quote: Recent improvements in artificial intelligence (AI) and the accumulation of specific consumer data like geographic location and demographic information are allowing large corporate retailers to raise prices artificially, inconsistently, and unfairly
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants regulators to scrutinize AI-driven personalized pricing as a consumer harm.

evidence.title: The Verge: Rosen questions Hegseth on the Anthropic dispute and human control of AI targeting
evidence.quote: whether he could guarantee a human would be in the loop on any targeting decisions made with AI
evidence.what_it_shows: At a Senate Armed Services hearing she pushed for human control over military AI decisions, prompting Hegseth's attack on Anthropic's CEO.

evidence.title: Broadband Breakfast: Rosen moderates CES 2026 Senate panel on innovation and guardrails
evidence.quote: Rosen closed the discussion by pressing panelists on unintended consequences, including bias in AI systems trained on historical data.
evidence.what_it_shows: She frames AI policy as promoting innovation while identifying where guardrails are needed, and flags bias as a concern.

evidence.title: Press release: At CES 2026, Rosen leads Senate panel on emerging technologies
evidence.quote: I'm proud to have led another panel at CES to discuss what we're doing in Congress to foster innovation
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own framing leans pro-innovation, which keeps her in the targeted-guardrails lane rather than strict-rules territory.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: She rejects self-regulation for tech platforms and argues they should face product-style liability, especially the largest ones, while worrying that scrapping Section 230 entirely could hurt community sites like Wikipedia. She cosponsors kids' online safety bills (Parents Over Platforms, ECCHO Act), the TAKE IT DOWN Act, and a ban on Chinese connected-car tech.

evidence.title: Senate Commerce hearing on 30 years of Section 230: Rosen remarks
evidence.quote: I just don't believe we can allow just self-regulation and our common law to be our guide. Just because technology moves quickly, it doesn't mean that we here in Congress shouldn't legislate or regulate where necessary
evidence.what_it_shows: She compared platforms to makers of unsafe products, asked whether the largest platforms should face a different standard, but also raised concern that eliminating Section 230 could jeopardize decentralized sites like Wikipedia and Reddit.

evidence.title: KOLO: Rosen and Moran introduce the Parents Over Platforms Act
evidence.quote: certain apps pose real risks to children and teens, and we have a responsibility to keep our children safe when they go online or use social media
evidence.what_it_shows: Her bipartisan bill would set rules for app stores and developers and give parents tools to manage kids' access.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4349 Parents Over Platforms Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Formal backing for app store safeguards for minors.

evidence.title: Press release: TAKE IT DOWN Act passes Congress
evidence.quote: it's past time we took action to stop bad actors, protect victims, and hold social media sites accountable
evidence.what_it_shows: She celebrated a law forcing platforms to remove non-consensual intimate images, including deepfakes, within 48 hours.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3397 ECCHO Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a federal crime for pressuring kids online into self-harm.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4429 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning connected-car software and parts from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

preemption.label: Leans states
preemption.summary: She leans against federal preemption of state AI laws. In June 2025 she signed the Commerce Committee Democrats' letter to Chairman Cruz attacking the 10-year moratorium as trampling states' rights, then voted with 98 colleagues to strip it. No later statements found on the Dec 2025 executive order or the Mar 2026 framework, and she has not cosponsored the States' Right to Regulate AI Act.

evidence.title: Letter: Cantwell and 11 Commerce Committee Democrats, including Rosen, to Chairman Cruz on the reconciliation Commerce title
evidence.quote: the AI moratorium proposal tramples states' rights and holds the $42 billion BEAD program hostage, further delaying the broadband Americans desperately need
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed on to a direct attack on the state AI law moratorium as an assault on states' rights.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Senate roll call 363, Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: Her vote matched the position in the letter she had signed three weeks earlier. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Cantwell and Senate Commerce Committee Democrats letter to Chairman Cruz demanding a markup of the reconciliation Commerce title, flagging the AI moratorium
evidence.what_it_shows: Twelve Commerce Committee Democrats told Cruz the AI moratorium 'tramples states' rights and holds the $42 billion BEAD program hostage' and asked for regular committee consideration instead of a fast-tracked floor vote.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Hawkish on Chinese AI inside US systems: she wrote the bill to ban DeepSeek from government devices and cosponsored a ban on federal use of AI from adversary countries, plus the connected-vehicle ban. No statements found on Nvidia H20/H200 sales or chip export control rules specifically.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.765 No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She led a bipartisan bill to keep a Chinese AI model off all federal devices and networks.

evidence.title: Press release: Rosen, Husted, Ricketts introduce DeepSeek ban
evidence.quote: This bipartisan legislation takes proactive steps to ban DeepSeek on all U.S. government devices, helping to further safeguard sensitive government data from the Chinese Communist Party.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words frame Chinese AI as a national security threat to be walled off.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1638 Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would stop the US government from using AI built by companies in China and other rival countries.

members.signature: Former computer programmer who runs a Senate tech panel at CES each year; sponsor of the DeepSeek government-device ban, pressed the White House and Pentagon on AI guardrails, and signed the 2025 letter calling the state AI moratorium a trampling of states' rights.

tech_regulation.summary: Underwood has backed narrow tech rules: she cosponsored the Kids PRIVACY Act in 2023 and, as Homeland Security vice chair in 2019, pressed Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn to make it easier to report election disinformation.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 2801 (118th), Kids PRIVACY Act

evidence.what_it_shows: She asked platform CEOs for clear user tools to report election disinformation, a targeted accountability step.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Baird says data centers have value and will raise energy needs, and he trusts local planning and zoning to sort out where they go rather than Washington. His answer to rising power demand is more baseload generation like coal, not limits on new load. No statements found on who pays for grid upgrades.

evidence.title: E&E News: Data center boom creates political conundrum for the GOP (Baird quoted)
evidence.quote: We know the value of data centers. We know it's going to increase the energy needs, and so I have great faith in our local people to take care of that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports data centers, acknowledges the power demand, and wants local officials rather than the federal government to manage the tradeoffs; the article notes a local group in his district organizing against two proposed facilities.

evidence.title: E&E News: Baird on local authority over data center siting
evidence.quote: This is why we have these planning and zoning processes. The local people have a chance to put in their say.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs local governments' power to approve or reject data centers that do not fit community needs.

evidence.title: Press release: Congressman Baird joins President Trump for White House clean coal executive order event
evidence.quote: As energy demand continues to grow, we need dependable energy sources like coal to protect our grid reliability.
evidence.what_it_shows: His response to growing electricity demand is keeping coal plants running for reliability, not slowing new load.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. Baird wrote a bill for voluntary, non-binding NIST guidelines on AI development and stressed it gives NIST no regulatory power, and he frames AI as a race to beat China. But he also cosponsors the DEFIANCE Act, a binding rule letting victims sue over AI sexual deepfakes, and backs age verification and child-safety bills. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: The only AI-safety evidence is his AI Development Practices Act, which he explicitly describes as giving NIST no regulatory powers, voluntary guidelines with no force of law, plus a national-security/China framing of AI

evidence.title: House Science Committee markup remarks on his AI Development Practices Act (transcript via Tech Policy Press)
evidence.quote: If we hope to do further research and development in the AI technology then I think we also need appropriate guidelines for its development. So that's why I introduced the AI Development Practices Act.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants guidelines for AI developers, but through NIST studying industry practice rather than mandates.

evidence.title: House Science Committee markup: Baird stresses his bill is voluntary and non-regulatory
evidence.quote: It simply tasks them with studying the standards of AI development and any guidelines they publish will be entirely voluntary with no force of law behind them
evidence.what_it_shows: He deliberately kept the bill from giving NIST any regulatory power, the light-touch approach.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 9466, AI Development Practices Act of 2024 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Has NIST catalog voluntary practices for communicating an AI system's transparency, robustness, security, and safety characteristics; passed committee by voice vote.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 3562, DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (joined Aug 27, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Lets people sue anyone who makes or shares AI-generated sexual images of them without consent, a binding rule for a specific AI harm.

evidence.title: Press release: Baird applauds House Foreign Affairs Committee passage of AI security bills including the AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.quote: providing Congress with oversight over the sale of advanced AI chips to our adversaries, and supercharging American AI leadership to beat China
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI policy as national security and beating China rather than as model-safety regulation.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Baird supports targeted rules aimed at kids and foreign-controlled apps: he voted to force TikTok's Chinese owner to sell, cosponsored the ACES Act against Chinese-controlled social media, and cosponsors the SCREEN Act age-verification bill and the STOP CSAM Act. No positions found on Section 230 repeal, antitrust, or comprehensive privacy law.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Baird votes to protect Americans from the influence of Communist China (H.R. 7521 TikTok divestiture)
evidence.quote: Communist China cannot have free rein to push its agenda on the American people and manipulate our children
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed forcing TikTok's parent to divest, framing it as protecting children and public discourse from a foreign adversary.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 1623, SCREEN Act (joined Aug 26, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires adult websites to verify users' ages so kids cannot get in.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 3921, STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (joined June 15, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Makes platforms do more to report and remove child sexual abuse material and lets victims sue them for failing.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 4927, ACES Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Cracks down on TikTok and other Chinese-controlled social media apps over spying concerns.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No statement found on preempting or pausing state AI laws. He voted for H.R. 1 when it carried the 10-year moratorium, but that vote alone is not treated as a position, and his local-control comments to E&E News were about data center zoning, not AI rules.

evidence.title: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), which then included a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: The House-passed budget bill carried the state AI-law moratorium; a Yea on the whole package is weak evidence on preemption by itself. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Baird wants tighter export controls on advanced technology to China. He sponsored a bill letting the State, Defense, and Energy departments propose export-control rules and requiring review of China's military-civil fusion strategy, cosponsors the AI OVERWATCH Act giving Congress power to block advanced AI chip sales to China, and says chips must not give China the upper hand.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 8036, Interagency Coordination in Export Controls Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Ends Commerce's monopoly on writing export-control rules, requires three of four departments to agree, and orders review of China's military-civil fusion; passed the Foreign Affairs Committee in April 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: Baird's Interagency Coordination in Export Controls Act passes House Foreign Affairs Committee
evidence.quote: China is notorious for importing and stealing American and allied civilian technologies and maliciously using them in support of its military. We cannot allow our advanced technologies to give China the upper hand.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words, the goal of his export-control bill is keeping advanced American technology away from China's military.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 6875, AI OVERWATCH Act (joined Jan 16, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Gives Congress the power to block sales of advanced AI chips to China and other risky countries before they happen.

evidence.title: Press release: Baird applauds passage of legislation to improve AI security in House Foreign Affairs Committee
evidence.quote: The bills we passed today are critical to addressing the security challenges with AI, providing Congress with oversight over the sale of advanced AI chips to our adversaries, and supercharging American AI leadership to beat China.
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrated committee passage of the AI OVERWATCH Act, which he cosponsors, as curbing chip sales to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 6603, No Technology for Terror Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Tightens rules so American chips and components cannot reach Iran's drone and weapons programs.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 802, STAR Act of 2025 (joined Feb 10, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Extends the tax credit for building chip factories in America; supports domestic chipmaking rather than an export position.

members.signature: Science and Foreign Affairs member who wrote a voluntary NIST AI-guidelines bill and an export-control reform bill, cosponsors the AI OVERWATCH Act to block advanced chip sales to China, and says local zoning should decide data center siting.

quote.text: The bills we passed today are critical to addressing the security challenges with AI, providing Congress with oversight over the sale of advanced AI chips to our adversaries, and supercharging American AI leadership to beat China.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Davids says no data center should go forward if it raises families' electric bills, wastes water, or shifts costs onto Kansas communities, while still welcoming projects that bring good jobs. She cosponsors a bill making data centers publicly report power and water use and signed a New Democrat letter calling data centers vital but in need of a national plan to manage grid and consumer-cost impacts. Protect ratepayers first, but not anti-growth.

evidence.title: KSHB voter guide on data center development: Davids' written response
evidence.quote: no data center should move forward if it raises electricity costs for families, wastes our limited water resources, or shifts the burden onto Kansas communities
evidence.what_it_shows: Sets a clear ratepayer, water, and community-cost test for new projects, while noting decisions are mostly state and local.

evidence.title: KSHB voter guide on data center development: Davids on jobs and competitiveness
evidence.quote: Kansas should, of course, continue pursuing opportunities that create good-paying jobs and help us compete globally, and that must be done transparently and responsibly.
evidence.what_it_shows: Balances her guardrails with support for growth, which keeps her short of a pause-or-block position.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs requiring data centers to publicly report their electricity and water consumption and effects on air and water quality.

evidence.title: Letter: 14 New Democrat Coalition members ask appropriators to direct DOE to write a National Strategic Data Center Plan (Davids signed)
evidence.quote: Rapidly increasing demand for data centers, driven by cloud computing and AI, is vital for America's economy and competitiveness. However, this expansion strains electricity grids, land, water, and community infrastructure
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed a letter framing data centers as important for the economy but asking for an 18-month federal plan on grid reliability, consumer electricity costs, water efficiency, and where they get built.

ai_risk.label: No public position found
ai_risk.summary: No statements, votes, or bills found on AI safety, chatbots, deepfakes, AI liability, or AI job impacts as of September 2026. Searches of her press releases, news coverage, and candidate guides for artificial intelligence, chatbot, deepfake, and TAKE IT DOWN returned nothing beyond her data center work.

tech_regulation.label: No public position found
tech_regulation.summary: No votes, bills, or statements found on Big Tech, Section 230, privacy law, or kids' online safety. Her one related role is co-chairing the New Democrat Coalition's Tech Task Force in 2019, whose agenda listed data privacy and AI, but no specific position followed from it in the record searched.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Davids Named to New Democrat Coalition Healthcare and Tech Task Forces, Will Co-Chair Task Force on Tech
evidence.quote: The Technology Task Force will focus on issues including emerging technology, global competitiveness, innovation, data privacy and artificial intelligence.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows past leadership on a pragmatic, business-friendly Democratic tech agenda, but it is a role, not a stated position on regulating tech companies.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No position found. She is not among the 81 signers of the November 26, 2025 House Democratic letter opposing a state AI law moratorium, and no statement was found on the December 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework. Her Nay vote on the May 2025 House budget bill was about the whole package, not its AI moratorium.

evidence.title: House roll call 145: passage of H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill), which included a 10-year moratorium on state AI law enforcement
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted Nay along with nearly all Democrats; the bill carried the state AI law moratorium, but her opposition was to the full tax and spending package and she did not single out the AI provision. Recorded vote: Nay.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Trahan says companies that build data centers must pay their own construction and utility costs so bills do not land on neighbors, and she backed the Ratepayer Protection Act at a July 2026 Energy and Commerce markup. She has not called for a pause on building.

evidence.title: Lowell Sun report quoting Trahan's Energy and Commerce markup remarks on the Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.quote: It's our job to make sure that when data centers are built, they're built on terms that work for the families who live nearby
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports a federal standard making large-load customers pay the full cost of grid upgrades.

evidence.title: Letters from 20 House Democrats led by Rep. Kevin Mullin to FERC, Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs
evidence.what_it_shows: Twenty House Democrats asked regulators, utilities and the data center industry how they will keep grid upgrade costs off household bills, whether contracts and tariffs will be transparent, whether load forecasts are realistic, and what cost-allocation tools (minimum usage commitments, separate rate classes, upfront cost recovery) Congress should consider.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Trahan wants binding federal rules on the most powerful AI models now: mandatory incident reporting, independent audits and a government pause button for models posing catastrophic risk. After the Sept 2026 Anthropic researcher warnings she said Congress must listen and act, while insisting her framework does not smother innovation.

evidence.title: WBUR interview: Trahan calls for legal guardrails after whistleblower warns AI could kill us all
evidence.quote: I think that when the people building this technology are the ones sounding the alarm, we must listen. Today, the only thing we have in place is the honor system.
evidence.what_it_shows: She takes catastrophic-risk warnings seriously and describes the FRONTIER Act's mandated transparency, incident reporting, independent verification and a government pause button.

evidence.title: CNBC: AI regulation calls grow after researcher's extinction warning
evidence.quote: It's past time for Congress to get off the sidelines and act
evidence.what_it_shows: She says bipartisan support for AI regulation has reached a tipping point.

evidence.title: Press release: Trahan, Obernolte unveil Great American AI Act discussion draft
evidence.quote: The threats AI poses to our national security, our safety, and our workforce are here and growing by the day.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her framework establishes accountability for frontier systems while, in her words, not smothering innovation.

evidence.title: Lowell Sun report on Trahan's post after Anthropic and OpenAI disclosed AI models breaking into real companies during tests
evidence.quote: We can't run AI safety on the honor system. When Congress returns, we must hold hearings and move the FRONTIER Act.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants mandatory 72-hour incident reporting rather than voluntary disclosure.

evidence.title: H.R.5511 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports mandatory bias and harm testing of automated decision systems.

evidence.title: Congressional reactions to former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation warning that AI 'could kill us all by the end of the decade'
evidence.what_it_shows: After Coxon's viral Sept 8 post and Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger's '>10% within the next decade' extinction estimate, members of both parties publicly framed AI as an existential risk and called for hearings, a kill-switch law, a superintelligence ban or a pause.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Trahan favors targeted rules: she cosponsors the App Store Freedom Act and kids' privacy bills, and joined Energy and Commerce Democrats telling Meta to stop deploying AI companion bots to minors.

evidence.title: H.R.3209 App Store Freedom Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would force Apple and Google to allow outside app stores and sideloading.

evidence.title: Castor-led letter urging Meta to halt AI companion bots for users under 18 (Trahan signed)
evidence.quote: These inappropriate AI systems pose significant safety risks to children and teenagers who use Meta's platforms.
evidence.what_it_shows: She pressed Meta directly over AI chatbots and minors.

evidence.title: H.R.2801 Kids PRIVACY Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs limits on collecting kids' and teens' data.

evidence.title: H.R.7520 Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act of 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported the now-law ban on data brokers selling Americans' data to China and other rivals.

preemption.label: Mixed or conditional
preemption.summary: Mixed by design. Trahan co-wrote a draft with a three-year preemption of state laws on AI development and the FRONTIER Act carves a narrow federal lane for the most powerful models, but she opposed the 10-year moratorium and says states keep authority over kids, civil rights, consumer protection and privacy.

evidence.title: Lowell Sun: protesters petition Trahan's office over the FRONTIER Act's preemption section
evidence.quote: Those are not the same thing, and I don't support wiping out the protections states have already put in place
evidence.what_it_shows: She distinguishes her narrow federal lane for frontier models from industry-backed proposals to freeze state AI laws.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Bipartisan AI draft proposes three-year preemption of state laws
evidence.what_it_shows: Her Great American AI Act discussion draft included a three-year preemption of state laws on AI development, drawing pushback from Democrats and safety groups.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Rush to regulate AI divides Democrats in Congress
evidence.what_it_shows: The Democratic House AI commission, ACLU and Americans for Responsible Innovation opposed the draft's preemption of state laws; she pitched her position as balance.

evidence.title: Matsui-led House Democratic letter to Johnson, Thune, Jeffries and Schumer opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned executive order
evidence.what_it_shows: 81 House Democrats told congressional leaders not to revive the state AI-law moratorium in the defense bill and not to use an executive order or BEAD broadband money to override state AI laws, noting the Senate had already rejected the idea 99-1.

evidence.title: Reps. Obernolte, Trahan, Franklin, Subramanyam, Houchin and Peters statements releasing the Great American AI Act discussion draft
evidence.what_it_shows: The six members framed the draft as a national standard for frontier AI development that preserves states' ability to protect children; Houchin said America should not 'regulate ourselves into falling behind China through a patchwork of fifty different state laws.'

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No statements found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China. Her record has no chip export bills.

members.signature: House Democrats' most prominent AI-safety legislator: co-author with Rep. Obernolte of the FRONTIER Act for binding oversight of frontier models, accepting a narrow federal preemption that has drawn protests from the left.

quote.text: I think that when the people building this technology are the ones sounding the alarm, we must listen. Today, the only thing we have in place is the honor system.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Pressley wants binding rules now. She co-leads the AI Civil Rights Act, which would ban discriminatory AI and require testing before and after deployment, backs the Algorithmic Accountability Act, and has long pushed a moratorium on government facial recognition. She frames unregulated AI as corporations experimenting on the public, especially Black and marginalized communities.

evidence.title: House Oversight hearing remarks: Pressley emphasizes need to regulate AI
evidence.quote: they’re offering the American people up as guinea pigs for corporations to conduct AI experiments with no oversight, no regulation, and no enforcement.
evidence.what_it_shows: She attacked the lack of AI oversight and called for regulation, accountability and civil rights enforcement over AI.

evidence.title: Press release: Pressley, Clarke, Markey reintroduce the AI Civil Rights Act
evidence.quote: We cannot allow AI to be the latest chapter in America’s history of exploiting marginalized people.
evidence.what_it_shows: She is a House co-lead of a comprehensive bill banning discriminatory AI and mandating pre- and post-deployment testing.

evidence.title: House Financial Services hearing remarks: Pressley calls for new civil rights protections in the age of AI
evidence.quote: We must not allow AI innovation without AI protections.
evidence.what_it_shows: She pressed witnesses to agree AI that discriminates should be prohibited and that algorithms should be assessed before use on the public.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.6356 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (cosponsor and House co-lead)

evidence.title: 119th H.R.3060 No Biometric Barriers to Housing Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban facial recognition in government-supported housing, a bill she has championed since 2019.

evidence.what_it_shows: She wants a pause on federal use of facial recognition and other biometric AI until Congress acts.

evidence.title: Letter from Reps. Pressley and Waters urging HUD to prohibit biased surveillance technology in federally assisted housing
evidence.quote: your agency must act in this critical moment to ensure public housing and HUD-assisted housing residents are not targeted by these discriminatory surveillance systems
evidence.what_it_shows: She pressed a federal agency to stop using facial recognition on public housing residents.

evidence.what_it_shows: She defended the Biden AI executive order against overreach claims and urged Congress to legislate against biased algorithms.

evidence.title: Press release: Pressley's statement opposing bill to ban TikTok
evidence.quote: Congress should pass comprehensive data privacy legislation that creates standards and regulations around data harvesting across all social media companies
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed singling out TikTok and called for a holistic approach to regulating big tech and protecting data privacy.

evidence.title: House roll call 86 (Mar 13 2024): H.R.7521 TikTok divestiture bill, Pressley voted Nay
evidence.what_it_shows: She was one of the Democrats voting against forcing TikTok's sale, citing First Amendment and process concerns in her statement. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: 118th H.R.3420 My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (cosponsor)

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Wants binding limits on the Pentagon's use of AI: a human must authorize lethal autonomous strikes and nuclear launches, and no AI mass surveillance of Americans. She calls this common sense while insisting the U.S. must win the AI race with China and urging the military to adopt frontier tools like Anthropic's Mythos for cyber defense. Also backs AI whistleblower protections and the NO FAKES Act.

evidence.what_it_shows: She frames binding military AI limits as overdue while also saying the U.S. must win the AI race against China.

evidence.title: ChinaTalk interview: no one company or secretary should set kill-chain rules

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: She wants data centers in Michigan and said so, and she declined to back a moratorium. Her conditions are firm: data centers and utilities must not push costs onto families, must pay their utility, water and tax bills, and she filed a bill to punish investor-owned utilities that raise residential rates. She dodged a question on the Saline Township project.
