evidence.quote: I want to force these data centers to pay their utility bills and to pay water bills for folks.
evidence.what_it_shows: At the debate she also said it is unacceptable for rates to rise and that she wants Michigan at the forefront of innovation; E&E notes she made clear she wants data centers in the state.

evidence.title: Detroit News: Data center upheaval spills into Michigan primary election campaigns
evidence.quote: I support tackling why we have 50-some data centers and one being built right now and no federal laws ... governing them, ensuring that the money goes into the communities,
evidence.what_it_shows: She called for federal laws on data centers and community benefit, but her staff cut off a follow-up about the Saline Township project.

evidence.title: Planet Detroit: Why data centers are key issue in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary
evidence.quote: We need to develop a clear, responsible policy framework to ensure these technologies are developed safely and securely,
evidence.what_it_shows: None of the Democratic candidates, including Stevens, told Planet Detroit they support a moratorium; her stated priorities were keeping data center costs off ratepayers and protecting union jobs.

evidence.title: Bridge Michigan: From AI to AIPAC, 6 issues defining the Stevens and El-Sayed race
evidence.quote: is making sure costs don't go up for Michigan families and that we are protecting good-paying union jobs.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 7926 Stop Unfair Electricity Prices Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her bill would cut off federal help to investor-owned utilities that raise residential rates, a ratepayer-protection tool she cited when asked about data centers.

evidence.what_it_shows: She claims credit for DTE's two-year rate freeze and wants binding limits on utility rate hikes.

evidence.what_it_shows: Describes her as less hostile to AI and data centers than El-Sayed and less vocal on the issue; her campaign pointed to her subcommittee post and AI task force service.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Kim writes targeted rules for AI and kids: he co-sponsored the CHAT Act 2.0 to regulate companion chatbots for minors and sponsors the Digital Age Assurance Act. He also backs innovation-friendly bills, including a regulatory sandbox for AI in financial services, and says concern about AI should not stop experimentation.

evidence.title: News 12: Sens. Kim and Husted introduce CHAT Act 2.0 (S.5154) to regulate AI companion chatbots for minors
evidence.quote: We all just want peace of mind that our kids will be okay growing up in this era of algorithms and AI. That's why we need guardrails in place to keep up with ever-evolving technology like chatbots and make sure our kids' safety, mental health, and well-being are always put first
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants binding rules on chatbots: age verification, parental controls, no romantic or self-harm content for minors, with FTC and state enforcement.

evidence.title: Biometric Update: Kim, Schiff, Lummis and Barrasso introduce the Digital Age Assurance Act (S.5090)
evidence.quote: The Digital Age Assurance Act puts kids' data privacy first as we make sure Congress and tech companies do their part to make online spaces safer for our kids,
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the lead sponsor of a bill making operating systems supply age signals to apps and websites, an alternative to ID or face-scan checks.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 (S.2381)
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants AI companies to screen training data so models cannot learn from or make child abuse images.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act (S.2528)
evidence.what_it_shows: A counterpoint: he supports letting banks test AI tools in special zones with fewer regulations.

evidence.title: VTDigger/NOTUS: Lawmakers on Capitol Hill are learning to love AI
evidence.quote: Are there things that I'm concerned about? Of course, but I think that that shouldn't make us so adverse to not try some things out.
evidence.what_it_shows: He sees AI as a tool for more responsive government and does not want concern to block experimentation.

evidence.title: Sponsor: bill to establish federal agency technology and AI talent teams (S.3410)
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants government to hire more AI experts, a capacity-building rather than restrictive approach.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

Ricketts to restrict chipmaking equipment exports, and backs bigger export-control fines. One minor bill he cosponsored would limit BIS's informal is-informed letters.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: SAFE Chips Act of 2025 (S.3374)

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Lee told the Nevada Independent that the federal government should require data centers to disclose water consumption and possibly meet energy efficiency standards, but she opposed a blanket federal pause on new data centers and said federal land can be used if the local community buys in. She also pushed an all-of-the-above energy permitting amendment and voted against the Republican SPEED Act permitting bill.

evidence.title: Nevada Independent survey: What do Nevada's congressional candidates think about data centers?
evidence.what_it_shows: In an interview she backed federal disclosure requirements on water use and potentially energy efficiency standards, while joining almost every other candidate in opposing a blanket federal moratorium; only Horsford left that door open.

evidence.title: E&E News: Republicans reject renewable energy, data center amendments to Interior-EPA bill (Lee amendment at House Appropriations markup)
evidence.quote: all-of-the-above energy permitting
evidence.what_it_shows: She offered an amendment at the Interior-EPA spending markup to push the Interior Department toward permitting all forms of energy, including the solar and wind projects the administration has slowed; Republicans rejected it.

evidence.title: House roll call 356: passage of H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act (permitting reform), Lee voted Nay
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed the House Republican bill to speed environmental reviews, a permitting change that data center and power developers favor. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Lee has backed targeted AI guardrails, mainly on deepfakes: she cosponsored the TAKE IT DOWN Act (now law) and both versions of the NO FAKES Act, plus a 2024 bill to study AI child exploitation. She also supports AI research and education funding and a bill letting small businesses borrow to buy AI tools. No statements on frontier AI dangers, licensing or a pause were found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 633, TAKE IT DOWN Act (criminalizes posting real or AI-faked intimate images and requires fast takedowns)
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined the bipartisan bill, now law, that punishes non-consensual deepfake sexual images and forces platforms to remove them.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 2794, NO FAKES Act of 2025 (right to control AI copies of one's voice and face)
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports a new legal right to stop unauthorized AI replicas of a person's voice or likeness.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 8915, NO FAKES Act of 2026 (updated version)
evidence.what_it_shows: She re-upped her support for the digital replica bill when it was reintroduced in 2026.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 8005 (118th), Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence Expert Commission Act of 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed creating an expert commission on how AI is used to exploit children.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 2385, CREATE AI Act of 2025 (national AI research resource)
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports public AI computing and data resources for researchers and students, a pro-innovation measure rather than a restriction.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 5351, NSF AI Education Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs federal spending on AI scholarships and teacher training.

evidence.title: FedScoop: House Small Business Committee advances the Small Business Technological Act (H.R. 915) from Reps. Alford and Susie Lee
evidence.what_it_shows: Her bipartisan bill would let SBA 7(a) loans pay for AI tools, cloud services and business software, showing she wants small firms to adopt AI, not be walled off from it.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Lee favors specific fixes rather than sweeping Big Tech crackdowns: she cosponsored bills making dating apps warn users about banned scammers, requiring social media companies to report fentanyl sales, and expanding platform reporting of child abuse, and she voted for the 2024 TikTok divestiture law. No calls for breakups or repealing Section 230 were found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 2481, Romance Scam Prevention Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs a rule forcing dating apps to warn users when a match was removed for being a scammer.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 6259, No Fentanyl on Social Media Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports new duties on social media companies to report and crack down on drug sales on their platforms.

data_centers.label: Pause or block
data_centers.summary: She sponsors the House AI Data Center Moratorium Act, which would halt new data centers and expansions until Congress passes AI safety, worker and utility-cost protections. She has also pressed EPA over water damage near Meta's Georgia campus, joined a letter to FERC on grid costs, and secured a DOE study of data centers' effect on electric bills.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act (H.R. 9442)
evidence.what_it_shows: She leads the House bill to pause new data centers and expansions, the companion to Sen. Sanders' S. 4214.

evidence.title: Press release: Ocasio-Cortez introduces House version of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act
evidence.quote: Congress has a moral obligation to stand with the American people and stop the expansion of these data centers until we have a framework to adequately address the existential harm AI poses to our society.
evidence.what_it_shows: In her own words, she wants construction stopped until federal safeguards on safety, workers and utility prices are in place.

evidence.title: E&C Oversight hearing remarks: presses EPA's Jessica Kramer on data center construction and drinking water
evidence.quote: They now rely on bottled water to drink and prepare meals, and nearby residents' water bills are expected to increase by 33%.
evidence.what_it_shows: After visiting Meta's Georgia data center campus she asked EPA to investigate water harm and criticized executive orders fast-tracking construction.

evidence.title: Mullin-led letter of 20 House Democrats to FERC, Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs
evidence.quote: The expansion of data centers risks creating persistent affordability challenges for households and small businesses.
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed a letter asking regulators and the industry how grid upgrade costs will be kept off household bills.

evidence.title: Press release: Ocasio-Cortez secures DOE study on impact of AI data centers on electric bills
evidence.quote: Electric bills across the country are already skyrocketing, and increased energy demand from Big Tech data centers may only make it harder for people to afford their electric bills and keep the lights on.
evidence.what_it_shows: Before backing a moratorium she pushed ratepayer-protection steps such as a federal study of demand response and load flexibility.

evidence.title: Markey-McClellan bicameral letter to EPA urging withdrawal of proposed rule letting data centers and power plants begin construction before air permits
evidence.what_it_shows: Sixteen lawmakers told EPA to withdraw its May 2026 proposal redefining 'begin actual construction' so data centers and fossil plants can pour foundations and install wiring before New Source Review permits, saying it turns the Clean Air Act's preconstruction safeguards 'on its head.'

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: She calls AI an existential harm to society and wants data center construction paused until binding federal safety rules exist. She has warned that AI chatbots are driving suicides and psychosis, called the AI investment boom a bubble that should get no bailout, and leads the DEFIANCE Act against sexual deepfakes. She has also backed public AI research infrastructure.

evidence.title: Press release: Ocasio-Cortez introduces House version of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act
evidence.quote: stop the expansion of these data centers until we have a framework to adequately address the existential harm AI poses to our society. We must choose humanity over profit.
evidence.what_it_shows: She ties a construction pause to binding rules that make AI safe and effective before harmful products are released.

evidence.title: E&C Oversight hearing remarks on AI chatbots and the economic threat from the AI bubble
evidence.quote: Many of the stories that we've heard today about the deadly consequences of some of these AI chat bots are pretty extreme and horrifying. We're talking about suicidality.
evidence.what_it_shows: She links chatbot harms to companies' pressure to profit, warns of a 2008-style bubble and says there should be no bailout if it pops.

evidence.title: Sponsor: DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (H.R. 3562)
evidence.what_it_shows: She leads the House bill letting victims sue over AI sexual deepfakes; it passed the Senate unanimously.

evidence.title: Press conference with Rep. Laurel Lee and Paris Hilton urging House passage of the DEFIANCE Act
evidence.quote: It is not enough to take down content; we need to give victims a civil right of action.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants liability for deepfake makers on top of the TAKE IT DOWN Act's removal rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (H.R. 5511)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports mandatory bias and harm testing of automated decision systems with FTC reporting.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (H.R. 6356)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning discriminatory AI and requiring pre- and post-deployment audits.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: CREATE AI Act of 2023 (H.R. 5077, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed a national public compute and data resource so researchers, not only big companies, can build AI; she is not against AI research itself.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: She wants to break up Big Tech. In June 2026 she said Congress should pass antitrust legislation to break up large technology companies after Apple raised prices, she co-signed the letter pressing Delta on AI-driven ticket pricing, and she cosponsors a bill banning AI-driven price and wage discrimination.

evidence.title: Washington Examiner report on her Fox News interview calling to break up tech giants after Apple price hikes
evidence.quote: said Congress should pursue antitrust legislation to “break up” large technology companies after Apple significantly raised prices on its products.
evidence.what_it_shows: A reporter's summary of her televised remarks; The Hill, New York Post, Fox News and The Independent reported the same call, but those pages could not be opened.

evidence.title: García and Nadler-led letter of 24 House Democrats demanding answers from Delta's CEO on AI ticket pricing (co-signer)
evidence.quote: this move could drive up prices for consumers and result in individualized, surveillance-based price discrimination
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a demand for transparency about generative AI pricing in a concentrated industry.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 (H.R. 4640)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning companies from using AI and personal data to charge people different prices or pay different wages.

evidence.title: Ocasio-Cortez and Laurel Lee press conference with Paris Hilton urging House passage of the DEFIANCE Act
evidence.what_it_shows: After the Senate passed the DEFIANCE Act unanimously, the bipartisan House co-leads and survivors publicly pressed Speaker Johnson to bring the deepfake civil-remedy bill to the floor.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: She opposes federal preemption of state AI laws. She signed the November 2025 letter from 81 House Democrats against reviving the moratorium, and at a December 2025 hearing she called the Republican moratorium push and Trump's executive order a story of corruption driven by AI company lobbying.

evidence.title: E&C Oversight hearing remarks on Trump and Republican efforts to ban states from regulating AI
evidence.quote: And the reason that these AI tech giants are lobbying for a ban on state-level regulations is because they know that they don't want to fight these regulations in all 50 states.
evidence.what_it_shows: She defends state AI laws on child safety and public health and says the executive order blocking them endangers lives.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter of 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned preemption executive order (signer)
evidence.quote: We write to express our strong opposition to any effort in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)
evidence.what_it_shows: Her name appears among the 81 signers telling congressional leaders not to revive the state AI law moratorium or override states by executive order.

evidence.title: House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence final report (118th Congress) - Federal Preemption of State Law chapter
evidence.what_it_shows: The 24-member bipartisan task force found that preempting state AI laws 'is complex,' has 'benefits and drawbacks,' can be done via floors or ceilings, and must use precise definitions; its only preemption recommendation was that Congress commission a study of existing federal and state AI regulations. data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Hawley is the Missouri delegation's loudest critic of data center power costs. He says data centers are fine if they create jobs, but wants a binding law forcing them to pay for their own electricity and water, and he sponsors the GRID Act to keep them off the regular grid.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley and Blumenthal introduce the GRID Act (S.3852) to stop data centers from raising consumer electricity bills
evidence.quote: American families should not have to shoulder the burden of the rising electricity costs produced by data centers in Missouri and across the country. This is unacceptable
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would bar consumer rate increases tied to data centers, give households grid priority, and require new data centers to use off-grid power.

evidence.title: St. Louis Public Radio interview: Hawley says ratepayers should not subsidize data centers
evidence.quote: If data centers are going to come into the state, fine. If they're going to create jobs? Hey, wonderful. But if they're going to suck up a bunch of electricity, they need to pay for that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He does not oppose data centers outright but conditions them on paying their own way, putting him at odds with Gov. Kehoe and Rep. Jason Smith.

evidence.title: Letter to Ameren CEO demanding answers on rate hikes, shut-offs and data center deals
evidence.quote: I am concerned Ameren is seeking dramatic rate increases in order to supply massive data centers and industrial users.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed Missouri's largest utility on whether residential customers are cross-subsidizing data center contracts.

evidence.title: Warren-Hawley letter to the Energy Information Administration seeking mandatory data center energy reporting
evidence.quote: Comprehensive information regarding the operations of data centers and other large loads is essential for accurate grid planning and will support policymaking to prevent large companies from increasing electricity costs for American families
evidence.what_it_shows: A left-right push for mandatory disclosure so the public can check whether data centers pay their share.

evidence.title: Missourinet: Hawley wants Trump's ratepayer protection pledge written into law
evidence.quote: I think we ought to say in the law that the data centers have to pay for their own electricity, the data centers have to pay for their own water supply.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats the White House's voluntary pledge as insufficient and wants binding law covering both power and water.

evidence.title: Free Press op-ed: AI Will Control Us If We Do Not Control It (cites the Festus, Mo. data center fight)
evidence.quote: The companies building these facilities can afford to supply their own power, protect residential rates, and safeguard local water. We must hold them to that with binding legal requirements, not hollow promises.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames data centers as a cost shifted onto working families and demands legally binding conditions.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Hawley wants binding rules now. He sponsors mandatory federal safety testing of the most powerful AI models, product liability for AI harms, a ban on AI companions for minors, and AI layoff reporting, and in Sept. 2026 he opened a Senate probe of OpenAI citing existential risk.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley and Blumenthal introduce the Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act (S.2938)
evidence.quote: This bipartisan legislation would guarantee common-sense testing and oversight of the most advanced AI systems, so Congress and the American people can be better informed about potential risks
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would make advanced AI systems go through a mandatory Energy Department evaluation program before release.

evidence.title: Press release and letter: Chairman Hawley launches investigation into OpenAI for the Hugging Face hack and existential risk of AI products
evidence.quote: My investigation will probe this AI hacking incident, along with growing allegations of the existential risk of new AI products.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats frontier AI as a potential existential danger and is using subcommittee oversight powers on a leading lab.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Hawley reacts to Trump executive order setting voluntary cyber reviews of advanced AI
evidence.quote: I would go farther. I think we ought to enact my legislation that I have with Senator [Richard] Blumenthal that would make that sort of reporting and monitoring mandatory
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the order but said voluntary review is not enough and mandatory testing should be law.

evidence.title: Axios AI+DC Summit: Hawley pushes ban on AI chatbots for minors (GUARD Act, S.3062)
evidence.quote: The first thing we need to do is we need to pass legislation that would prevent AI chatbots from targeting minor children
evidence.what_it_shows: His GUARD Act, which the Judiciary Committee later passed 22-0, would ban AI companions for minors and add criminal penalties for chatbots that sexualize children.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI LEAD Act (S.2937), product liability for AI systems
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs letting people hurt by AI sue the developer like any other defective product.

evidence.title: Sponsor: AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act (S.3108)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require companies to report AI-driven layoffs to the government.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI Whistleblower Protection Act (S.1792)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports legal protection for AI company employees who report safety problems.

evidence.title: Blumenthal-Hawley Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act (licensing regime, liability, transparency)
evidence.quote: Congress must act on AI regulation, and these principles should form the backbone
evidence.what_it_shows: As far back as 2023 he proposed licensing sophisticated general-purpose models through an independent oversight body.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley warns 'AI threatens the working man' at NatCon 5
evidence.quote: millions of Americans out of work. That's not any conspiracy theory, by the way. That's what the tech titans openly tell us.
evidence.what_it_shows: He casts AI as a threat to jobs and liberty and says protecting children should be the lodestar for guardrails.

evidence.title: Washington Examiner: Public First Action launches $15 million project featuring Hawley among pro-guardrail Republicans
evidence.what_it_shows: An AI safety group is spending to promote him, along with Sens. Cotton and Moody and Rep. Donalds, as Republicans who back AI guardrails.

evidence.title: Hawley op-ed, 'AI Will Control Us If We Do Not Control It' (The Free Press)
evidence.what_it_shows: Hawley argued the federal government must set binding rules on AI jobs impacts, data centers and child safety, that AI 'is a question of self-government' that 'cannot be left to' Silicon Valley, and that the final stake is 'the conquest of some men by other men.'

evidence.title: Hawley, Blumenthal and Padilla remarks at Senate Judiciary markup of the GUARD Act (22-0 vote)
evidence.what_it_shows: At the unanimous committee vote to ban AI companions for minors, Hawley said a beneficial AI age 'is a choice, not an inevitability,' Blumenthal predicted tech companies would fight the bill 'with armies of lawyers and lobbyists,' and Padilla said he would keep refining one section.

evidence.title: Hawley document-request letters to Character.AI, Google, Meta, OpenAI and Snap on AI chatbot policies after Judiciary subcommittee hearing
evidence.what_it_shows: Following his Sept 16, 2025 hearing with parents of children who died after chatbot interactions, Hawley demanded all communications about the companies' AI chatbot policies.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

evidence.title: Hawley letter to Mark Zuckerberg launching Judiciary subcommittee investigation into Meta AI chatbots and children
evidence.what_it_shows: Hawley demanded Meta preserve and produce all versions of its 'GenAI: Content Risk Standards' by Sept 19, 2025, after reports its rules allowed chatbots to have 'romantic' and 'sensual' exchanges with children.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: A longtime Big Tech antagonist. He cosponsors sunsetting Section 230, sponsors STOP CSAM and a bill letting people sue AI companies over use of their data and creative work, backs the Kids Online Safety Act, and asked the Supreme Court to narrow Section 230.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Sunset Section 230 Act (S.3546)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would end platforms' liability shield and force Congress to write new rules.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley files amicus brief urging Supreme Court to hear Doe v. X Corp. and narrow Section 230
evidence.quote: Senator Hawley argued that lower courts have distorted Section 230 far beyond its original purpose
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants platforms that knowingly host child sexual abuse material to face civil liability.

evidence.title: Sponsor: STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (S.1829)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would let victims sue platforms that fail to remove child abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms serving minors.

evidence.title: Sponsor: AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act (S.2367)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would let people sue AI companies that train on their personal data or creative work without permission.

evidence.title: Hawley letter to Mark Zuckerberg opening Senate Judiciary subcommittee investigation into Meta AI chatbots' 'romantic' and 'sensual' exchanges with children
evidence.what_it_shows: After Reuters reported Meta's internal AI rules allowed chatbots to flirt with children, Sen. Hawley demanded Meta preserve and hand over documents and announced a formal investigation by the Crime and Counterterrorism Subcommittee he chairs.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

evidence.title: Grassley, Blackburn, Hawley letter to Zuckerberg on Meta's emotional targeting of teens and alleged COPPA violations
evidence.what_it_shows: The Judiciary Committee chairman and two members demanded answers on a 2014 Facebook study of teens' emotional triggers for ads and on FTC allegations that Meta let under-13s onto Horizon Worlds without parental consent.

evidence.title: Hawley document requests to Character.AI, Google, Meta, OpenAI and Snap on AI chatbot policies after Judiciary subcommittee hearing
evidence.what_it_shows: Following testimony from parents whose children died after chatbot interactions, Hawley demanded five companies turn over all communications about their chatbot policies by Oct 17, 2025, writing 'children are dead. Families are broken.'

evidence.title: Hawley and Durbin letter to Roblox CEO opening Judiciary subcommittee investigation into child sexual abuse on Roblox
evidence.what_it_shows: The subcommittee chair and Judiciary ranking member told Roblox it 'appears to prioritize revenue and engagement metrics over the safety and well-being of our children,' cited 65,381 suspected exploitation reports in 2025, and directed it to preserve all child-safety records.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Hawley opposed the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws in the 2025 budget bill, said he would offer an amendment to strip it, and cheered when a preemption provision was dropped from the NDAA, calling it a terrible provision that should stay out.

evidence.title: The Hill: AI moratorium sparks GOP battle over states' rights (Hawley says he will move to strip it)
evidence.quote: I'm only for AI if it's good for the people
evidence.what_it_shows: Weeks before the vote he told reporters he would introduce an amendment to eliminate the state-law moratorium if it was not removed first.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to remove the moratorium, consistent with his stated plan to do so himself. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: The Hill: Hawley applauds decision to drop AI preemption provision from the NDAA (X post)
evidence.quote: Good. This is a terrible provision and should remain OUT
evidence.what_it_shows: Direct opposition to federal preemption of state AI laws, breaking with President Trump's push for one national standard.

evidence.title: Sen. Josh Hawley X post after preemption was dropped from the NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: Hawley posted 'Good. This is a terrible provision and should remain OUT.'

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: A chip hawk. He wrote a bill to decouple U.S. AI from China, cosponsors the Chip Security Act, and said he wants to reduce, not increase, China's access to American hardware after Trump approved Nvidia H200 sales, while saying the president deserves some deference.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act (S.321)

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Chip Security Act (S.1705)

evidence.title: CNBC: Trump's blessing of Nvidia H200 sales to China gets a chilly reception from GOP
evidence.quote: if we want to beat China, I think we need to constrain their ability to leverage our own technology, and I think we would want to reduce their access to our hardware, not increase it.
evidence.what_it_shows: He questioned the H200 deal while stopping short of directly criticizing Trump.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (S.4429)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning connected-car technology from China and other adversaries.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Golden is the lead Democrat on the SPEED Act, a bill to speed federal permitting for energy and infrastructure that backers tie to the AI buildout, and he says he would go even further by deeming projects approved if the government misses deadlines. He frames it as building power and cutting costs while protecting the environment. He has not spoken about data centers or Maine's moratorium directly and did not answer a question on a national pause.

evidence.title: Press release: Golden introduces permitting reform bill with Natural Resources Chairman Westerman (SPEED Act)
evidence.quote: America must get back into the business of building. We need modern infrastructure. We need robust power production that does not discriminate between energy sources.
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the primary Democratic cosponsor of the bill and casts faster permitting as the way to more power and lower prices; Westerman's quote in the same release ties it to the AI race.

evidence.title: House roll call #356 (2025): passage of H.R.4776, the SPEED Act (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: One of 11 Democrats who voted for the permitting overhaul that passed 221 to 196. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Press release: Golden's bipartisan permitting reform bill passes House
evidence.quote: The simplest way to make energy, housing, and other essentials more affordable is to make it possible to actually produce enough of it at a reasonable cost. America's broken permitting system is standing in the way,
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues scarcity from slow permitting is what raises costs, the opposite framing from data center critics who blame new demand.

evidence.title: E&E News: Moderate Democrat would go tougher on permitting
evidence.quote: deeming projects approved if the government can't get their ducks in a row in a certain amount of time.
evidence.what_it_shows: He told E&E he was at times willing to be more aggressive than the Republican chairman on permitting.

evidence.title: Maine Public: Maine groups join call for U.S. data center moratorium (delegation asked for comment)
evidence.what_it_shows: His office did not respond when asked about a proposed national data center moratorium.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Murphy is a strong data center booster. At an August 2026 constituent meeting in Snow Hill he said data centers are wrongly treated as 'the boogeyman', that America needs them to beat China on AI, and that water and energy worries are 15 years out of date. He did not cast a vote on the SPEED Act permitting bill.

evidence.title: Reported remarks at Snow Hill meet-and-greet (Derek Burress newsletter): data centers and the AI race with China
evidence.quote: And data centers are the boogeyman. But if we don't have some way of computing all that artificial intelligence, we can't compete with them.
evidence.what_it_shows: He raised data centers on his own and framed them as essential national security infrastructure in the AI race with China, saying China spreads disinformation about them.

evidence.title: Reported remarks at Snow Hill meet-and-greet: modern data centers use water like a car wash
evidence.quote: The concerns I think were valid 15 years ago, entirely different from what we're doing now,
evidence.what_it_shows: He dismissed water and energy concerns as outdated, saying modern facilities are self-contained, use about as much water as a car wash, and that operators pledged not to raise local rates.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (permitting reform), Murphy recorded as No Vote
evidence.what_it_shows: He was absent for the House vote on the permitting reform bill that other members' data center positions are often judged by. Recorded vote: Not Voting.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Murphy, a surgeon, wants specific guardrails on AI in health care: he asked the FDA for a regulatory framework in 2024, sponsored a 2026 bill to independently audit the VA's AI systems, and co-led a bill to stop Medicare Advantage insurers from using AI to deny claims. At the same time he frames AI as a race with China that America must win. Leans toward targeted rules.

evidence.title: Press release: Murphy co-introduces Protecting Patients from Automated Denials Act on AI in Medicare Advantage prior authorization
evidence.quote: I am proud to lead on this issue by establishing sensible guardrails that ensure the proliferation of AI in the field of medicine does no harm.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants binding rules on how insurers use AI: disclosure of AI use, physician review, ten-year record retention and reports to HHS, saying insurers must not use AI to deny care.

evidence.title: Press release: Murphy letter to FDA Commissioner on artificial intelligence regulation in health care
evidence.quote: We must be judicious in cultivating a regulatory environment that both protects consumers and encourages innovation.
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked the FDA to prepare a regulatory framework for AI in medicine and said consensus and guardrails must be laid out first, while praising AI's potential.

evidence.title: H.R. 9862 Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill directs the VA to commission an independent evaluation of the AI systems used by the Veterans Health Administration, a modest oversight measure.

evidence.title: Reported remarks at Snow Hill meet-and-greet: AI as a battle with China
evidence.quote: We're in a battle with artificial intelligence. Fortunately, we're ahead right now. But if they ever get ahead, our world changes completely,
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI mainly as a race with China that the US must win, a light-touch framing that sits alongside his health care guardrails.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: His only located tech-regulation action is national security focused: he voted for and praised the 2024 law forcing TikTok to split from its Chinese owner. No statements found on Section 230, antitrust, privacy law or kids online safety.

evidence.title: Press release: Murphy votes to force TikTok to divest from China (H.R. 7521)

evidence.title: Roll call 86 (118th): H.R. 7521 Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, Murphy Yea
evidence.what_it_shows: Recorded Yea on the TikTok divestiture bill. Recorded vote: Yea.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Tiffany's record is mixed. In Congress he called AI and data centers a new era needing more coal, gas and nuclear power, and voted for the SPEED Act and the House bill with the state AI moratorium. As the GOP nominee for governor he now vows to end all data center subsidies, give towns the final say, protect ratepayers and farmland, and brands his opponent 'Data Center David,' while still opposing a moratorium.

evidence.quote: There should be no new data centers without strong standards to protect Wisconsin. If we pave over productive farmland and drive up demand on our electric grid, families will pay the price through higher food and utility costs.
evidence.what_it_shows: His campaign position is build only with strong standards for ratepayers, farmland and water.

evidence.title: Up North News: Tiffany pledges to end the state data center sales tax exemption
evidence.quote: These companies do not need to be subsidized on the back of hardworking taxpayers here in Wisconsin.
evidence.what_it_shows: He promises to repeal the tax break the Legislative Fiscal Bureau says could cost the state more than $2 billion.

evidence.quote: there should be local input. There should be local control. Local people should have a say in whether it’s being built in their community.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants communities to decide whether a data center gets built; CAP Action notes this clashes with his vote for the House AI moratorium.

evidence.title: Wisconsin Watch/NOTUS: Data centers become a flashpoint in Wisconsin politics
evidence.quote: Existing ratepayers and commercial users should not have their rates go up as a result of someone that’s coming in using massive amounts of electricity
evidence.what_it_shows: Early ratepayer-protection framing, before data centers became the center of his campaign.

evidence.title: Wisconsin Independent: Tiffany's February 2026 PBS Wisconsin remarks and August WSAW remarks
evidence.quote: I think we need to make sure on the energy side of it that we do not harm existing ratepayers, so residential ratepayers and manufacturers
evidence.what_it_shows: He called data centers an exciting new technology to be managed, and later said they are needed to keep technology from moving to China but must meet strict conditions.

evidence.title: Press release: Tiffany letter to the Wisconsin PSC demanding baseload power and no early coal plant closures
evidence.quote: This is particularly critical as we enter a new era of artificial intelligence and data centers, which require a steady supply of reliable, and low-cost energy, such as coal, natural gas, and nuclear power generation.
evidence.what_it_shows: In 2025 he treated data center growth as a reason to expand fossil and nuclear generation, a pro-buildout stance.

evidence.title: Roll call 145: Yea on H.R. 1, whose 10-year state AI moratorium critics said would have blocked local rules on data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the House bill with language CAP Action and Democrats say would have stripped the local control he now campaigns on. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.what_it_shows: An environmental PAC is spending against him, saying he voted to fast-track data centers and cut environmental review.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Kelly wants the AI buildout to continue and warned that local rejections like Chandler and Tucson could cost the US the race with China, but he says companies must work with communities up front, homeowners must not pay for the grid upgrades, and he is drafting a bill to pool money from data center companies for grid and community costs.

evidence.title: Quartz interview: Kelly on data center revolts in Chandler and Tucson
evidence.quote: I think what happened in Chandler and in Tucson shows that companies need to work with these communities upfront
evidence.what_it_shows: He accepts that communities get a say but wants developers to engage early rather than stop building.

evidence.title: Quartz interview: Kelly on local data center rejections and the China race
evidence.quote: If we see that become a trend across the country, it's going to be hard to win against China in this race to develop intelligent models
evidence.what_it_shows: He is pro-buildout and frames data centers as needed for national competitiveness, while saying locals should not pay more for electricity.

evidence.title: Broadband Breakfast: Kelly outlines his vision for AI regulation at Brookings
evidence.quote: If we can get this legislation passed...we can be part of the solution here to building the grid, so costs don't go up for homeowners
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI Horizon Fund would pool money from data center companies to pay for grid upgrades so ratepayers are not stuck with the bill; he also said tech firms arrive too late asking for the power of 50,000 homes and called Trump's ratepayer pledge a handshake deal.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Kelly wants AI to succeed and his roadmap leans on taxing AI firms rather than regulating models, but he backs a long list of specific guardrails: human responsibility for lethal military AI, congressional oversight of AI in intelligence, chatbot protections for kids and seniors, worker involvement, and pre-release risk testing. He attacked Trump for dropping even a voluntary testing order.

evidence.title: Yahoo/Benzinga: Kelly's May 22 2026 X post on Trump abandoning his AI executive order
evidence.quote: America cannot lead in AI if our policy is determined by whichever billionaire gets the President on the phone last
evidence.what_it_shows: He called it a failure when Trump dropped an order that would have set up voluntary pre-release risk assessments of frontier AI after pushback from tech executives.

evidence.title: The Hill: Gillibrand, Schiff, Warner, Coons and Kelly letter on access to advanced AI models
evidence.quote: develop a public, durable, and technically grounded framework that allows U.S. companies and their customers to understand the rules of the road
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a clear federal framework for frontier AI instead of ad hoc decisions, after OpenAI agents breached Hugging Face and Anthropic pulled models.

evidence.title: Press release: Kelly secures AI oversight provisions in the FY2027 Intelligence Authorization Act
evidence.quote: As AI takes a bigger role in our intelligence and military operations, Congress has a responsibility to understand how it's being used and build in safeguards for the American people before problems arise
evidence.what_it_shows: His amendments require reports on new AI uses, a review of AI in targeting, labeling of AI outputs, and research on AI-on-AI attacks and inadvertent escalation.

evidence.title: S.4682 Ultimate Human Responsibility in Defense Systems Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill sets requirements for human judgment in the use of force by autonomous weapon systems; verified on govtrack.

evidence.what_it_shows: Requires chatbots to disclose they are AI, bans posing as licensed professionals, limits data use and bans manipulative design aimed at seniors.

evidence.quote: But seniors need to know when they're talking to a machine, what its limits are, and how their information is being used to make sure they aren't being scammed or put at risk.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pairs praise for AI's benefits with binding disclosure and design rules.

evidence.title: S.3062 GUARD Act (cosponsored 2025-10-28)

evidence.quote: That promise will only be realized if AI is developed and deployed with meaningful worker involvement and input
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants worker-centered guardrails, collective bargaining and retraining built into federal AI policy.

evidence.quote: I want to see AI be successful. I think this is a real opportunity for the American people if we get it right
evidence.what_it_shows: He is not an AI skeptic; his concern is job displacement, and his roadmap would tax frontier AI firms that cut jobs to fund retraining and the grid.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions

But she also wrote the POWER Up Act, the first Republican bill to give federal regulators authority over how city-sized data centers connect to the grid, citing ratepayers. Her family sold about 3,500 acres near Cheyenne to Microsoft for a data center campus in June 2026.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.4806 POWER Up Act (FERC rules for 100 MW+ large-load grid connections)
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants uniform federal interconnection rules for data centers while leaving siting and retail rates to states.

evidence.what_it_shows: She treats giant data centers as a grid-wide issue needing clear rules, not a local retail matter.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Hagerty celebrates xAI's Memphis data center and wants Tennessee to become America's energy hub, using TVA nuclear power to attract AI compute and Bitcoin mining. In the interview found, he raised no conditions on ratepayer costs, water or siting. An August 2026 WBIR story headlined his discussion of data center concerns in Knoxville could not be opened.

evidence.quote: I think we've got a unique opportunity here to move forward and become the energy hub of America
evidence.what_it_shows: His answer to data center power demand is to build more nuclear generation through TVA, a build-faster stance with no ratepayer conditions mentioned.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Hagerty is mixed. In a 2023 hearing he warned against rushing federal rules on AI in campaign ads and said he did not trust the Biden administration or Congress to balance fraud concerns with free speech. Yet he cosponsors the NO FAKES Act, a binding federal right against AI voice and face clones, and his own 2026 AI bill targets Chinese theft of US models rather than domestic safety rules. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: The only AI-risk evidence cited is the 2023 Rules hearing, where Hagerty warned against 'heavy-handed regulation' of AI political content and against the impulse to 'just do something' before understanding the technology

evidence.title: Tennessee Lookout: Senate Rules hearing on AI in elections, Hagerty remarks
evidence.quote: We shouldn't immediately indulge the impulse for government to just do something, as they say, before we fully understand the impacts of the emerging technology, especially when that something encroaches on political speech.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argued Congress should be careful before regulating AI-made political content and said federal overregulation risks limiting political speech.

evidence.title: S.1367 NO FAKES Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a binding federal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice or likeness, a targeted guardrail.

evidence.title: S.4591 NO FAKES Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: He re-upped support for the revised likeness-rights bill in 2026.

evidence.title: S.5252 BLADE Act (Blocking Large-scale Adversarial Distillation Efforts Act of 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: His main AI bill treats American AI models as national-security assets to shield from foreign adversaries, not as a domestic risk to regulate.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined KOSA in October 2025, supporting a duty of care toward minors on social platforms.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Hagerty's Big Tech agenda is driven by conservative censorship complaints: in 2021 he sponsored a bill to repeal Section 230 and treat large platforms as common carriers, and he cosponsors KOSA. On financial technology he is deregulatory, cosponsoring the resolution that killed CFPB oversight of big payment apps. The mix nets out to targeted rules rather than a broad crackdown.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care and safety defaults for minors on social media, games and video sites.

evidence.title: S.J.Res.28 disapproving the CFPB rule on larger participants in digital payment apps

evidence.title: S.1974 Protecting Americans' Data From Foreign Surveillance Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would stop data brokers from selling Americans' personal data to countries like China.

preemption.label: No public position found

No statement, letter, cosponsorship or interview was found on whether federal AI law should override state laws, including after the December 2025 executive order and the March 2026 White House framework.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the AI moratorium from H.R. 1 (Yea)

In 2026 he introduced the BLADE Act to stop Chinese firms from extracting US AI models and cosponsors limits on US investment in Chinese military tech. No statement was located on the 2025-26 Nvidia H20 or H200 sales decisions.

evidence.title: S.5252 BLADE Act (Blocking Large-scale Adversarial Distillation Efforts Act of 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would block foreign adversaries from extracting key technical features of closed US AI models, introduced after Anthropic accused Alibaba of a distillation attack.

evidence.what_it_shows: Four Republicans told Raimondo before her China trip not to create a working group with Beijing on chip export controls and that China should expect more, not fewer, controls.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Wants binding but targeted federal oversight of the largest frontier AI developers (model cards, independent audits, incident reporting) to guard against catastrophic risk, and sponsored AI whistleblower protections. He pairs this with an innovation-first message and has warned against rushing to regulate or pausing AI.

evidence.title: Press release: Obernolte, Trahan introduce bipartisan FRONTIER Act to strengthen oversight of advanced AI
evidence.quote: This legislation will protect Americans from catastrophic risk, provide developers with clear rules of the road, and ensure the United States remains the global leader in AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the lead sponsor of a bill requiring transparency, independent evaluation and safety-incident reporting from the largest AI developers, explicitly aimed at catastrophic risk.

evidence.title: Press release: Obernolte, Trahan release discussion draft of the Great American AI Act
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is advancing rapidly, which is why Congress must take a thoughtful and bipartisan approach to regulating this critical technology

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 3460 AI Whistleblower Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Sponsored the House bill protecting AI company workers who report safety problems from retaliation.

evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI safety threats as real and national-security relevant, and wants insiders able to flag them.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8516 American Leadership in AI Act (Lieu-Obernolte package)
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-introduced a broad bipartisan package built on the AI Task Force report that relies on voluntary standards, testing frameworks and research infrastructure rather than mandates.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Backs targeted federal tech rules such as a national privacy law and the TAKE IT DOWN Act, but favors lighter, preemptive approaches over Senate-style mandates and warned that app-level age verification would create new privacy risks.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 633 TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported the now-enacted law criminalizing nonconsensual intimate images, including AI deepfakes, and forcing platforms to remove them.

evidence.title: Fox News interview (republished on his site): AI caucus vice chair says privacy regulations should be a priority for Congress
evidence.what_it_shows: He told Fox News that privacy regulation should be a top short-term priority for Congress as it grapples with AI, while calling himself an optimist about the technology.

preemption.label: Leans national rule
preemption.summary: The House's chief architect of a national AI standard: his Great American AI Act draft would preempt state laws on AI model development for three years and his FRONTIER Act sets a uniform national rule to prevent a state patchwork. He says states should keep a lane outside the federal one, with the federal government defining the boundary first. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: A score of 2 ('One national rule (block states)') overstates the evidence. His own words at the Jan 2026 hearing were that 'there should be a federal lane, and that there should be a state lane,' with states free to act

evidence.title: Press release: FRONTIER Act creates a uniform national standard to prevent a patchwork of state regulations
evidence.quote: It also creates a uniform national standard for transparency, auditing, and reporting of catastrophic risk to prevent a patchwork of state regulations.
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill summary says the federal rules for frontier models are meant to replace differing state rules.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Bipartisan AI draft proposes three-year preemption of state laws
evidence.what_it_shows: The Obernolte-Trahan Great American AI Act discussion draft includes a three-year preemption of state laws related to AI development.

evidence.title: Roll Call: White House holds back on national AI framework specifics (Obernolte chairs Science subcommittee hearing with OSTP's Kratsios)
evidence.quote: I think what everyone believes is that there should be a federal lane, and that there should be a state lane
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports federal preemption within a defined lane but, unlike a blanket moratorium, wants states free to act outside it; he pressed the White House on what its guardrails would be.

evidence.title: IAPP: Obernolte remarks at State of the Net on a national AI standard before a state patchwork emerges
evidence.quote: We need to get moving because, frankly, you're seeing these states act to fill the void that we've left on AI regulation at the federal level.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues Congress must set a national standard quickly so state AI laws do not multiply, the core case for preemption.

evidence.title: Press release: Great American AI Act discussion draft (co-sponsor Houchin on a national standard over fifty state laws)
evidence.what_it_shows: The release he issued describes the draft as a clear national standard for how AI models are developed while preserving the ability of states and parents to protect children.

evidence.title: Reps. Obernolte, Trahan, Franklin, Subramanyam, Houchin and Peters statements releasing the Great American AI Act discussion draft
evidence.what_it_shows: The six members framed the draft as a national standard for frontier AI development that preserves states' ability to protect children; Houchin said America should not 'regulate ourselves into falling behind China through a patchwork of fifty different state laws.'

evidence.title: House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence final report (118th Congress) - Federal Preemption of State Law chapter
evidence.what_it_shows: The 24-member bipartisan task force found that preempting state AI laws 'is complex,' has 'benefits and drawbacks,' can be done via floors or ceilings, and must use precise definitions; its only preemption recommendation was that Congress commission a study of existing federal and state AI regulations. It did not endorse a moratorium.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls

No speeches or statements on Nvidia H20/H200 sales were found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3447 Chip Security Act

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Jacobs wants binding federal AI rules now. She sponsors bills to let agencies write enforceable AI rules, to test the most advanced models for nuclear and catastrophic risks, to track Pentagon AI failures, and to keep humans in control of lethal and nuclear decisions. She pairs this with language about encouraging innovation.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs and Maloy introduce the ATOMIC Act to test advanced AI for nuclear risks
evidence.quote: As AI becomes more powerful, we have a responsibility to identify and guard against new risks before they become real-world threats.
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs a mandatory Energy Department program to test frontier models from the largest developers for deception, guardrail bypass, and nuclear-related dangers, and calls these guardrails a first step against worst-case scenarios.

evidence.title: H.R. 9965, AI Threat Output and Monitoring Incident Containment (ATOMIC) Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-lead of a bill requiring evaluation of the most advanced AI systems for nuclear-related risks and containment protocols.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs introduces the Sectoral AI Governance Act
evidence.quote: My Sectoral AI Governance Act gives federal agencies clearer authority to write and enforce rules when AI is used to break existing federal laws.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants every federal agency to write binding rules for AI in the sector it already oversees, a comprehensive regulatory framework rather than voluntary standards.

evidence.title: H.R. 9125, Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Lead sponsor of a bill giving agencies authority to issue AI rules whenever AI is likely to contribute to violations of existing law.

evidence.title: Press release: Beyer, Barrett, Jacobs introduce the Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act
evidence.quote: AI mistakes on the battlefield have the potential to be catastrophic: civilian casualties, friendly fire, unintended escalation, and calculations made on faulty data
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants a legal requirement that a human decision-maker stay in the loop before any AI-enabled weapon uses lethal force.

evidence.title: H.R. 9729, Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-lead of a bill requiring meaningful human control over lethal autonomous weapons.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs introduces bipartisan bill to address AI weaknesses and failures at the Pentagon
evidence.quote: when AI fails at the Pentagon, the consequences can be deadly and could even pull the United States into a war
evidence.what_it_shows: She treats military AI failures as potentially catastrophic and wants a department-wide incident and vulnerability reporting program; the provision passed the House in the FY27 NDAA.

evidence.title: H.R. 10189, Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Lead sponsor of a bill making the Pentagon track and fix AI incidents and report to Congress.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs and Lieu praise inclusion of provision preventing autonomous AI from launching nuclear weapons in the FY25 NDAA
evidence.quote: AI should never have the final say in deploying nuclear weapons, which pose one of the biggest threats to human life
evidence.what_it_shows: She authored the committee amendment that put a human-in-the-loop requirement for nuclear launches into the defense bill, citing AI's escalatory behavior in war games.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs on the Bipartisan AI Task Force final report
evidence.quote: This is our opportunity to strike the right balance that encourages innovation and American leadership, while also creating guardrails that protect our rights and safety.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows her framing: guardrails on rights and safety paired with support for innovation, plus a push to empower sectoral regulators.

evidence.title: H.R. 5511, Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports mandatory bias and harm testing of automated decision systems with reporting to the FTC.

evidence.title: H.R. 8094, AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring large AI developers to disclose training data and testing.

evidence.title: H.R. 9477, AI Incident Reporting Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a system for reporting AI accidents and harms.

evidence.title: Fortune report quoting Jacobs's joint press release on the AI Tax and Work Protection Act (H.R. 10044)
evidence.quote: If Congress does nothing, the rise of AI could create the biggest wealth transfer in history from the bottom to the top
evidence.what_it_shows: She co-introduced a bill taxing AI companies, with rates rising if unemployment climbs, to fund jobs for displaced workers.

evidence.title: H.R. 10044, AI Tax and Work Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-lead of a bill taxing companies that replace workers with AI.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs, Horsford, Moylan introduce the AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act
evidence.quote: We know that AI will rapidly transform our economy and our workforce, but we don't yet know when, how, or to what extent.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants large employers to report AI-driven layoffs to the Labor Department so Congress can legislate on job losses.

evidence.title: H.R. 9352, AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-lead of a bill requiring disclosure of AI-related layoffs.

evidence.title: Press release (Obernolte site): Obernolte and Jacobs introduce the Economy of the Future Commission Act
evidence.quote: I'm constantly hearing from young people who are absolutely terrified that AI will take their jobs and make their degrees irrelevant.
evidence.what_it_shows: Bipartisan work with the House AI Task Force chair on a commission to study AI's labor-market effects, showing she also works across the aisle on study-first measures.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: She backs targeted privacy rules, such as protecting reproductive health data and stopping warrantless purchases of location data, and has called for comprehensive privacy law and guardrails for social media. But she voted against the 2024 TikTok divest-or-ban bill, calling it a blunt instrument and a free-speech risk.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs votes against the TikTok ban (H.R. 7521)
evidence.quote: Instead, we need comprehensive data privacy legislation, alongside thoughtful guardrails for social media platforms
evidence.what_it_shows: She favors privacy law and platform guardrails over app bans, and warned the TikTok bill would expand government power to ban apps and harm civil liberties.

evidence.title: H.R. 3420 (118th), My Body, My Data Act of 2023

evidence.title: H.R. 4639 (118th), Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act

evidence.title: H.R. 3218, Reproductive Data Privacy and Protection Act

evidence.what_it_shows: After Grok's antisemitic posts, she urged robust, transparent safeguards from AI and social media companies, a call for platform accountability short of new binding law.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Strong opponent of federal preemption of state AI laws. She co-led the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal Trump's December 2025 executive order, signed both House Democratic letters against an AI moratorium, and praised states like California for acting where Congress has not.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs blasts Trump's executive order to block state-level AI laws
evidence.quote: This executive order is deeply misguided, wildly corrupt, and will actually hinder innovation and weaken public trust in the long run.
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed the December 2025 preemption order, credited states with addressing deepfakes, election disinformation, and unsafe chatbots, and vowed to fight it in the courts and Congress.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs, Beyer, Matsui, Lieu, McClain Delaney introduce the GUARDRAILS Act
evidence.quote: President Trump's laissez-faire approach to AI regulation and trampling on states' AI rights is incredibly dangerous for Americans' rights and safety
evidence.what_it_shows: She co-led the House bill to block the executive order and criticized the March 2026 White House framework for preempting states without enforceable federal guardrails.

evidence.title: H.R. 8031, GUARDRAILS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Original co-lead of the bill protecting states' right to enforce their own AI laws.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order
evidence.quote: our strong opposition to any effort in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would reintroduce a sweeping moratorium on the ability of states and local governments to enforce their own artificial intelligence (AI) laws
evidence.what_it_shows: Jacobs is one of the 81 signers telling congressional leaders not to revive the state AI-law moratorium or override states by executive order or by withholding broadband funds.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: Jacobs is listed among the 44 signers asking defense-bill negotiators to keep any preemption of state AI laws out of the NDAA.

evidence.title: Reps. Beyer, Matsui, Lieu, Jacobs and McClain Delaney statements introducing the GUARDRAILS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Beyer said the White House 'aims to kill state AI laws without setting even minimally acceptable federal guardrails'; Lieu said 'any attempt by Donald Trump to create laws through executive order is a sham.'

evidence.title: House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence final report (118th Congress) - Federal Preemption of State Law chapter
evidence.what_it_shows: The 24-member bipartisan task force found that preempting state AI laws 'is complex,' has 'benefits and drawbacks,' can be done via floors or ceilings, and must use precise definitions; its only preemption recommendation was that Congress commission a study of existing federal and state AI regulations. It did not endorse a moratorium.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: No statements on data centers found as of Sept 2026. He is an original cosponsor of the House Democrats' Energy Bills Relief Act, which would make data centers and other very large power users pay for the grid upgrades they cause, and he has fought Con Edison rate hikes.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: Energy Bills Relief Act (H.R.7977), the House Democratic energy affordability package
evidence.what_it_shows: Section 603 of the bill makes large load facilities such as data centers their own customer class that must fully pay for grid upgrades built to serve them, so his cosponsorship leans toward protecting ratepayers.

evidence.title: Voted Nay on the SPEED Act permitting reform bill (House roll call 356)
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed the Republican permitting overhaul that backers say would speed energy and data center construction; a party-line vote, so a weak signal on its own. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Mixed but leaning toward targeted rules. His own 2023 bill would require a disclaimer on all AI-generated content and he called managing AI's existential risks a central challenge for Congress, while warning against over-regulation. In 2025 he cosponsored a bill letting financial firms test AI with some rules waived, and the AI industry super PAC backed his 2026 primary.

evidence.title: Press release: Torres introduces the AI Disclosure Act of 2023 requiring a disclaimer on AI-generated material
evidence.quote: Carefully crafting a regulatory framework for managing the existential risks of AI will be one of the central challenges confronting Congress in the years and decades to come. There is danger in both under-regulating and over-regulating.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI as a serious risk and wants a federal regulatory framework, starting with mandatory disclosure enforced by the FTC, but says over-regulation is also a danger.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act (H.R.4801)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed a regulatory sandbox letting banks and other financial firms test AI projects with some normal rules turned off, a lighter-touch signal.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act (H.R.8858, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported banning AI-made fake media meant to trick voters, a targeted guardrail.

evidence.title: AI Money Watch and Transformer trackers: Leading the Future endorsed Torres; its Think Big arm spent $1.12 million supporting him in the NY-15 primary
evidence.what_it_shows: The industry-funded super PAC network that fights strict AI regulation chose to back him, which suggests it sees him as friendly to a lighter-touch approach; this is the PAC's view, not his own statement.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter: Leading the Future backs Democratic incumbents including Torres
evidence.quote: Leading the Future has also backed Democratic incumbents, like Reps. Richie Torres (D., N.Y.), Val Hoyle (D., Ore.), and Rob Menendez (D., N.J.).
evidence.what_it_shows: Independent confirmation that the pro-industry AI super PAC supported his re-election.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Supports targeted rules: he cosponsored the Kids Online Safety Act, the TikTok divest-or-ban law, a reproductive health data privacy bill and a 2026 bill pushing face-scan age checks to keep kids off adult products. He voted against the House Republican kids online safety package in June 2026, though I did not find his own explanation.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (H.R.7891, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed a duty-of-care law requiring platforms to protect kids from harmful content and addictive design.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (H.R.7521, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a ban.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Facial Recognition to Protect Children Act (H.R.9706)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed pushing online services to use face-scan age checks to keep children out of adult accounts.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: My Body, My Data Act (H.R.3420, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported limits on how apps collect and share reproductive health data.

evidence.title: Voted Nay on the KIDS Act, the House Republican kids online safety package (House roll call 228)
evidence.what_it_shows: He was among 85 Democrats who voted against the package; most Democratic opponents said it lacked a duty of care and was too soft on platforms, but I found no statement from Torres explaining his vote. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: Press release: Torres files the Social Media Bank Run Act after the Silicon Valley Bank collapse
evidence.quote: Digital platforms enable financial panic to spread on a scale and at a pace we've never before seen
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants federal regulators to monitor social media for signs of bank runs, a narrow new oversight role rather than broad platform regulation.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026. I checked the Nov 2025 Matsui letter (81 signers) and the Dec 2025 Clarke letter (44 signers) against state AI law preemption; he signed neither, and I found no statement on the Dec 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework.

evidence.title: Voted Nay on House passage of H.R.1, which then contained the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws (House roll call 145)
evidence.what_it_shows: A party-line vote against the whole Republican budget bill; it does not by itself show a view on state AI law preemption. Recorded vote: Nay.

A fact-checker adjusted this reading: The only China-related source is a CFIUS letter about a PRC-linked buyer acquiring iRobot (inbound investment and consumer data), not semiconductor export controls. data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Bentz says Oregon will run short of power as data centers and electrification grow, and his answer is to build faster: permitting reform, more transmission, nuclear power and, in his words at an AI hearing, waiving environmental rules. He voted for the SPEED Act. He has not proposed conditions on data centers themselves.

evidence.title: Bend Bulletin: Bentz warns of future power shortfall in Oregon, calls for changes to energy policy
evidence.quote: I asked them directly if they have enough power to meet demand around here. And the answer was no.
evidence.what_it_shows: He cites Prineville data centers among the drivers of a looming shortage and wants Oregon to lift its nuclear restrictions and speed transmission.

evidence.title: Bend Bulletin: Bentz on permitting reform
evidence.quote: If we don’t streamline permitting, we’re not going to build what we need in time.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs federal permitting changes to speed power lines and generation to meet data center-driven demand.

evidence.title: House roll call 356: passage of H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the NEPA permitting overhaul meant to accelerate energy and infrastructure projects. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: KOBI-TV: Congressman Bentz urges passage of SPEED Act in light of energy shortfalls
evidence.quote: We need about as much power in the future as we have today and we need it really soon, so that means we have to about double the amount we have in the Northwest
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants the Senate to pass permitting reform, citing a 9-gigawatt Northwest shortfall and maxed-out transmission.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: House Energy and Commerce hearing on AI's role in energy and climate (Bentz remarks)
evidence.quote: We need to waive environmental rules, we need to push things aside. We need to create exemptions. We need to get past this haystack of obstacles that we created for ourselves to protect things.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argued for clearing environmental and permitting obstacles to build AI energy infrastructure quickly.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Bentz frames AI as an existential race the United States must win against China and wants obstacles cleared, not new mandates. At a May 2025 hearing he called consumer protection serious but steered toward how AI is funded, and he has not backed AI safety rules.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: House Energy and Commerce hearing on AI's role in energy and climate (Bentz on winning the race)
evidence.quote: Why It's absolutely essential that we win this race to a goal that's not as clear as I would like.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called AI competition with China an existential issue and asked witnesses to make the public case for it.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: House subcommittee hearing on AI Regulation and the Future of US Leadership (Bentz remarks)
evidence.quote: the question about consumer protection is interesting and serious and I'm happy for our discussion of it
evidence.what_it_shows: At the hearing that launched Republicans' national AI framework push, he focused on how the trillions invested in AI get funded and whether smaller players can compete, not on new rules.

tech_regulation.label: Mixed

Bentz sponsors a bipartisan bill ordering an FTC study of social media's effects on kids and joined the 2021 GOP task force on reining in Big Tech, but he stresses caution about government action and in 2021 amended a House antitrust bill to make it friendlier to innovation.

evidence.title: H.R.6290 Safe Social Media Act
