evidence.title: Press release: Bentz's Safe Social Media Act passes Energy and Commerce subcommittee
evidence.quote: This Act will require a study that will gather the data necessary to learn how and what social media is impacting our children. My bill is a necessary step toward real accountability.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants data on harms to kids first, calling the study a step toward accountability rather than proposing mandates.

evidence.title: Press release: Bentz appointed to GOP Task Force on Big Tech Censorship and Data
evidence.quote: we must make sure government actions are carefully considered as we weigh many subjects, including: free speech, innovation, data privacy, national security, and the welfare of consumers
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a Republican effort to rein in Big Tech but urged caution, and his amendment to a 2021 antitrust bill made it more supportive of innovation.

data_centers.label: Pause or block
data_centers.summary: Mace called for a one-year moratorium on new data center construction in South Carolina in May 2026 and renewed it in July 2026, saying data centers must pay their own way or not come. This is a reversal from January 2025, when she praised Trump's $500 billion Stargate data center plan, and she voted for the SPEED Act permitting bill in December 2025.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Nancy Mace Calls For One-Year Moratorium On New Data Centers In South Carolina
evidence.quote: South Carolina is not Big Tech's personal power grid
evidence.what_it_shows: She asked for a statewide pause on new data centers so lawmakers can require the companies to cover all energy and grid upgrade costs.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Nancy Mace Renews Call for One-Year Moratorium as New Report Ranks South Carolina Among Top States for AI Data Center Deals
evidence.quote: The moratorium sets the terms for what comes next: data centers pay their own way, or they don't come here
evidence.what_it_shows: She repeated the moratorium call and tied it to grid, water and family bill impacts as AI data center interest in the state grew.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Nancy Mace Statement on President Donald Trump's Investment in Artificial Intelligence Technology (Stargate)
evidence.quote: Building out state-of-the-art data centers and ensuring we lead the global AI race will drive innovation, create jobs, and keep us competitive against nations like China.
evidence.what_it_shows: Contradictory earlier stance: she celebrated a massive national data center build-out before turning against new projects in her state.

evidence.title: House roll call 356 (Dec. 18, 2025): passage of H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act permitting reform bill, Mace voted Yea
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted for a bill to speed federal permitting of energy and infrastructure projects, which cuts against a pause on building. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Mace Calls for a Statewide Pause on New Data Centers
evidence.quote: South Carolina is not Big Tech's personal power grid
evidence.what_it_shows: National coverage placing her among a growing list of lawmakers seeking data center moratoriums over electricity costs.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. Mace sponsors and cosponsors bills to criminalize AI deepfake pornography and pressed Hertz over AI damage scanners, which are targeted guardrails. But as Oversight IT subcommittee chair she frames AI as a race the U.S. must win, warns against stifling innovation, and notes rivals have no guardrails, while saying AI should be developed responsibly.

evidence.title: Oversight Committee release: Mace Opens Hearing on the Future of Artificial Intelligence
evidence.quote: It is essential the United States lead, not just in building these technologies, but in ensuring they are developed responsibly, deployed safely, and used in ways which advance American values.
evidence.what_it_shows: She compares AI to the space and nuclear races, raises the possibility of artificial general intelligence within years, and says the future is too important to leave to chance, but proposes no binding rules.

evidence.title: Oversight Committee hearing wrap-up: The U.S. Must Develop and Advance Artificial Intelligence to Dominate the Tech Race
evidence.quote: They’ve stolen a bunch of our data.
evidence.what_it_shows: She stressed not stifling AI innovation and noted China, Russia and Iran have no guardrails, a light-touch framing.

evidence.title: Press release: Mace: Deepfake Porn Is Digital Rape, Congress Must Act (reintroducing the Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act)
evidence.quote: My bill puts predators on notice: you do this, you're going to prison.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants federal criminal penalties for creating or sharing AI-generated sexual deepfakes, a specific AI guardrail.

evidence.title: H.R.3562: DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed letting victims sue people who make or share AI sexual deepfakes of them.

evidence.title: H.R.4600: RESPECT Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own bill adds prison time for sharing or threatening to share private explicit images, including AI deepfakes, building on the TAKE IT DOWN Act.

evidence.title: New York Post: Rep. Nancy Mace demands answers from Hertz over AI scanners charging hundreds of dollars for minor scratches
evidence.what_it_shows: As subcommittee chair she wrote Hertz's CEO seeking answers about AI damage scanners billing renters with no human review, an oversight push on a specific AI use.

evidence.title: H.R.3775: AI Training Extension Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Her bill extends AI training for federal workers; her press release said it gives them the tools, training, and guardrails to securely use AI and protect citizens' privacy.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Mace backs targeted rules: bills criminalizing non-consensual intimate images and deepfakes, tougher child abuse material reporting, a crackdown on Chinese-controlled apps, and scrutiny of Hertz's AI scanners, and she calls out Big Tech's energy grab. But she opposed the 2024 TikTok ban as government overreach and cosponsored a bill barring officials from pressuring platforms to remove posts.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Nancy Mace Opposes Government Overreach In TikTok Ban
evidence.quote: Representative Nancy Mace condemns the proposal to ban TikTok as an alarming trend toward government overreach reminiscent of authoritarian regimes.
evidence.what_it_shows: Contradictory evidence: she opposed one of the biggest tech restrictions Congress passed, calling it overreach.

evidence.title: H.R.5182: Child Online Safety Modernization Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed making online companies report child abuse material more fully and keep evidence longer.

evidence.title: H.R.1218: SHIELD Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed a federal crime for sharing private nude images without consent, a targeted online rule.

evidence.title: H.R.4927: ACES Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed cracking down on TikTok and other Chinese-controlled apps over spying, months before opposing the TikTok ban.

evidence.title: H.R.140: Protecting Speech from Government Interference Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She backed banning federal workers from pressuring social media companies to take down posts, a limit on government rather than on platforms.

evidence.quote: For too long, predators have exploited technology to harass, threaten, and destroy lives, without facing real consequences
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants stiffer criminal penalties layered on the TAKE IT DOWN Act's platform takedown rules.

preemption.label: Leans national rule

She has not signed the House letters against preemption.

evidence.title: Oversight Committee hearing wrap-up: The U.S. Must Develop and Advance Artificial Intelligence to Dominate the Tech Race
evidence.quote: They’ve stolen a bunch of our data.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words lean toward one national standard over state-by-state AI laws, in an exchange about the proposed ten-year moratorium on state AI laws.

evidence.quote: They’ve stolen a bunch of our data.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Britt wants data centers built to keep America's edge over China, but insists their power costs stay off family bills, wants Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge made law, and says local communities should decide. She rejects both a moratorium and 'a data center on every corner.'

evidence.title: Yellowhammer News: Britt presses Energy Secretary Wright on power bills at Appropriations subcommittee hearing
evidence.quote: We have to keep that compute power advantage. That is critically important
evidence.what_it_shows: She paired support for compute growth with a demand that data center costs not land on residential bills, citing a 40 percent rise in power bills since 2021.

evidence.title: Yellowhammer News: Britt endorses Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge on X
evidence.quote: Data centers should pay for their own electricity, not hardworking Americans. I support @POTUS taking steps to protect ratepayers while maintaining our competitive edge over China and ensuring America remains a global leader in technological advancement. This is the way.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her core formula: build for the China race, but make data centers pay their own way.

evidence.title: Alabama Daily News: Britt wants to find a middle way on data centers
evidence.quote: I don't think people who want a full moratorium…I don't think that that is the right avenue.
evidence.what_it_shows: She rejects both a moratorium and unlimited building, and says communities with full information that say no should not be forced.

evidence.title: Alabama Daily News: Britt on local decision-making
evidence.quote: But I absolutely think that those decisions need to be made on a local level.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames beating China as a national interest but leaves siting decisions to local communities.

evidence.title: Alabama Political Reporter: Britt talks data center accountability, defends ratepayer pledge (Capitol Journal)
evidence.quote: I think for many communities, these make sense. And, I think for others, that's not what they're looking for.
evidence.what_it_shows: Calls the pledge an outstanding first step and urges public input and accountability while arguing the AI buildout is an economic and security necessity.

evidence.title: Semafor: Britt says Congress should turn Trump's data center pledge into law
evidence.quote: I want to see people go ahead and do it on their own. As you know, they don't call it an act of Congress for nothing.
evidence.what_it_shows: She would love to see the voluntary pledge codified, opposes national moratoriums, and says localities should be free to reject data centers.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: Advancing Water Reuse Act (S.4506), 30 percent tax credit for water recycling at data centers and industrial sites
evidence.what_it_shows: Bipartisan bill with Sen. Lujan to reduce data center freshwater demand; cosponsorship verified in govinfo bill status.

evidence.title: Alabama Daily News: New Britt bill encourages data centers to recycle water
evidence.quote: A safe, reliable supply of freshwater is crucial to facilitating economic development while ensuring Americans across the country have access to clean water
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own framing of the water reuse bill as protecting communities while allowing industry to keep investing.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Britt is one of the Senate's most active Republicans on AI harms to children. She is lead cosponsor of the GUARD Act to ban AI companions for minors with criminal liability for companies, co-led letters to eight AI companies demanding safety disclosures, and says guardrails are imperative. Her focus is kids and chatbots, not frontier or existential risk.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (lead Republican cosponsor): GUARD Act (S.3062)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require age checks, ban AI companions for minors, force bots to disclose they are not human, and create criminal liability for harmful chatbots.

evidence.title: Press release: Britt priorities advanced out of Senate Judiciary Committee (GUARD Act remarks)
evidence.quote: We know they could put up those guardrails. They should do it anyway. It is sick that we're having to sit here to make them do that.
evidence.what_it_shows: Spoke before the unanimous committee vote and urged leadership to bring the bill to the floor.

evidence.title: CNN State of the Union transcript: Britt on AI chatbots and guardrails
evidence.quote: it is imperative that we put up guardrails, especially when you're looking at A.I.
evidence.what_it_shows: Said AI companies put profits over people, that voluntary steps are not enough, and that Congress must act now.

evidence.title: NBC News: Schatz and Britt lead letters to eight AI companies asking for public safety disclosures
evidence.quote: In the past few years, reports have emerged about chatbots that have engaged in suicidal fantasies with children, drafted suicide notes, and provided specific instructions on self-harm
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-led a bipartisan push for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft, xAI, Character.AI and Luka to commit to transparency about AI risks.

evidence.title: Press release: Britt discusses dangers of AI chatbots in Judiciary subcommittee hearing
evidence.quote: The growing culture of preying on our kids is OUTRAGEOUS. Meta is allowing bots to hold 'sensual' chats with CHILDREN!! Are you kidding me? This is sick and twisted. I will not stop until they are held accountable.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her reaction to Meta's chatbot policies; she also joined the bipartisan letter to Meta demanding safeguards for minors.

evidence.title: Press release: Britt on Jillian Michaels podcast on AI chatbots and Big Tech
evidence.what_it_shows: Described parents whose children died after chatbots encouraged suicide and called the GUARD Act common sense with support across the political spectrum.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: NO FAKES Act of 2026 (S.4591)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a legal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice or face (also cosponsored the 2025 version, S.1367).

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Britt is a leading Republican voice for reining in Big Tech on kids: she sponsors the Stop the Scroll Act and cosponsors KOSA, Kids Off Social Media, COPPA 2.0, STOP CSAM and Sammy's Law. She has gone further in words, saying the Section 230 liability shield 'has to be taken down,' though her bills are targeted rather than a full repeal.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Stop the Scroll Act (S.1885)
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own bill requiring mental health warning labels on social media.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms toward minors; also cosponsored the 118th Congress version (S.1409).

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Off Social Media Act (S.278)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban under-13s from social media and stop algorithmic targeting of users under 17.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (S.836)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stronger privacy rules for kids' and teens' data.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (S.1829)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would let victims sue platforms that fail to remove child sexual abuse material.

evidence.title: CNN State of the Union transcript: Britt on Section 230 and the liability shield
evidence.quote: the liability shield that we see in these social media companies and to an extent in this A.I. space has to be taken down, because people need to be held accountable.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her strongest anti-Big Tech statement, blaming Section 230 for letting platforms escape accountability for harms to kids.

evidence.title: Press release: Britt on Jillian Michaels podcast, taking on Big Tech
evidence.quote: But then also Congress has been completely and totally feckless in this arena. And at the end of the day, we're allowing social media companies to put their profits above people, and in this case, these people are our children.
evidence.what_it_shows: She says Big Tech could fix these problems on its own but has chosen not to, and that Congress must act.

evidence.title: Alabama Political Reporter: Britt joins bipartisan push to expand parental oversight online (Sammy's Law)
evidence.what_it_shows: Introduced Sammy's Law with Sens. Husted and Warner to force large platforms to allow third-party child safety software.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: Senate Judiciary privacy subcommittee hearing on social media verdicts and KOSA
evidence.quote: the earlier they get our children addicted, then the more likely they are to be a lifetime user
evidence.what_it_shows: She argued platforms are designed to addict children and urged the House to pass the Senate's version of KOSA.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found on federal preemption of state AI laws. Searched for reactions to the 2025 Senate moratorium vote, the Dec 2025 executive order and the March 2026 White House framework and found none. Her opposition to a national data center moratorium and support for local siting decisions concern data centers, not state AI laws.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted Yea with 99 senators after the deal collapsed; the near-unanimous vote does not by itself show a stance on preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China. She often frames data centers and AI as a race against China, but searched for statements on the Chip Security Act, GAIN AI Act, the AI Diffusion rule and H20/H200 sales and found none. Her Leadership in CET Act cosponsorship (faster patents for AI and chips) is neutral on export controls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Leadership in CET Act (S.1833)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would speed patent review for AI, chip and quantum inventions; a competitiveness measure, not an export control position.

members.signature: Lead Republican cosponsor of the GUARD Act to keep kids off AI companion chatbots; wants data centers built but ratepayers protected, with Trump's pledge written into law.

quote.text: We know they could put up those guardrails. They should do it anyway. It is sick that we're having to sit here to make them do that.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: No direct statement on Missouri's data center fights was found. At a Kansas City AI roundtable he said the country must have its computing capacity at home and meet sharply higher energy demand with small nuclear reactors, which leans toward building.

evidence.title: Startland News: Schmitt at KC Tech Council AI roundtable on computing infrastructure and energy
evidence.quote: We have to have the processing ability here in this country
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants domestic AI computing capacity and said energy needs will be astronomically higher, pointing to small modular nuclear reactors as the answer; he did not discuss ratepayer protections.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Schmitt talks about AI as a productivity boom and a race with China to win, and his past AI oversight targeted 'woke' algorithmic-fairness spending rather than safety. He has not backed safety testing, licensing or liability bills.

evidence.title: Startland News: Missouri's weapon in the AI race with China is KC tech companies, says Schmitt
evidence.quote: That's the kind of innovation and competition that's going to make us win this really important AI race with China.
evidence.what_it_shows: His framing is innovation and beating China; the only federal role he described was keeping Big Tech from blocking smaller innovators.

evidence.title: Press release: Schmitt amendment to cut NTIA funding for 'algorithmic justice' work
evidence.quote: This amendment would stop the NTIA's woke transfer, cutting the Biden NTIA's ability to fund an Orwellian "algorithmic justice" bureaucracy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treated federal work on algorithmic bias as a bureaucracy to defund, a light-touch signal.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act (S.1290)
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI bills focus on workforce mapping, not risk controls.

evidence.title: Schmitt site repost: Senate Republicans accuse FCC of advancing election-year AI advertising regulations
evidence.what_it_shows: He highlighted GOP opposition to an FCC rule requiring disclosure of AI in political ads.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed but leaning toward targeted rules: he wants Section 230 protection pulled from platforms that act as publishers or take down speech at government request, cosponsors ad-tech antitrust and a bill to break Big Tech's hold on Pentagon AI contracts, and hopes for bipartisan kids' online safety action. He also raised free speech concerns about the NO FAKES Act.

evidence.title: Press release: Schmitt questions witnesses on screentime and social media algorithms at Senate Commerce hearing
evidence.quote: they should lose that Section 230 protection. There's not really been a hammer behind that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He said platforms that act as publishers should lose Section 230 immunity and voiced hope for bipartisan agreement on protecting kids online.

evidence.title: Sponsor: COLLUDE Act (S.69)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would strip a platform's liability shield when it removes political speech at the government's request; his Big Tech focus is censorship.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AMERICA Act (S.1060), digital advertising antitrust
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs breaking up conflicts of interest in Google-style ad markets.

evidence.title: Press release: Schmitt reintroduces Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act with Sen. Warren (S.1775)
evidence.quote: I am proud to be leading this bill that promotes competition, as well as encourages innovation so the U.S. can continue to lead A.I.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to stop the Pentagon from handing AI and cloud contracts to a few giants without competition.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: Senate Commerce hearing on 30 years of Section 230
evidence.quote: And the government can't outsource that censorship to private actors either, can it?
evidence.what_it_shows: His questioning centered on government jawboning of platforms rather than platform accountability for harms.

evidence.title: Roll Call: AI deepfakes (NO FAKES Act) bill advanced by Senate Judiciary Committee; Schmitt among senators voicing free speech concerns
evidence.what_it_shows: He raised free speech concerns about a bill giving people rights over AI copies of their voice and likeness, a caution against new rules.

preemption.label: One national rule
preemption.summary: Schmitt told a Kansas City tech roundtable it is probably important for the federal government to preempt state AI rules, saying different rules in Kansas and Missouri will not work. His Yea vote to strip the 2025 moratorium came after the deal collapsed and is not evidence against preemption.

evidence.title: Startland News: Schmitt agrees consistent federal oversight is key at KC Tech Council AI roundtable
evidence.quote: It's probably important for the federal government to come in and preempt this
evidence.what_it_shows: He explicitly endorsed federal preemption of a state-by-state patchwork, adding that Kansas and Missouri having different AI rules is not going to work.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the near-unanimous vote to remove the moratorium; no statement accompanying the vote was found. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Mixed
china_chips.summary: Mixed. He signed the April 2025 letter urging Commerce to withdraw Biden's AI diffusion rule that capped chip exports to most countries, but he also cosponsors the Chip Security Act to track exported chips and block smuggling to China.

evidence.title: Ricketts-led letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick calling for withdrawal of the Biden AI Diffusion Rule (Schmitt signer)
evidence.quote: we urge you to withdraw this rule and propose an alternative that is effective in preventing Communist China from capturing the world market in a leading technology without compromising American advantages
evidence.what_it_shows: He wanted looser export limits for allies and customers while still keeping China out, a lighter-controls lean.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Chip Security Act (S.1705)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports location verification on advanced chips so they cannot be diverted to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (S.4429)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning Chinese connected-car technology, part of a broader China-hawk record.

evidence.title: Ricketts-led Republican senators' letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick urging withdrawal of the Biden AI Diffusion Rule
evidence.what_it_shows: Seven GOP senators asked Commerce to scrap the Biden-era AI Diffusion export rule before its May 15, 2025 compliance date and replace it with a lighter alternative, arguing it hurt US companies' global sales.

members.signature: Innovation-first China hawk on AI: says the federal government should preempt state AI rules, fought Biden's chip diffusion rule, and aims his tech oversight at government censorship and Big Tech's grip on defense contracts.

quote.text: Can you imagine Kansas has one set of rules for AI and Missouri has another? That's not going to work.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Fetterman is one of the loudest Democratic supporters of building AI data centers. He called the Sanders-Ocasio-Cortez moratorium bill 'China First', posted 'China wins' when New York paused data centers, and backed Trump's 'let data reign' message after Gov. Shapiro's guardrails order. He earlier cosponsored the Clean Cloud Act, which would charge polluting data centers a fee.

evidence.title: X post reported by Fox News: Fetterman calls AI data center moratorium proposal 'China First'
evidence.quote: The emerging chassis of AI must be built by America. We can put appropriate guardrails in place without handing the win on AI to China. A moratorium is China First
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposes a national pause on data center construction and frames it as helping China.

evidence.title: X post reported by CNBC after New York imposed the first state AI data center ban
evidence.quote: China wins
evidence.what_it_shows: He mocked a state moratorium on data centers as a gift to China.

evidence.title: X post reported by WGAL days after Gov. Shapiro signed a data center guardrails executive order
evidence.quote: China continues to fuel and benefit from our overreaction. I reject the political pandering and hyperbole over data centers or AI doomsdaying.
evidence.what_it_shows: He dismissed the backlash to data centers as pandering and overreaction.

evidence.title: X post reported by The Philadelphia Inquirer: Fetterman agrees with Trump's 'let data reign' post
evidence.quote: We must win the war for AI supremacy over China. They foment the 'anti' argument through misinformation
evidence.what_it_shows: He sided with Trump against communities resisting data centers and blamed China for stoking opposition.

evidence.title: Truthout: Fetterman backs Trump's comments berating opponents of data centers
evidence.quote: There's nothing more damaging to a Democrat than agreeing with Trump AND data centers, but what's right is right
evidence.what_it_shows: He acknowledged the political cost inside his party and stuck with his pro-data-center position anyway.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Clean Cloud Act of 2025 (S.1475), a pollution fee on big data centers and crypto mines
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier in 2025 he backed an emissions standard for data centers, a guardrail that sits in tension with his later rhetoric.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Fetterman treats winning the AI race with China as a national security priority and rejects calls for a pause or what he calls 'AI doomsdaying'. He says appropriate guardrails are possible but has not backed binding safety rules for advanced AI.

evidence.title: X post reported by The National News Desk: Fetterman rejects Sanders's call to pause AI development
evidence.quote: America must lead in the development of AI, otherwise we live under China's rules. That must not happen.
evidence.what_it_shows: He publicly opposed a pause on frontier AI development proposed by Sen. Sanders.

evidence.title: X post reported by Fox News: Fetterman warns China benefits from US 'overreaction' on AI
evidence.quote: AI supremacy and energy dominance underpins our national security
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI as a race to win, not a danger to contain.

evidence.title: X post reported by Fox News on the data center moratorium bill
evidence.quote: We can put appropriate guardrails in place without handing the win on AI to China.
evidence.what_it_shows: He leaves room for some guardrails but puts beating China first.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Fetterman consistently backs targeted rules for social media and kids' safety. He cosponsors the Kids Online Safety Act, the Kids Off Social Media Act, the Stop the Scroll Act warning-label bill and the STOP CSAM Act, and has promoted them on national TV with Sen. Britt.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms to protect minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Off Social Media Act (S.278)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning children under 13 from social media and limiting algorithmic targeting of teens.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Stop the Scroll Act (S.1885), mental health warning labels on social media
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a specific disclosure mandate on platforms.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (S.1829)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting victims sue platforms that fail to remove child sexual abuse material.

evidence.title: Alabama Political Reporter: Sens. Britt and Fetterman discuss social media regulations on NBC News
evidence.what_it_shows: On an NBC panel he and Britt promoted the Stop the Scroll Act and other social media regulations they cosponsor.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public statement found on whether Washington should override state AI laws. He voted Yea on the July 2025 amendment that struck the 10-year state AI law moratorium, but that vote was 99 to 1 and is not evidence of a position on its own. Searched for reactions to the December 2025 executive order and March 2026 White House framework and found none.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R.1 (Senate roll call 363)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined 98 other senators in removing the moratorium; nearly every senator voted the same way after a deal collapsed. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Fetterman cosponsored the FIGHT China Act to restrict American investment in Chinese military and surveillance technology, and he talks constantly about beating China in AI. No statement found specifically on Nvidia chip sales or export controls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: FIGHT China Act of 2025 (S.1053), outbound investment restrictions
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports limits on US money flowing to Chinese military tech firms, a China-hawk signal but not a chip export position.

evidence.title: X post reported by The Philadelphia Inquirer
evidence.quote: We must win the war for AI supremacy over China.
evidence.what_it_shows: His China framing is about the AI race, not about whether to sell chips abroad.

members.signature: Democrat who breaks with his party to back Trump on data centers and the AI race with China, while cosponsoring kids' online safety bills.

quote.text: The emerging chassis of AI must be built by America. We can put appropriate guardrails in place without handing the win on AI to China. A moratorium is China First

evidence.what_it_shows: The 24-member bipartisan task force found that preempting state AI laws 'is complex,' has 'benefits and drawbacks,' can be done via floors or ceilings, and must use precise definitions; its only preemption recommendation was that Congress commission a study of existing federal and state AI regulations. data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Balanced and noncommittal. Asked on Aug 31, 2026 about Trump calling data center critics backwards and poor, she would not endorse the remark, attacked her opponent's data center investments, and said each state's people should decide. She voted for the SPEED Act permitting bill. No bills or detailed statements on data center costs found.

evidence.title: Where Is The Buzz: Luna on Trump calling data center critics 'backwards and poor'
evidence.quote: My opponent heavily invested in data centers, and I think really the issue right now is what are the people of each state going to decide on what’s best for them?
evidence.what_it_shows: She declines to back or oppose data centers and says the decision belongs to states and local people, adding 'Leave it for the people to decide.'

evidence.title: Roll call 356: Yea on H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act (permitting reform)
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted for a permitting reform bill that backers say speeds energy and infrastructure buildout. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Open to rules but not specific. After Anthropic researchers warned in Sept 2026 that AI could end humanity, she called for a special session of Congress on AI and said protecting all Americans comes first. She cosponsors the DEFIANCE Act on sexual deepfakes and a bill to codify Trump's anti-woke AI procurement order. No detailed AI safety proposal of her own was found.

evidence.title: The Hill: Lawmakers sound alarm on AI dangers after Anthropic researchers' warning (Luna calls for special session)
evidence.quote: We MUST be ready. This is happening whether or not we want it to.
evidence.what_it_shows: She treated the extinction warnings as serious, asked Congress to convene a special session on AI, and said the first priority is protecting all Americans while noting AI's potential in health care and food.

evidence.title: H.R. 3562, DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs letting victims sue over AI-made sexual deepfakes, a targeted guardrail.

evidence.title: H.R. 4873, bill to codify Executive Order 14319 on preventing 'woke AI' in the federal government
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants the government to buy only AI it considers politically neutral, a culture-war rule rather than a safety rule.

evidence.title: Gizmodo: Luna denies using AI to write bill after 'Claude responded' appears in NDAA summary
evidence.what_it_shows: Context only: she defended her staff after an AI assistant's text appeared in a bill summary, showing comfort with AI tools rather than a policy stance.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Backs targeted rules on Big Tech, mainly for kids and foreign influence. She is House lead of the Kids Off Social Media Act (bans under-13 accounts, limits algorithms for teens), cosponsors the DEFIANCE Act, supported a TikTok ban in 2023, and introduced a bill making paid foreign-government influencers register. She also cosponsored a bill barring officials from pressuring platforms to remove posts.

evidence.title: H.R. 7399, Kids Off Social Media Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She leads the House companion to the Cruz-Schatz bill banning social media accounts for kids under 13 and algorithmic targeting of teens.

evidence.title: Press release: Congress introduces landmark bipartisan bill to protect children online (Kids Off Social Media Act)
evidence.quote: The Kids Off Social Media Act is about putting children’s safety first and holding Big Tech accountable.
evidence.what_it_shows: In her own words she frames the bill as holding Big Tech accountable and answering parents' alarm about social media harms.

evidence.title: H.R. 7433, Kids Off Social Media Act (second version)
evidence.what_it_shows: She reintroduced the bill with a cosponsor days later.

evidence.title: H.R. 140, Protecting Speech from Government Interference Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Her Big Tech concerns also run to censorship; this bill bars federal workers from pressuring platforms to take down posts.

evidence.title: Fox News, Your World with Neil Cavuto: 'We Must Come Together and Ban TikTok' (posted on luna.house.gov)
evidence.what_it_shows: She called for banning TikTok, a China-focused platform restriction.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found on the state AI law moratorium, federal preemption, the Dec 2025 executive order, or the Mar 2026 White House framework. She did not sign the Matsui or Clarke letters and no statement was located in news searches.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China. She is not a cosponsor of the Chip Security Act or AI OVERWATCH Act. Her China comments found were about a bot farm targeting the U.S. AI debate, not chips.

members.signature: Populist Republican who sponsors the House Kids Off Social Media Act and, after the Sept 2026 Anthropic researcher warnings, called for a special session of Congress on AI.

quote.text: We MUST be ready. This is happening whether or not we want it to.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Lee wants the grid built out to meet AI and data center demand and voted for the SPEED Act permitting bill, but she cosponsors the Ratepayer Protection Act so large data centers pay for their own power instead of households. Build, with conditions.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 9340, Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed onto the bipartisan bill that makes 100 MW+ data centers pay for the power and grid upgrades they need so household bills do not rise.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Laurel Lee questions witnesses on energy demand and grid reliability at Energy Subcommittee hearing
evidence.quote: With rapid population growth, increased manufacturing, and advances in technologies including AI and data centers, our electricity demand and production will only continue to rise.
evidence.what_it_shows: She treats AI and data center demand as growth the grid must be ready to serve, not something to block.

evidence.title: Energy and Commerce excerpts: Energy Subcommittee hearing on electricity transmission for reliable and affordable power
evidence.quote: The system wasn't built by federal mandate. It was built state by state utility, by utility, with state regulators who understood their communities, their geography, their customers, and their specific energy needs better than any federal agency ever could.
evidence.what_it_shows: At a hearing on building transmission for rising power demand she praised the state-led, utility-led way the grid was built, signaling deference to states and utilities on grid growth.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 4776, SPEED Act (House roll call 356)
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted for a broad permitting reform bill that speeds federal environmental reviews for energy and infrastructure projects; it is general permitting reform, not data-center specific. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Lee backs specific AI rules: lawsuits over sexual deepfakes, a right to control AI copies of your voice and face, disclosure of training data, and her own bill forcing AI web crawlers to identify themselves. She pairs this with pro-innovation framing and interest in voluntary NIST standards, not sweeping AI mandates.

evidence.title: Hearing remarks: House Judiciary subcommittee hearing 'AI Regulation and the Future of US Leadership' (Tech Policy Press transcript)
evidence.quote: So as policymakers, we have two responsibilities. One is to protect the public from real risks, but second, to ensure that American innovation continues to lead the world. Those goals are not mutually exclusive.
evidence.what_it_shows: She frames AI policy as balancing real risks against innovation; in the same hearing she asked whether model card disclosures should be mandated and whether NIST should write voluntary AI standards.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Laurel Lee introduces bipartisan Stealth Bot Prohibition Act
evidence.quote: As artificial intelligence becomes more sophisticated, we must ensure innovation is accompanied by transparency and accountability.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own bill would require AI web crawlers to identify themselves and let the FTC fine deceptive bots, a targeted transparency rule on AI companies.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3562, DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting victims sue over AI-made sexual deepfakes; she co-led the House push with Rep. Ocasio-Cortez.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8915, NO FAKES Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a legal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice and face; she also cosponsored the 2025 version (H.R. 2794).

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7209, TRAIN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting artists and writers force AI companies to reveal whether their work was used in training.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Laurel Lee appointed to the House Task Force on Artificial Intelligence
evidence.quote: Because of quick advancements in AI, it is important for Congress to remain diligent and plan for complexities to keep a competitive edge
evidence.what_it_shows: Her early framing stresses competitiveness and diligence rather than alarm about AI danger.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 6998, Renewed Hope Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She also promotes beneficial uses of AI, here letting investigators use face-matching technology to identify children in abuse images.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Lee is a kids-online-safety legislator: she co-led the House COPPA 2.0 update, sponsored the Promoting a Safe Internet for Minors Act and the REPORT Act, and backs the KIDS Act package. Her approach is targeted rules for platforms, not break-ups or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Press release (Walberg office): Walberg and Lee lead effort to protect children's online privacy (COPPA 2.0)
evidence.quote: COPPA 2.0 provides necessary updates to existing law, sets clear limits on data collection, and ensures platforms act to protect the privacy and data of young users.
evidence.what_it_shows: She co-leads the House bill limiting how platforms collect data on children and teens.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6291, Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Formal cosponsorship of the House COPPA 2.0 bill she co-leads.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Laurel Lee introduces bipartisan legislation to strengthen online safety for children
evidence.quote: The digital landscape is constantly evolving, and our approach to online safety must evolve with it.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her Promoting a Safe Internet for Minors Act directs the FTC to run a national online-safety education campaign, citing deepfakes and AI-generated abuse material.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 6289, Promoting a Safe Internet for Minors Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own kids-online-safety bill, introduced with Democrat Darren Soto.

evidence.title: Sponsor (118th): H.R. 5082, REPORT Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her earlier bill made platforms report more kinds of child exploitation to the national tipline; it passed the House in 2024.

evidence.title: Roll Call: House panel advances kids online safety bills
evidence.quote: A child's level of protection should not depend on their zip code
evidence.what_it_shows: Roll Call reports she cosponsored the House children's privacy bill that advanced 14-10 at the Energy and Commerce subcommittee markup over Democratic objections to its preemption clause.

evidence.title: Ocasio-Cortez and Laurel Lee press conference with Paris Hilton urging House passage of the DEFIANCE Act
evidence.what_it_shows: After the Senate passed the DEFIANCE Act unanimously, the bipartisan House co-leads and survivors publicly pressed Speaker Johnson to bring the deepfake civil-remedy bill to the floor.

preemption.label: Leans national rule
preemption.summary: Lee leans toward one national standard. She defended the House COPPA 2.0's override of state kids' privacy laws, saying a child's protection should not depend on zip code, and has asked whether a single federal body should set AI model standards. We found no statement from her on the 2025 state AI law moratorium or the Dec 2025 executive order.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Lee defends preemption in House COPPA 2.0 at Energy and Commerce subcommittee markup
evidence.quote: A child's level of protection should not depend on their zip code
evidence.what_it_shows: She argued that preempting state children's privacy laws would standardize protections and fix the patchwork of state rules, over Democratic objections.

evidence.title: Floridian Press: Laurel Lee discusses the federalization of AI regulations (House Judiciary hearing)
evidence.quote: Should we designate a single federal entity to try and develop those standards?
evidence.what_it_shows: She asked witnesses about state AI laws as 'laboratories of democracy' and about giving NIST or CAISI authority over frontier model standards; the reporter characterized this as discussing the need for a federal standard, but she did not state a firm position.

evidence.title: House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence final report (118th Congress) - Federal Preemption of State Law chapter
evidence.what_it_shows: The 24-member bipartisan task force found that preempting state AI laws 'is complex,' has 'benefits and drawbacks,' can be done via floors or ceilings, and must use precise definitions; its only preemption recommendation was that Congress commission a study of existing federal and state AI regulations. It did not endorse a moratorium.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on chip export controls as of Sept 2026. We searched for Chip Security Act, H20/H200, Nvidia and export control statements; her only semiconductor remarks concern protecting intellectual property and Florida's chip workforce.

evidence.title: Energy and Commerce excerpts: CMT Subcommittee hearing on the semiconductor ecosystem and supply chain
evidence.quote: When it comes to semiconductors, U.S. leadership depends not just on investment, but on protecting our intellectual property that drives innovation and ensuring that we have the workforce to sustain it.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her semiconductor focus is IP protection and workforce, with no statement on selling or restricting AI chips to China.

members.signature: Kids-online-safety and deepfake bills (DEFIANCE, NO FAKES, COPPA 2.0), sponsor of the Stealth Bot Prohibition Act, House AI Task Force alum who backs data center growth with ratepayer protections.

quote.text: So as policymakers, we have two responsibilities. One is to protect the public from real risks, but second, to ensure that American innovation continues to lead the world. Those goals are not mutually exclusive.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: McCormick is one of the House's most vocal data center boosters. As chair of the Science Committee's oversight subcommittee he ran a February 2026 hearing pushing faster permitting and more power generation for AI data centers, voted for the SPEED Act permitting bill, and went on Bloomberg in August 2026 to warn against slowing the AI buildout. He does acknowledge the risk that homeowners could end up subsidizing grid upgrades for data centers.

evidence.title: Hearing: McCormick chairs House Science oversight hearing 'Powering America's AI Future' on data center infrastructure (Roll Call)
evidence.quote: Data centers consume vast amounts of electricity, sometimes 10 to 50 times more per square foot than traditional buildings
evidence.what_it_shows: He used his subcommittee chairmanship to frame the AI buildout as needing far more electricity and faster permitting, while praising companies that fund new generation themselves.

evidence.title: Hearing: McCormick raises ratepayer subsidy question at the same data center hearing (Roll Call)
evidence.quote: That raises serious questions of whether residential ratepayers could end up subsidizing upgrades that primarily serve high-intensity industrial complexes.
evidence.what_it_shows: Even as a booster, he acknowledged that traditional utility rate structures could push data center grid costs onto households and said that needs to be addressed.

evidence.title: E&E News: McCormick backs streamlined environmental review for AI infrastructure at Feb 24 hearing
evidence.quote: I'm not advocating that we change the rules in some sort of dramatic capacity. But we do need to change.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants permitting and environmental review changed to speed data center and energy construction, though he frames it as a moderate change.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act (NEPA permitting reform), House roll call 356
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the permitting-reform bill that the administration and industry pushed as a way to build data centers and power plants faster. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Interview: McCormick joins Bloomberg This Weekend to talk data centers and AI (listed on his official video page)
evidence.what_it_shows: Bloomberg titled the segments 'Rep. McCormick Warns Against Slowing AI Buildout' and 'Data Center Investment Will Make Communities Better, Says Rep. McCormick'; the video itself could not be opened, so no quote is given.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: McCormick treats AI mainly as a race the U.S. must win against China and argues policy should help industry thrive rather than constrain it. He has not called for binding safety rules, and the pro-industry super PAC Leading the Future named him a 'GOP Champion' in 2026.

evidence.title: Op-ed: 'Don't let AI slip away: Why US policy must match innovation' (Washington Examiner)
evidence.quote: The federal government and private industry must move in lockstep to maintain American leadership in AI innovation.
evidence.what_it_shows: After meeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, he framed the goal of AI policy as keeping industry thriving and beating adversaries, not new safety mandates.

evidence.title: PAC: Leading the Future super PAC names McCormick on its 'House GOP Champions' list (Breitbart)
evidence.quote: part of a broader ecosystem of current members who have engaged with the industry
evidence.what_it_shows: The AI industry's main super PAC, which backs a light-touch national framework, singled him out as an ally.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 2385, CREATE AI Act of 2025 (national AI research resource)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports public investment in AI research capacity, a neutral-to-pro-innovation position.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5351, NSF AI Education Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs federal AI education and workforce programs.

tech_regulation.label: Light touch
tech_regulation.summary: McCormick voted against the House's 2026 kids online safety package (the KIDS Act) even though most Republicans supported it. He did vote to force TikTok's sale in 2024 and backed a bill to keep data brokers from selling service members' data to hostile countries, so his skepticism is aimed at broad new platform rules rather than national security measures.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 7757, the KIDS Act kids online safety package, House roll call 228 (passed 267-117)
evidence.what_it_shows: He was among the House Republicans who opposed the chamber's main children's online safety bill. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 7521, Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok divestiture), House roll call 86
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell, a national-security style tech rule. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6573 (118th), Protecting Military Servicemembers' Data Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed a narrow data-broker rule to stop sales of troops' personal data to hostile countries.

preemption.label: Leans national rule
preemption.summary: In February 2025 a Georgia state senator said McCormick called and asked the legislature not to pass its own AI bill because AI should be handled at the federal level, and the state bill stalled. McCormick's office did not comment, and no statement from him on the 2025 federal moratorium or the 2026 White House framework was found.

evidence.title: Georgia Recorder: State Sen. Brandon Beach says McCormick asked Georgia lawmakers not to act on AI because it is a federal issue
evidence.quote: I got a call from Congressman Rich McCormick asking us not to do anything on AI, saying that they were going to do it at the federal level
evidence.what_it_shows: As relayed by the committee chair, McCormick argued a patchwork of state AI laws would hurt the U.S. against China and wanted Washington, not states, to set AI rules; the state AI Accountability Act did not get a vote that day.

evidence.title: House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence final report (118th Congress) - Federal Preemption of State Law chapter
evidence.what_it_shows: The 24-member bipartisan task force found that preempting state AI laws 'is complex,' has 'benefits and drawbacks,' can be done via floors or ceilings, and must use precise definitions; its only preemption recommendation was that Congress commission a study of existing federal and state AI regulations. It did not endorse a moratorium.

china_chips.label: Leans sell more
china_chips.summary: Mixed record. McCormick wants to stop China from using American AI through cloud loopholes or theft and cosponsored several bills to do that. But he also led the push to scrap the Biden AI chip export rule, celebrated its rescission as making America 'open for business,' and was one of only two committee members to vote against the AI Overwatch Act giving Congress a veto over chip sales to China. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: The sources show a consistent pro-export posture since 2025: he led the push to kill the AI Diffusion Rule and claimed credit for its rescission, argued controls on allies cede markets to China, and was one of only two c

evidence.title: Press release: 'Big Win for US Tech: Rescission of the Biden Administration's AI Export Rule'
evidence.quote: By removing these overly burdensome export controls, we are sending a clear message that America is open for business and ready to lead the world in AI innovation.
evidence.what_it_shows: He and Rep. Scott Franklin wrote to Commerce urging repeal of the AI Diffusion Rule and claimed credit when it was rescinded, a pro-export position.

evidence.title: Op-ed: McCormick describes leading the fight against BIS Rule 00636 after meeting Nvidia's Jensen Huang (Washington Examiner)
evidence.quote: I have led the charge to change the Bureau of Industry and Security Rule 00636, issued by the Biden administration, that threatened these objectives by constraining companies in ways that may ultimately harm our national security.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues broad chip export controls, including on allies, cede markets to China and hurt U.S. companies.

evidence.title: Committee vote: McCormick one of two no votes as House Foreign Affairs advances the AI Overwatch Act 42-2-1 (The Hill)
evidence.quote: Reps. Andy Barr (R-Ky.) and Rich McCormick (R-Ga.) were the only two on the committee to oppose the measure.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed giving Congress arms-sale style power to block advanced AI chip exports to China; Roll Call reported he did not explain the vote.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 1486, Economic Espionage Prevention Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill lets the President punish foreign companies, notably Chinese ones, that steal trade secrets or break export rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 2683, Remote Access Security Act (closes cloud loophole for restricted chips)
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to stop Chinese firms from renting restricted American AI chips through the cloud.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 1121, No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed removing the Chinese AI app from federal devices.

evidence.title: Press release: 'Congressman McCormick BANS China from Exploiting American AI' (CLOUD AI Act, 118th)
evidence.quote: We cannot allow communist China to endanger America's future and oppress their own people by abusing our technology.
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-authored the 2023 bill to stop China from remotely accessing American chips it cannot buy under export controls.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Sorensen wants data centers in Illinois but only on strict terms: no rate increases for residents, build their own renewable or nuclear power, use gray water, sit in industrial corridors, and use union labor. A balance between building and protecting bills.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Burlison is Missouri's most vocal data center champion. He wrote that Missouri must lead the data center revolution, calls water worries overblown, says opposition is stoked by China or solar and wind interests, and held Oversight hearings promoting AI infrastructure. He allows that projects deserve oversight and local review of measurable impacts, but opposes blanket opposition and moratoriums.

evidence.title: Op-ed (St. Louis Post-Dispatch, posted on his site): Missouri Must Lead America's Data Center Revolution
evidence.quote: Projects like these deserve oversight, but blanket opposition only slows us down. Missouri can pursue this responsibly while creating high-paying jobs, strengthening schools, and attracting new investment across the state.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants Missouri to build data centers aggressively, criticizes local moratoriums and argues state law already protects ratepayers.

evidence.title: Missourinet: Burlison says data centers are a national security issue
evidence.what_it_shows: He said the only groups with reason to demonize data centers are the solar and wind industry or foreign actors, that data centers pay for infrastructure and cut peak demand, and that you do not want your data housed in China (page blocked; quotes seen only via a summary).

evidence.title: Newstalk KZRG: Burlison blames China for hate against data centers
evidence.quote: From what I understand, most of them use less water than a car wash
evidence.what_it_shows: He dismisses water-use concerns and warns that foreign actors including China shape online opposition.

evidence.title: Missouri Times: Burlison post blaming China for anti-data-center content
evidence.quote: They know the future runs on AI and data centers, and they want the edge.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames anti-data-center sentiment as something China wants Missourians to feel.

evidence.title: Newstalk KZRG: Burlison defends AI, says data centers deserve a fair look
evidence.quote: Whether it’s a data center or any other business, I think we should approach them all the same way
evidence.what_it_shows: He accepts local review of power, water and traffic impacts but rejects fear-based restrictions on data centers as central planning.

evidence.title: Oversight subcommittee release: Burlison opening statement at hearing on the economics of AI, data centers and power consumption
evidence.quote: This rapid growth is astounding and has concerning implications for both current and future power generation.
evidence.what_it_shows: He acknowledges data center power demand is a real planning problem while praising the Stargate buildout and Trump's AI dominance order.

evidence.title: Oversight release: Burlison remarks at roundtable on economic competition with China
evidence.quote: As part of undermining American AI development, China is funding nonprofits in the U.S. and spreading propaganda to impede data center construction and energy projects.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats obstacles to data center construction as part of China's strategy against American AI.

evidence.title: Press release: Burlison reintroduces Reliable Grid Act to limit EPA rules that reduce dispatchable power
evidence.quote: My Reliable Grid Act puts an end to this madness and stops future radical EPA tyrants from destroying our energy infrastructure
evidence.what_it_shows: His grid bill is a supply-side answer (keep fossil plants running) that supporters explicitly tie to new demand from data centers and AI.

ai_risk.label: Hands off
ai_risk.summary: Burlison argues regulation makes American AI slower, not safer, praised Trump for revoking Biden's AI order, and was one of only two House members to vote against the Take It Down Act on AI deepfake porn. He does support limits on government AI surveillance (the Flock-Off Act) and once said Congress should fight potential AI abuse, but his overall stance is hands off.

evidence.title: Oversight release: Burlison opening statement at roundtable on AI and American power
evidence.quote: Government-mandated red tape and free-speech constraints do not make AI safer, they just make American companies slower while our adversaries sprint ahead unchecked.
evidence.what_it_shows: He explicitly opposes AI regulation and praised the revocation of Biden's AI executive order.

evidence.title: Oversight release: Burlison remarks on regulating AI into mediocrity

evidence.what_it_shows: Frames AI policy as a race with China in which regulation is the enemy.

evidence.title: Newsweek: Burlison one of two Republicans voting against the Take It Down Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted no on the 409-2 bill criminalizing nonconsensual AI deepfake sexual images, the only bipartisan AI guardrail to become law in 2025.

evidence.what_it_shows: Wants Congress to help the administration reduce barriers to AI, with pro-market rather than regulatory answers.

evidence.what_it_shows: His interest in deepfakes centered on commercial detection tools rather than new rules.

evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed a platform takedown mandate for nonconsensual intimate images that nearly every other member supported.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls

He sponsors the Remote Access Security Act, which passed the House 369-22 in January 2026 to stop Chinese firms from using restricted chips through the cloud, and cosponsors the Chip Security Act, the AI OVERWATCH Act giving Congress a veto over chip sales to China, and a dozen other bills toughening export enforcement.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Remote Access Security Act (H.R.2683)

evidence.quote: Our export controls are only as strong as the weakest link, and right now, the CCP has a real tool to sidestep these prohibitions. We need action now.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames cloud access to controlled chips as a national security gap that needs stricter federal control.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Chip Security Act (H.R.3447)

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI OVERWATCH Act (H.R.6875)

evidence.title: Cosponsor: STRIDE Act (H.R.6058)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed tighter rules on shipping advanced chips to China and other rivals.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Stop Stealing our Chips Act (H.R.6322)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported paying and protecting whistleblowers who report chip export violations.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 (H.R.8283)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed penalties on foreign companies, especially Chinese ones, that steal or copy American AI models.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Export Controls Enforcement Act (H.R.4505)

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Langworthy treats rising demand from data centers as a reason to build more power plants and speed up permitting, not as a reason to slow data centers. He has not been found commenting on Gov. Hochul's 2026 data center pause. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: Both sources are pure supply-side (repower a gas plant, cut hydropower red tape) with no conditions, ratepayer protections, or data-center-specific caveats mentioned; he never states a data center position. The evidence

evidence.title: Wellsville Sun: Borrello, Langworthy and Molitor call on Hochul to repower the idle NRG plant in Dunkirk
evidence.quote: You cannot remove dependable energy from the grid while demand is growing and expect costs to fall or reliability to improve.
evidence.what_it_shows: He named data centers, along with manufacturing, as drivers of rising electricity demand and argued the answer is more generation, not less demand.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: Yea on the SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), federal permitting reform

evidence.what_it_shows: Another supply-side, cut-red-tape energy bill; it shows his general build-more-power approach rather than a data center position.

ai_risk.label: Light touch

He backs targeted protections for kids, deepfake victims and AI child-exploitation cases, yet he asked Commerce to treat New York's frontier-AI safety law (the RAISE Act) as harmful overregulation and wants innovation-first national standards to stay ahead of China.

evidence.quote: The United States is best positioned to establish strong, innovation-driven standards that protect consumers, safeguard children, and promote economic growth.

evidence.title: Statement on House passage of the Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act (KIDS Act)
evidence.quote: Families deserve real tools to shield children from online predators, addictive algorithms, scams, dangerous and illegal products, explicit content, and the emerging risks posed by AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports specific, kid-focused rules that include AI risks.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence Expert Commission Act of 2024 (H.R. 8005, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: His own AI bill created a study commission on AI-generated child abuse material rather than new binding rules.

evidence.title: Press release: Langworthy introduces legislation to combat the use of AI to create child sexual abuse material

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act (H.R. 1941)

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Federal A.I. Governance and Transparency Act of 2024 (H.R. 7532, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed public reporting on how federal agencies use AI.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

evidence.title: Statement on House passage of the Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act (KIDS Act)

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Landsman is one of the House's leading voices for making data centers pay their own way. He sponsors three bills: a FERC conference on protecting ratepayers (H.R. 6529, advanced by Energy and Commerce), the No Harm Data Centers Act requiring data centers to pay full grid costs and banning NDAs with officials (H.R. 8033), and a national study of noise, air and water impacts (H.R. 9629). He wants a federal framework so towns have a say, but he has not called for a moratorium on building.

evidence.title: Press release: Landsman leads new bill requiring Big Tech to pay for data centers and no NDAs
evidence.quote: You're either with Big Tech or with our towns. A handshake and a promise from these tech companies is not enough.
evidence.what_it_shows: His No Harm Data Centers Act would make data centers pay full energy and infrastructure costs, study environmental impacts and prohibit NDAs with elected officials.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R.8033, No Harm Data Centers Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Binding cost-allocation and transparency rules for data centers.

evidence.title: Press release: Landsman, Beyer introduce bill to protect residents from rising costs caused by AI data centers
evidence.quote: Residents and small businesses in states like Ohio, which is home to nearly 200 data centers, shouldn't be footing the bill to support them.
evidence.what_it_shows: His first data center bill has FERC convene stakeholders and recommend how to keep AI data center costs off household bills.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R.6529, Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
evidence.what_it_shows: 23 cosponsors; included in the Energy and Commerce data center markup in June and July 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: Landsman introduced third AI data center bill in Congress
evidence.quote: There are legitimate concerns about pollution and AI data centers. Our bill makes sure these environmental impacts are studied so communities have the information they need and peace of mind they deserve.
evidence.what_it_shows: His Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act orders an EPA and National Academies study of noise, air, water, carbon and e-waste impacts.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R.9629, Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Third data center bill, focused on environmental impacts.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R.7066, SHIELD Act (data center electricity costs)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs another bill to keep data center costs off family electric bills.

evidence.title: WCPO: Data centers emerge as key issue in Ohio's 1st Congressional District race
evidence.quote: If they're going to come in, they're going to come in, they're going to pay for everything. They're not going to pollute. You're going to have a say.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his reelection race he calls for a national framework making data centers pay everything and negotiate in public; his opponent Eric Conroy called it a local issue.

evidence.title: FOX19: Ohio data center bill would require voter approval, ban local tax incentives
evidence.quote: One forces the data centers to pay for everything. There's no reason our taxpayers should pay for anything of this. They have so much money.
evidence.what_it_shows: His own summary of his three bills: pay for everything, no NDAs, a national environmental standard.

evidence.title: Press release: Landsman, Reece call on DeWine to rein in energy costs in Southwest Ohio
evidence.quote: There is a time for rate increases, but this is arguably the worst possible time for such an increase.
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a county commissioner's call for a moratorium on further Duke Energy rate increases, tying it to affordability.

evidence.title: E&E News: House panel sets vote on data center, grid bills
evidence.what_it_shows: His H.R. 6529 was part of the bipartisan Energy and Commerce data center markup alongside the Ratepayer Protection Act.

evidence.title: Letters from 20 House Democrats led by Rep. Kevin Mullin to FERC, Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs
evidence.what_it_shows: Twenty House Democrats asked regulators, utilities and the data center industry how they will keep grid upgrade costs off household bills, whether contracts and tariffs will be transparent, whether load forecasts are realistic, and what cost-allocation tools (minimum usage commitments, separate rate classes, upfront cost recovery) Congress should consider.

evidence.title: New Democrat Coalition letter to House appropriators requesting FY2027 report language directing DOE to develop a National Strategic Data Center Plan
evidence.what_it_shows: Fourteen New Democrats asked the Energy-Water appropriations leaders to direct DOE, with Commerce, DHS, FERC and EPA, to produce an 18-month national plan on data center electricity demand, grid reliability and consumer cost impacts, water efficiency and geographic diversification, framing data centers as vital but in need of managed growth.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Landsman focuses on specific AI harms rather than broad AI rules. He sponsors the Doctors Not AI Act to stop insurers' AI from denying care, the Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act, and the resolution to overturn Medicare's WISeR AI prior authorization pilot, and he cosponsors the DEFIANCE Act on AI sexual deepfakes and a bill against AI election deception. No statements on frontier AI safety, licensing or a pause were found.

evidence.title: Press release: Landsman introduces bipartisan legislation to keep AI from making health care decisions (Doctors Not AI Act)
evidence.quote: When a computer system is making decisions about health care, people will get hurt. We have to make sure health care professionals remain the decision makers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Bipartisan bill limiting AI to a supporting role in insurance coverage decisions and requiring disclosure when AI is used.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R.10210, Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires a licensed professional, not AI, to make medical necessity denials.

evidence.title: Press release: Landsman, DelBene lead fight to overturn AI model delaying and denying care for seniors (WISeR)

evidence.what_it_shows: Led a Congressional Review Act resolution against Medicare's AI prior authorization pilot in Ohio and five other states.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.J.Res.187, disapproving the CMS WISeR AI prior authorization model

evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a ban on AI deepfakes that deceive voters in federal elections.

No calls for breakups, Section 230 repeal or a comprehensive privacy law were found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R.8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected cars and software tied to China and other adversaries.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R.6437, Kids Internet Safety Partnership Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a government and industry partnership on kids' online safety.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Landsman signed both House Democratic letters against overriding state AI laws: the November 2025 Matsui letter (81 signers) opposing a moratorium in the defense bill or by executive order, and the December 2025 Clarke letter (44 signers) calling a moratorium 'wildly irresponsible' with no federal law in place. He does want a federal framework for data centers, but that is about energy costs, not about blocking state AI rules.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order
evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
evidence.what_it_shows: Landsman is listed among the signers; the letter opposes any federal moratorium or preemption of state AI laws.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: Landsman is listed among the 44 signers; the letter says any preemption would put Americans at risk online.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Landsman leans toward tighter controls on China's access to AI technology. He cosponsors the Chip Security Act, which would put location tracking on advanced AI chips to catch smuggling to China, and the ban on DeepSeek on government devices, and he sponsored a bill to bring more chip manufacturing to the U.S. No statement on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales was found.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R.1121, No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Early cosponsor of the ban on the Chinese AI app on federal devices.

evidence.what_it_shows: His Securing Semiconductor Supply Chains Act passed the House; it is about onshoring chip production rather than export controls.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R.2480, Securing Semiconductor Supply Chains Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Directs Commerce to work with states to attract allied investment in U.S. chip plants.
