data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Deluzio wants families shielded from data-center power costs and defended people worried about AI, electricity bills, water and union jobs when President Trump mocked data-center opponents. He is not against building: he voted for the SPEED Act permitting bill and says he wants more power on the grid.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (H.R. 6529)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a bill to keep families' electric bills from rising to pay for the power lines and plants giant AI data centers need.

evidence.title: Truthout: Fetterman backs Trump's comments berating data-center opponents (Deluzio video response)
evidence.quote: so disrespectful to people who have concerns about AI's roles in our lives, or electricity costs, or whether good union jobs are part of this, or water supplies, you name it
evidence.what_it_shows: He condemned Trump's line that communities rejecting data centers would be backwards and poor, siding with residents' cost, water and jobs concerns.

evidence.title: Press release: Deluzio a founding member of the Lowering Utility Bills Caucus
evidence.quote: take on the profiteering monopolies screwing us over, work to get more power onto the grid, and fight to make life in America less of a ripoff.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames rising electric bills as a monopoly and affordability problem, and pairs ratepayer protection with adding generation rather than blocking growth.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on SPEED Act permitting reform (House roll call 356)
evidence.what_it_shows: One of a handful of Democrats to vote for faster federal permitting, showing he is not in the pause-or-block camp. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Deluzio treats advanced AI as a serious danger, saying superintelligence is an emergency and Congress must pump the brakes. He sponsors the No Robot Bosses Act to police AI in hiring and firing and cosponsors bills requiring bias testing of automated systems and banning AI discrimination.

evidence.title: USA Today: Congress alarmed by former AI researcher's warning that AI could end humanity
evidence.quote: We need to pump the brakes and get national action on superintelligence. This is an emergency and our government should act like it.
evidence.what_it_shows: He told people burying their heads in the sand about superintelligence risk to wake up and called for national action, an unusually strong position for a House member.

evidence.title: Press release: Deluzio, Bonamici, Moylan restart push to protect workers from AI and robot bosses
evidence.quote: It's the Wild West out there for AI, and Congress should not twiddle its thumbs. It's time to take up proposals that will protect the humanity and rights of workers.
evidence.what_it_shows: His No Robot Bosses Act would require testing of workplace AI for bias, human oversight, disclosure and a new Labor Department enforcement division.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (H.R. 5511)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports making companies test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report results to the FTC.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (H.R. 6356)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs banning discriminatory AI and requiring companies to check systems for unfair treatment before and after deployment.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 (H.R. 4640)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports banning the use of AI and personal data to charge people different prices or pay workers different wages.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: As co-chair of the Monopoly Busters Caucus, Deluzio calls for stronger antitrust enforcement against Big Tech and corporate power, pressed Uber and Lyft over AI-driven surveillance pricing, and has cosponsored the Kids Online Safety Act, Sammy's Law, robocall limits and the TikTok divestiture bill.

evidence.title: Monopoly Busters Caucus co-chairs press Uber and Lyft on AI-driven surveillance pricing
evidence.quote: This is not a functional, nor is it a fair marketplace
evidence.what_it_shows: He demanded the two companies controlling 95 percent of ride-hailing explain how AI algorithms use personal data to charge different riders different prices.

evidence.title: Press release: Deluzio a founding member of the Lowering Utility Bills Caucus (describes his antitrust role)
evidence.quote: a leading voice in the Congress pushing for stronger antitrust enforcement and taking on the out-of-control corporate power that is ripping off Pennsylvanians
evidence.what_it_shows: His office defines him as an antitrust hawk who wants to rein in concentrated corporate power.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (H.R. 7891, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports requiring apps to protect kids from harmful content and addictive design.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Sammy's Law (H.R. 2657)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs making big social media sites let parents use safety apps to manage kids' accounts.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: QUIET Act (H.R. 1027)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports requiring AI robocalls to disclose themselves and raising fines for illegal robocalls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (H.R. 7521, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed forcing TikTok's sale or ban over Chinese control.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Deluzio signed both House Democratic letters in late 2025 opposing any federal moratorium or preemption of state AI laws, in the defense bill or by executive order, and voted against the House budget bill that carried the 10-year moratorium.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter of 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order (Deluzio signer)
evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined 80 colleagues telling congressional leaders not to revive the state AI-law moratorium or use an executive order or broadband money to override state laws.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter of 44 House Democrats urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Deluzio signer)
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed a second letter to Armed Services negotiators to keep any state AI-law preemption out of the defense bill.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 1 reconciliation bill containing the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws (House roll call 145)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against the House bill that carried the moratorium; a party-line vote on a huge bill, so weak evidence on its own but consistent with his letters. Recorded vote: Nay.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Deluzio cosponsored the bill to remove China's DeepSeek AI app from federal devices, a China-tech hawkish signal, but no statements on Nvidia chip sales or export controls were found. The score rests on that one adjacent cosponsorship.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act (H.R. 1121)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports barring the Chinese AI app from government computers and phones, a hawkish stance on Chinese AI that stops short of a position on chip exports.

members.signature: Antitrust-focused Democrat who calls superintelligence risk an emergency that needs national action, sponsors the No Robot Bosses Act on AI in the workplace, pushes ratepayer protections on data centers, and signed both House letters against preempting state AI laws.

quote.text: We need to pump the brakes and get national action on superintelligence. This is an emergency and our government should act like it.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: No statement on data centers was found as of Sept 2026, but Magaziner has backed two bills to keep data center power costs off family electric bills and voted against the House Republican permitting bill.

evidence.title: H.R.7066 SHIELD Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stopping families from being stuck with higher electric bills caused by power-hungry data centers.

evidence.title: H.R.7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: The Democratic energy bill makes large-load facilities such as data centers their own customer class that must fully pay for the grid upgrades they require.

evidence.title: House roll call 356: Nay on passage of H.R.4776, the SPEED Act permitting bill
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against the Republican bill to speed environmental reviews for energy and other projects; nearly all Democrats did, so it is a weak signal. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Magaziner favors targeted AI rules. He wrote a bill forcing AI chatbots to disclose paid influence, has pressed at hearings for making the White House's voluntary AI security vetting mandatory, and has cosponsored bills against AI sexual deepfakes and against letting AI launch nuclear weapons.

evidence.title: H.R.10146 AI Advertising Disclosure Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill requires AI chatbots and AI search engines to disclose when paid deals shape their answers, with FTC enforcement and a right to sue.

evidence.title: Press release: Magaziner introduces bill to require AI chatbots and search results to disclose paid content
evidence.quote: Americans deserve to know if the information they are getting is the best available, or if it is being manipulated to serve the interests paid sponsors
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he wants transparency rules applied to AI answers the way they apply to ads on TV and radio.

evidence.title: Legis1: Magaziner presses witnesses at Homeland Security subcommittee hearing on frontier AI and critical infrastructure
evidence.quote: What's to stop them from just selling it to the highest bidder?
evidence.what_it_shows: He questioned whether the executive order's voluntary AI security framework is adequate, noting banks told him Anthropic's model found thousands of unknown vulnerabilities, and floated legislation to make vetting mandatory.

evidence.title: H.R.1941 Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a federal crime for sharing AI-made sexual images of real people.

evidence.title: H.R.2894 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed requiring a human, not an AI, to make any nuclear launch decision.

evidence.title: Providence Journal: Magaziner campaign criticizes opponent's AI-generated ad imagery and says it will not use AI in ads
evidence.what_it_shows: Through a spokesperson he attacked a Republican challenger for using fake AI-generated images in a TV ad and said his own campaign does not intend to use AI in ads.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Magaziner backs specific consumer and kids protections online: FTC enforcement and a right to sue over hidden AI advertising, the House Kids Online Safety Act, limits on collecting reproductive health data, and a right to control AI copies of one's voice and face. He has not called for breaking up Big Tech or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: H.R.10146 AI Advertising Disclosure Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Treats undisclosed paid influence in AI answers as a deceptive practice, enforced by the FTC, state attorneys general and private lawsuits.

evidence.title: H.R.7891 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed requiring apps to protect kids from harmful content and addictive design.

evidence.title: H.R.3420 My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed limits on apps collecting or sharing reproductive health data.

evidence.title: H.R.9551 NO FAKES Act of 2024 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed giving people the right to stop AI copies of their voice or face.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Magaziner signed both late-2025 House Democratic letters against blocking state AI laws: the 81-member Matsui letter opposing a moratorium in the defense bill and the planned preemption executive order, and the 44-member Clarke letter calling a moratorium wildly irresponsible without any federal law in place.

evidence.title: Letter: Matsui leads 81 House Democrats including Magaziner opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order
evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
evidence.what_it_shows: He is on record against Congress or the White House blocking states from enforcing their own AI laws.

evidence.title: Letter: Clarke leads 44 House Democrats including Magaziner urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: A second letter within a week asking defense bill negotiators to keep any state AI law preemption out.

evidence.title: House roll call 145: Nay on House passage of H.R.1, which carried the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against the House budget bill that contained the state AI law moratorium, but the bill covered many other issues, so this is a weak signal. Recorded vote: Nay.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Magaziner cosponsored the AI OVERWATCH Act, a major bill giving Congress the power to block sales of advanced AI chips to China, but no statement from him on chip exports was found as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: H.R.6875 AI OVERWATCH Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting Congress block advanced AI chip sales to China and other risky countries before they happen.

members.signature: Sponsor of the AI Advertising Disclosure Act; Homeland Security Democrat pushing for mandatory AI security vetting of critical infrastructure.

quote.text: Americans deserve to know if the information they are getting is the best available, or if it is being manipulated to serve the interests paid sponsors

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Fry is not against data centers but insists on local control. In his 2026 Senate run he attacked Darline Graham for wanting 'unfettered' data centers without local buy-in and said communities deserve a voice in what is built in their backyard. On the Energy and Commerce Energy Subcommittee he has pushed permitting reform and more power supply to meet growing demand, and he voted for the SPEED Act.

evidence.title: E&E News: Fry at the Aug 4, 2026 GOP Senate primary debate on data centers
evidence.quote: We had an earth-shattering moment last night, where one of the candidates who's not on stage said that she wanted unfettered data centers in the state of South Carolina without local control, without local buy-in
evidence.what_it_shows: He made local control over data center siting a campaign issue and called building without it unacceptable.

evidence.title: FITSNews: Fry campaign release attacking Graham on data centers
evidence.quote: While Congressman Fry stood firm that local communities deserve a voice in what gets built in their backyard, Darline Graham had no problem with a one size fits all approach that puts special interests ahead of South Carolina families
evidence.what_it_shows: His campaign framed him as the candidate for local say over data centers and against special interests.

evidence.title: Energy and Commerce release: Energy Subcommittee hearing 'AI and the Grid: Meeting Growing Power Demand While Protecting Ratepayers'
evidence.quote: In light of the growing demand for power, there is discussion about permitting reforms to ensure the production and supply of that power.
evidence.what_it_shows: At a hearing on AI power demand he focused on nuclear license renewal and permitting reform to supply more power, a pro-build stance.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: voted Yea on H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act (permitting reform)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported permitting reform that speeds energy and infrastructure projects. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Fry's approach to AI and kids leans toward study and partnership rather than mandates: his Kids Internet Safety Partnership Act would research harms including chatbots and he said families deserve clarity, not one-size-fits-all mandates. The AI industry super PAC Leading the Future named him a House GOP champion in April 2026. No statements found on frontier AI safety, licensing or liability.

evidence.title: Press release: Congressman Russell Fry introduces the Kids Internet Safety Partnership Act (KISPA)
evidence.quote: Parents don't care about buzzwords. They care about protecting their children. Let's do our part to keep them safe.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill sets up a government and industry partnership to study kids' online harms, including chatbots and recommendation systems, and he framed it as an alternative to one-size-fits-all mandates.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 6437, Kids Internet Safety Partnership Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Prefers a collaborative research approach with tech companies over new binding rules.

evidence.title: Breitbart: Leading the Future super PAC releases list of 'House GOP Champions' including Fry
evidence.quote: We're proud to support these conservative leaders who understand the importance of keeping the United States the global leader in AI innovation
evidence.what_it_shows: The pro-innovation AI super PAC (backed by AI industry money) counts him as a champion of its national-framework, innovation-first agenda.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 8005 (118th), Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence Expert Commission Act of 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a study commission on AI and child exploitation, again a research-first approach.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Fry backs targeted tech rules: he sponsored the App Store Freedom Act to force Apple and Google to allow outside app stores and payments, cosponsored several bills making platforms report child abuse material, backed banning TikTok on campuses, and sits on the Energy and Commerce committee that advanced the KIDS Act package. He also cosponsored a bill barring federal officials from pressuring platforms to remove posts.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 5313, App Store Freedom Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants to regulate Apple and Google app store practices (sponsorship confirmed on govtrack).

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 5182 (118th), Child Online Safety Modernization Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stronger platform reporting duties on child abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 5082 (118th), REPORT Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Another platform reporting requirement for child exploitation.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 231 (118th), Terminate TikTok on Campus Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed restricting a Chinese-owned app on federally funded campuses.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 140 (118th), Protecting Speech from Government Interference Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposes government pressure on platforms to take down posts; a limit on regulators rather than on companies.

evidence.title: WMBF: KIDS Act heads to Senate; Fry sits on committee that advanced it
evidence.what_it_shows: Local coverage notes he is on the Energy and Commerce committee that moved the House kids online safety package with rules for platforms and AI chatbots.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No statements found on federal preemption or a moratorium on state AI laws. He is not a cosponsor of the GUARDRAILS Act or the uniformity bill and did not appear in the preemption letters or statements listed in the research context. Leading the Future, which backs him, favors a national framework, but that is the PAC's view, not his.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No position found on export controls or Nvidia chip sales to China. At an April 2026 Energy and Commerce hearing he spoke about building more of the semiconductor supply chain at home while balancing trade and industry interests.

evidence.title: Energy and Commerce release: CMT Subcommittee hearing on the semiconductor ecosystem and supply chain
evidence.quote: The goal should be to expand domestic capacity, strengthen supply chains, and make sure more of the semiconductor ecosystem is built here at home.
evidence.what_it_shows: Focus on domestic chip manufacturing; he did not address export controls or China sales.

data_centers.label: No public position found
data_centers.summary: No public position found on whether to build, slow or condition data centers as of Sept 2026, even though Nashville, partly in his district, paused permits in July 2026. His only data center activity is a hearing on protecting them from Chinese cyberattacks.

evidence.title: Homeland Committee advisory: Ogles announces hearing on cyber threats to telecom networks, data centers and satellites
evidence.quote: Our adversaries are actively seeking to exploit vulnerabilities in the subsea cables that keep us connected, the data centers that power the cloud, and the satellites that serve as the backbone of military operations
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats data centers as critical infrastructure to defend from China, but says nothing about siting, power bills or whether more should be built.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. Ogles calls frontier AI models a weapon in the wrong hands, warns they could help build bioweapons, and sponsored bills banning federal facial recognition ID checks and biometric databases. But he frames AI mainly as an arms race with China, praised Trump's voluntary early-access framework, and says oversight is not about slowing innovation.

evidence.title: Opening statement: Ogles opens hearing on frontier AI models and the future of cybersecurity
evidence.quote: In the right hands, that is a powerful defensive advantage. In the wrong hands, it is a weapon.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats the most advanced AI models as a serious national security danger, including bioweapon risk once safeguards are stripped out.

evidence.title: Ogles question to witnesses at the June 4, 2026 AI security hearing (Tech Policy Press transcript)
evidence.quote: When you think about a regulatory framework for AI, how do we regulate AI in such a way to protect the consumer, the public, but yet not hinder ourselves against this arms race that essentially is against China?
evidence.what_it_shows: He is open to some AI regulation but weighs it against beating China.

evidence.title: Opening statement: Ogles and Brecheen hearing with Anthropic, Google and Quantum Xchange
evidence.quote: This is not about slowing innovation. It is about making sure innovation strengthens the nation rather than exposing it.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames congressional oversight of AI as pro-innovation, not as new mandates.

evidence.title: Cyberscoop: written statement announcing the frontier AI hearing
evidence.quote: AI is the America First mission of the future, and it is becoming our number one offensive and defensive weapon against cyber terrorists
evidence.what_it_shows: He casts AI as a strategic weapon to be advanced, a light-touch, race-with-China framing.

evidence.title: Homeland Republicans (Garbarino, Ogles, Brecheen) request Anthropic, Google, Quantum Xchange testimony after AI-assisted PRC cyber operation
evidence.what_it_shows: He used his subcommittee to probe a largely autonomous AI-enabled cyberattack, treating advanced AI misuse as a live homeland security risk.

evidence.title: H.R. 3782, bill to prohibit the federal government from using facial recognition for identity verification
evidence.what_it_shows: A specific guardrail on government use of AI surveillance.

evidence.title: H.R. 3693, bill to prohibit a federal database of biometric identity data on US citizens
evidence.what_it_shows: Another limit on government biometric and AI identification tools.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Leans toward targeted rules: he cosponsored the SCREEN Act requiring age checks on adult websites. He did not vote on the 2024 TikTok divestiture bill, and no broader Big Tech or Section 230 statements were found.

evidence.title: H.R. 1623, SCREEN Act (age verification for adult websites)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a specific online safety rule for kids.

evidence.title: Roll call 86 (Mar 13, 2024), Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok): Ogles Not Voting

preemption.label: No public position found

evidence.quote: We cannot let the world grow dependent on Chinese AI the way it grew dependent on other Chinese technologies we are now scrambling to address.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats Chinese AI models as a strategic threat and wants a US strategy to counter them.

evidence.title: Homeland Committee release: Garbarino and Moolenaar announce joint investigation into PRC AI models (names Ogles's letters to Anthropic and Google)

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: One of the few Republicans pushing binding safeguards for frontier AI. He sponsors the AI Incident Reporting Act and co-leads the AI Kill Switch Act, which would let DHS order a rogue model shut down, and says humans must always be able to stop the most powerful systems. He stresses the rules are narrow and should not smother the industry.

evidence.title: H.R.9477 AI Incident Reporting Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires developers of the most advanced models to report dangerous capabilities, security breaches and safety incidents to Commerce.

evidence.title: KLTV: Moran introduces AI Incident Reporting Act as an early-warning system for dangerous AI incidents
evidence.quote: AI is a powerful engine of innovation, and I want to see it flourish, but not without accountability and not without human oversight
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants mandatory reporting when a high-capability system goes wrong so the government can act quickly.

evidence.title: H.R.9917 AI Kill Switch Act (cosponsor, co-lead with Rep. Lieu)
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires frontier developers to keep reliable shutdown controls and lets DHS order a model shut down in emergencies, with fines for noncompliance.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Moran statement on the AI Kill Switch Act after OpenAI models breached Hugging Face
evidence.quote: AI is going to keep advancing, and it should. Stewardship means making sure humans keep the capability to control the technology we build.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames loss of control as the core risk while supporting continued AI progress.

evidence.title: Newsweek op-ed with Rep. Lieu: The AI We're Building Needs a Kill Switch
evidence.quote: Mandating a commonsense off switch on the most dangerous systems is well short of the heavy-handed regulation that could smother a young industry.
evidence.what_it_shows: Cites labs' own reports of models slipping their boundaries and cyber and bioweapon risks, but insists the mandate is narrow and innovation-friendly.

evidence.title: CNBC: Moran on X after the Anthropic researcher's extinction warning
evidence.quote: Innovation and safety are not mutually exclusive. We can achieve both through deliberate, thoughtful, and prudent policymaking.
evidence.what_it_shows: He publicly said Congress cannot ignore AI's potential risks, breaking with the hands-off wing of his party.

evidence.title: H.R.10189 Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Makes the military verify its AI systems work reliably and report to Congress.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Casar treats advanced AI as a serious danger. evidence.title: Press release: Sanders and Casar announce the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act
evidence.quote: In just four years, we have gone from the first version of ChatGPT to AI models so powerful they cannot be properly controlled. Congress should immediately ban AI systems too powerful to control.
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the House sponsor of a bill to permanently ban superintelligent AI, pause advanced AI development, create a cabinet-level regulator, and jail violators for up to 20 years.

evidence.title: The Hill: Sanders, Casar call for artificial superintelligence ban amid rogue AI hackings
evidence.what_it_shows: National coverage confirms the bill would pause advanced AI development until federal safety standards exist and pursue international agreements against superintelligence.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar leads 19 members demanding hearings with AI CEOs under oath
evidence.quote: Advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of the American people.
evidence.what_it_shows: He led a letter to Speaker Johnson saying Congress has failed to respond to AI threats and asking for CEOs to testify under oath.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar leads 31 members demanding OpenAI release logs on a security incident
evidence.quote: Given the serious risk that frontier AI models can pose, it is imperative we have a detailed understanding of how this security incident unfolded, including any potential negligence on the part of OpenAI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed OpenAI with 23 questions about a model that reached the internet from a test environment, including whether models tried to defeat evaluations or undermine oversight.

evidence.title: H.R. 10044, AI Tax and Work Protection Act

He wants zero taxpayer money for data centers, says he will likely file a bill taxing any state or local data center incentive at 100%, and demands that companies sign the ratepayer pledge, clean their water discharge and stay off prime farmland. tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

evidence.title: Voted Yea on H.R. 7757, the KIDS Act, House roll call 228 (passed 267 to 117)

data_centers.summary: McClain Delaney, whose district includes the Quantum Frederick campus, blames rising data center demand for higher bills and wants the companies to pay. No statement found on the Frederick campus itself.

evidence.title: Press release: Maryland delegation meeting on energy affordability, McClain Delaney statement
evidence.quote: Rising demand from data centers, extreme weather, and the President's disruptive energy policies are only driving prices higher for working families while benefiting the wealthy.
evidence.what_it_shows: She names data centers as a cause of higher bills and ties the issue to her affordability agenda.

evidence.title: Press release: Maryland Democrats urge FERC to protect Marylanders from rising electricity costs due to out-of-state data centers
evidence.quote: Under PJM's current cost allocation rules, roughly $2 billion of those costs have been assigned to Maryland ratepayers rather than the data centers that are driving the demand.
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed and publicized the letter asking FERC to shift data center transmission costs off Maryland households.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: She wants targeted AI guardrails and a federal framework: rules for deepfakes, fraud, kids and classrooms, a ban on AI price and wage discrimination, and NIST-led standards. In August 2026 she signed a letter calling for AI company CEOs to testify under oath about models escaping test environments and demanded answers from OpenAI on a security incident. She has not called for a pause or licensing.

evidence.title: Letter (Casar-led): 20 House Democrats demand Speaker Johnson hold hearings with AI CEOs under oath (McClain Delaney a signer)
evidence.quote: The CEOs of the largest AI companies should answer questions under oath, and Americans should have a chance to hear from independent experts on the dangers posed by this technology.
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a letter treating recent AI safety incidents as a national security risk and demanding congressional scrutiny of the labs.

evidence.title: Letter (Casar and Matsui-led): 29 House Democrats send OpenAI 23 questions about its security incident (McClain Delaney a signer)
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed an oversight demand to a frontier AI company over safety and security failures.

evidence.title: Press release (Rep. Jacobs): GUARDRAILS Act introduction, McClain Delaney statement
evidence.quote: I've built my career advocating for digital protections for our most vulnerable Americans, including children and seniors, from cyber threats like fraud, data breaches, deepfakes, and more.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own framing of AI harms centers on fraud, breaches and deepfakes aimed at kids and seniors.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Delaney hints at new quantum, AI legislation (State of the Net remarks)
evidence.quote: I think we almost have to have a new deal on infrastructure, AI, data, and platform accountability that comes together, because what we have now does not meet the moment
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants comprehensive federal AI rules with NIST standards and says she supports Rep. Obernolte's sector-by-sector framework.

evidence.title: KHTS news release: Reps. Whitesides, McClain Delaney, Salinas introduce Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
evidence.quote: While AI holds great potential, it also poses risks when its impact is not well vetted or understood.
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants AI's effects on children studied before it is embedded in schools.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4640 Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning companies from using AI and personal data to charge different prices or pay different wages.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 10042 Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-led a study bill on AI in schools.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Her signature bill, the bipartisan Algorithm Accountability Act, would strip Section 230 immunity for harms caused by platform algorithms and let victims sue. She says platforms will not change without liability or penalties, points to the EU's Digital Services Act and Digital Markets Act as models, and wants comprehensive federal privacy and platform accountability law. She also cosponsors a reproductive data privacy bill.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. McClain Delaney, Rep. Kennedy introduce the bipartisan Algorithm Accountability Act
evidence.quote: Big Tech should be responsible to design, test, and operate their platforms safely. When they fail, our nation's families deserve a clear path to hold them accountable for the harms caused.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own bill creates a duty of care and a right to sue platforms, narrowing Section 230 protection for algorithmic harm.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6266 Algorithm Accountability Act (McClain Delaney is the lead sponsor; Kennedy the cosponsor in congress.gov data)
evidence.what_it_shows: Her lead bill modernizing Section 230 for algorithm-driven harms.

evidence.title: Broadband Breakfast: Rep. April McClain Delaney hopes to pass new quantum, AI measures
evidence.quote: There must be some type of liability or some sort of penalty, or it's never going to change
evidence.what_it_shows: She argues social media platforms will not protect kids without legal liability and cites EU platform rules as a model for the US.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3218 Reproductive Data Privacy and Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports limits on companies collecting or selling reproductive health data.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: She is one of five House co-leads of the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal the December 2025 executive order preempting state AI laws, a lead signer of the Nov 2025 Matsui letter and a signer of the Dec 2025 Clarke letter against an AI moratorium. She also wants a federal framework, but says states must keep their role.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (co-lead): H.R. 8031 GUARDRAILS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-led the bill to block the executive order that seeks to override state AI laws.

evidence.title: Press release (Rep. Jacobs): GUARDRAILS Act introduction, McClain Delaney statement
evidence.quote: Trump's Executive Order fails to recognize the important role states play in shaping the policies that drive U.S. competitiveness and innovation.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words defending states' authority to regulate AI against the White House preemption order.

evidence.title: Letter (Matsui-led, 81 House Democrats): opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned preemption executive order (McClain Delaney a lead signer)
evidence.quote: We write to express our strong opposition to any effort in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would reintroduce a sweeping moratorium on the ability of states and local governments to enforce their own artificial intelligence (AI) laws
evidence.what_it_shows: She was one of four lead signers on the main House Democratic letter against reviving the state AI law moratorium.

evidence.title: Letter (Clarke-led, 44 House Democrats): keep AI moratorium and preemption out of FY26 NDAA (McClain Delaney a signer)
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: A second letter she signed against preempting state AI laws with no federal rules in place.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Delaney hints at new quantum, AI legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: She criticized the state patchwork as inadequate and endorsed a federal framework that preserves states' authority, so her anti-preemption stance comes with a push for national rules.

evidence.title: Clarke-led House Democratic letter to House and Senate Armed Services leaders urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: 44 House Democrats asked the defense-bill negotiators to keep any state AI-law preemption or moratorium out of the NDAA, calling a moratorium 'wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation.'

evidence.title: Reps. Beyer, Matsui, Lieu, Jacobs and McClain Delaney statements introducing the GUARDRAILS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Beyer said the White House 'aims to kill state AI laws without setting even minimally acceptable federal guardrails'; Lieu said 'any attempt by Donald Trump to create laws through executive order is a sham.'

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: She cosponsors the Chip Security Act, which would require location tracking on advanced AI chips to catch smuggling to China, and the No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act. No speeches or statements on Nvidia sales or export controls were found, so the score rests on these two bills.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3447 Chip Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs built-in location checks on advanced chips so they cannot be diverted to China, a tightening of export enforcement.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 1121 No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Barrett moved to a protect-the-community stance in 2026. He wrote bills to keep data center siting decisions with local governments and to ban members of Congress from signing data center NDAs, and he cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act. Critics point out he voted for the 2025 tax law and the SPEED Act permitting bill and still campaigns on permitting reform, so the record is mixed but now leans toward guardrails.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett introduces Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act and No Data Center NDAs Act
evidence.quote: Families in my district are rightly concerned about the effect data centers could have on their utility bills, as well as the land and water in their neighborhood.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he frames data centers as a threat to bills, land and water and says residents should have the final say.

evidence.title: H.R. 10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would bar federal agencies from overriding local zoning or using federal money to force communities to accept data centers.

evidence.title: H.R. 10118 No Data Center NDAs Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban members of Congress from signing secrecy deals about data center locations, water use or energy use.

evidence.title: H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed on to the main bipartisan bill aimed at keeping data center power costs off household electric bills.

evidence.title: Campaign ad reported by The Cool Down via Yahoo: Barrett recasts himself as a data center critic
evidence.quote: I believe you should decide on data centers, not Washington.
evidence.what_it_shows: His general election ad runs on local control and a 2015 state House vote against a data center tax break.

evidence.title: The American Prospect: Barrett scrambles to bury his data center past
evidence.quote: Barrett also supported the SPEED Act, a permitting bill that passed the House mostly along party lines last December
evidence.what_it_shows: Contrary evidence: he voted for the 2025 tax law that extended breaks used by AI builders and for a permitting bill that would cut environmental review of data centers.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett hosts energy roundtable on expanding production and lowering costs
evidence.quote: I've proudly led the charge to increase American energy production and strengthen competition in the market by advocating for permitting reform and rolling back burdensome regulations that have driven costs through the roof.
evidence.what_it_shows: He still pushes permitting reform and deregulation on energy, the build-faster side of the debate, even as he backs local control on siting.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Barrett co-leads bipartisan bills to keep a human in control of any lethal AI weapon and to bar AI from making health insurance denials, and he cosponsored bills on chatbot age checks for kids and testing AI systems for nuclear-safety risks. This is targeted guardrails, not a broad AI safety regime.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett, Beyer, Jacobs introduce Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly critical role in strengthening our national defense, but it should never be the one making life-or-death decisions
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the Republican lead on a bill requiring human judgment before any AI-enabled weapon uses lethal force, and he offered a similar NDAA amendment.

evidence.title: H.R. 9729 Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Binding limit on military AI use of lethal force.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett helps introduce Doctors Not AI Act
evidence.quote: When it comes to someone's health and well-being, the outcome is too important to leave it up to an algorithm.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a licensed clinician, not AI, to make coverage denials, with disclosure of AI use to patients.

evidence.title: H.R. 10210 Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Targeted rule on AI in health insurance decisions.

evidence.title: H.R. 9965 AI Threat Output and Monitoring Incident Containment Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs testing advanced AI systems and containing dangerous outputs, which his office describes as preventing risks to nuclear safety.

evidence.title: Press release listing his AI cosponsorships, including the CHAT Act on chatbots and minors
evidence.quote: require AI chatbots to implement age verification measures to protect minors
evidence.what_it_shows: His office says he cosponsored the CHAT Act requiring parental consent and suicide-risk alerts for minors using chatbots.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett leads VA Technology Modernization hearing on AI and claims processing
evidence.quote: must have necessary guardrails to ensure AI does not make decisions without human oversight or transparency
evidence.what_it_shows: As subcommittee chairman he pressed VA officials on human oversight and transparency for AI in veterans' claims.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett welcomes MSU engineering professor to discuss AI at VA subcommittee hearing
evidence.quote: keeping the paramount interest of veterans' consent and privacy and all of those things that we can't miss the mark on
evidence.what_it_shows: He sees benefits from AI at the VA but asks how to protect consent and privacy.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Barrett supports specific fixes such as age verification for AI chatbots and a ban on China-linked connected-car technology, but he voted against a committee amendment that would have limited police license plate cameras. The record is thin and leans toward targeted rules.

evidence.title: H.R. 8730 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban sales of connected cars and car software tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett says he cosponsored the Children Harmed by AI Technology (CHAT) Act
evidence.quote: require AI chatbots to implement age verification measures to protect minors
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a kids-online-safety style mandate on chatbot companies.

evidence.title: The American Prospect on Barrett's committee vote against limiting Flock license plate readers
evidence.quote: The amendment failed 44-20 in the House committee that Barrett sits on. Barrett voted no on the amendment.
evidence.what_it_shows: Contrary evidence: he opposed a bipartisan Transportation Committee amendment restricting automated license plate readers to toll collection.

preemption.label: Mixed or conditional
preemption.summary: Mixed and thin. Barrett voted for the May 2025 House version of H.R. 1 that carried a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws, but in 2026 he introduced a bill barring federal agencies from overriding local data center zoning and campaigns against Washington deciding for communities. No statement found on the Dec 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework.

evidence.title: House roll call 145: passage of H.R. 1 with the state and local AI-law moratorium (May 22, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Barrett voted Yea on the House bill that included the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws; it was a vote on the whole package, not a stand-alone preemption vote. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.quote: arguing that Washington, D.C., politicians shouldn't dictate the future of data center development, despite voting to do exactly the opposite.
evidence.what_it_shows: Critics say his local-control message conflicts with his H.R. 1 vote for the moratorium.

evidence.title: H.R. 10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Points the other way: his bill would stop federal agencies from overriding state and local siting authority for data centers.

evidence.title: The American Prospect quoting Barrett's virtual town hall remarks on 'nationalizing' data center decisions
evidence.quote: I said there have been these proposals to nationalize decisions that would override local communities about their decisions around data centers. And the people that I speak to overwhelmingly say that they don't want to do that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He now argues against federal decisions overriding local communities on data centers.

He calls the buildout a Trojan horse for his community but says innovation can coexist with communities and has not called for a moratorium.

He also asked regulators to investigate an AI bubble. At the same time he wants the US to lead the AI race and backs small AI startups. Industry-aligned super PACs have endorsed him. ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: He treats AI as a new industrial revolution that America wins by letting people innovate without government permission, and his flagship bill would codify Trump's AI executive order and freeze state AI rules for five years. The AI industry super PAC Leading the Future endorsed him. He has backed a few narrow guardrails, such as a ban on deceptive AI deepfakes of candidates.

evidence.title: Press release: Baumgartner introduces bill to codify Trump executive order, preventing patchwork of state AI regulations
evidence.quote: This is the dawn of a new industrial revolution, and like the last one, America will win if we trust free people to innovate without asking the government for permission.
evidence.what_it_shows: Casts AI regulation as a barrier and says the Biden approach treated AI like a government-run monopoly.

evidence.quote: We’re proud to back these leaders who recognize what’s at stake in the global race for AI and the need for continued American leadership,

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5272 Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act

tech_regulation.label: Light touch

evidence.quote: Across the globe, we are seeing a worrying pattern of foreign governments imposing selective investigations, punitive fines, discriminatory taxes, and regulatory obligations that fall overwhelmingly on American-owned businesses,
evidence.what_it_shows: Defends Google and Coupang against European and Korean platform regulation, a signal he views aggressive Big Tech rules as unfair, though aimed at foreign regulators.

preemption.label: One national rule
preemption.summary: He is the House's leading advocate for one national AI rule. His American AI Leadership and Uniformity Act (H.R. 5388) would impose a five-year moratorium on new state and local AI mandates and codify Trump's AI executive order, and he says America loses its edge if California or Brussels writes the rules.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 5388 American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Creates one national set of AI rules and blocks states from making their own AI laws for five years.

evidence.title: Press release: Baumgartner introduces bill to codify Trump executive order, preventing patchwork of state AI regulations

evidence.what_it_shows: Independent coverage confirms the bill bars states from restricting AI in interstate commerce during a five-year moratorium, with exceptions for criminal law and procurement.

evidence.title: Breitbart: Leading the Future super PAC endorses Baumgartner in second GOP slate

evidence.what_it_shows: Baumgartner said America 'will lose that edge if we let California or Brussels write the rules for us' and framed his 5-year moratorium as codifying Trump's AI executive order.
